Invoke the location functionality using the file system and configured locator, then assert that the location attempt returns null, confirming that the strategy correctly fails to locate the file when the base path configuration creates an invalid or inaccessible path combination. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the byte buffer write functionality of cryptographic output streams using both JCE and OpenSSL cipher implementations. Initialize random byte arrays for test data, encryption keys, and initialization vectors using a secure random generator, then set up the test environment and prepare encrypted reference data by creating a crypto output stream with the JCE cipher implementation. Create a byte array output stream to capture the encrypted output, then systematically test byte buffer write operations by invoking the helper method four times with different combinations of JCE and OpenSSL cipher class names and channel usage flags. For each cipher implementation and channel configuration, reset the output stream, create a new crypto output stream with the specified cipher and buffer settings, perform byte buffer write operations, then repeat the process using the cipher's transformation string and properties for stream creation. Validate that the output stream remains open after writing a single byte and verify that the stream properly closes and reports its closed state when explicitly closed. The test includes a timeout annotation limiting execution to 120 seconds and uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that an attribute pointer can correctly retrieve the base value of a configuration attribute. Initialize a configuration structure with a parent node that contains a named attribute with a specific value, then create a pointer that references this attribute within the parent node's context. Call the method to retrieve the base value from the attribute pointer and assert that the returned value matches the expected attribute value that was originally set on the parent node. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates that cryptographic operations properly detect and reject tampered encrypted data when using authenticated encryption modes. Initialize configuration properties to specify the cipher implementation and prepare test data arrays containing predefined cryptographic test vectors. Generate random byte arrays for the encryption key, plaintext data, initialization vector, and additional authenticated data with varying lengths to simulate realistic encryption scenarios. Create a cipher instance using the configured transformation and initialize it in encryption mode with the generated key and initialization vector parameters. Update the cipher with the additional authenticated data and perform the final encryption operation to produce encrypted output that includes both ciphertext and authentication tag. Deliberately tamper with the encrypted data by modifying a single byte to simulate data corruption or malicious alteration. Create a new cipher instance and initialize it in decryption mode using the same key and initialization vector. Update the cipher with the same additional authenticated data and attempt to decrypt the tampered encrypted data. Assert that the decryption operation throws an authentication exception indicating tag mismatch, confirming that the cipher correctly detects the data tampering and rejects the corrupted input. Verify that the exception message matches the expected authentication failure message. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the home directory location strategy's behavior when attempting to locate a file that exists in the temporary folder but fails to be found due to base path configuration. Create a new file with a specified name in a temporary folder, then construct a file locator using the file locator utilities builder pattern with a base path and the same file name. Initialize a home directory location strategy with base path evaluation enabled through the setup helper method. Call the locate method on the strategy with a file system and the configured locator, then assert that the result is null, confirming that the strategy correctly fails to locate the file when the base path does not align with the actual file location. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the CombinedConfiguration properly synchronizes read access when retrieving the number of configurations and ensures the combined root node remains uninitialized during this operation. Initialize a CombinedConfiguration instance and a CombinedListener, then register the listener for any configuration events on the configuration. Call the helper method setUpSynchronizerTest which internally calls setUpSourceTest to establish source configurations, creates a new SynchronizerTestImpl instance to track synchronization method calls, and sets this synchronizer on the configuration using setSynchronizer. Invoke getNumberOfConfigurations on the configuration instance, which should trigger the synchronizer's read lock mechanism and return the count of child configurations. Assert that the returned value equals 2 using assertEquals to validate the correct number of configurations is reported. Call verify on the SynchronizerTestImpl instance with Methods.BEGIN_READ and Methods.END_READ parameters to confirm that the configuration properly acquired and released the read lock during the getNumberOfConfigurations operation. Finally, call the helper method checkCombinedRootNotConstructed which retrieves the configuration's model, accesses its node handler, gets the root node, and asserts using assertTrue that the root node's children collection is empty, ensuring that accessing the configuration count does not trigger construction of the combined configuration tree. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the encryption and decryption functionality of cryptographic cipher implementations across multiple transformation algorithms. Initialize the test environment by calling the abstract initialization method and asserting that the cipher class and transformations array are properly configured, then create a properties object with the cipher class configuration. For each transformation algorithm in the transformations array, retrieve test data containing hexadecimal-encoded keys, initialization vectors, input bytes, and expected output bytes from a test data provider, asserting that test data is available for the transformation. Parse each set of test vectors from hexadecimal strings into byte arrays representing cryptographic keys, initialization vectors, plaintext input, and expected ciphertext output. Create direct byte buffers for the input and output data, populate them with the parsed bytes, and flip the buffers to prepare them for reading. Execute byte buffer-based encryption and decryption tests by creating cipher instances, initializing them in encrypt and decrypt modes with the test key and IV, performing encryption on the input buffer, comparing the encrypted result against the expected output buffer, then performing decryption and verifying the decrypted result matches the original input buffer. Execute byte array-based encryption and decryption tests by resetting cipher instances, encrypting the input byte array, asserting the encrypted output matches the expected ciphertext, then decrypting the ciphertext and asserting the result matches the original plaintext. Additionally, perform randomized testing with larger datasets using predefined static key and IV values, generating random plaintext of various sizes, encrypting and decrypting the data in chunks using update and final operations, and asserting that the decrypted result exactly matches the original random plaintext. The testing framework used is JUnit.

This test validates the base value retrieval functionality of a configuration attribute pointer within an XPath-based configuration tree structure. Initialize an immutable node builder and configure it with a parent node name and an associated attribute using predefined string constants for the attribute name and value. Create the immutable node from the builder and construct a configuration node pointer that wraps this node along with a root locale and an in-memory node model handler. This test validates the comprehensive functionality of cryptographic cipher operations across multiple transformation algorithms and data formats. For each supported transformation algorithm, retrieve predefined test data containing hexadecimal-encoded keys, initialization vectors, input data, and expected output data, then iterate through each test case to convert the hex strings into byte arrays and direct byte buffers. Execute encryption and decryption operations using both byte buffer and byte array approaches, where the byte buffer test allocates direct buffers for input and output data, initializes separate cipher instances for encryption and decryption modes with the provided key and initialization vector, performs the cryptographic operations, and validates that the encrypted output matches the expected result and that decryption returns the original input. Similarly, execute byte array testing by resetting cipher configurations, performing encryption and decryption operations on the byte arrays, and asserting that the results match expected values. The testing uses JUnit framework for assertions and test execution.

This test validates the byte buffer writing functionality of cryptographic output streams across different cipher implementations and channel configurations. The test exercises the CryptoOutputStream class with both JCE and OpenSSL cipher backends, testing scenarios with and without channels to ensure proper encryption and stream management behavior. Initialize a SecureRandom instance and populate the test class fields data, key, and iv byte arrays with random bytes, then call the setUp and prepareData helper methods to establish the test environment and create encrypted reference data using the JCE_CIPHER_CLASSNAME with the transformation field, defaultBufferSize field, key, and iv wrapped in an IvParameterSpec. Create a ByteArrayOutputStream and invoke the doByteBufferWrite helper method four times with different parameter combinations: first with JCE_CIPHER_CLASSNAME and withChannel false, then with OPENSSL_CIPHER_CLASSNAME and withChannel false, followed by JCE_CIPHER_CLASSNAME with withChannel true, and finally OPENSSL_CIPHER_CLASSNAME with withChannel true. Within the helper method, write a single byte value of 1 to the output stream, assert that isOpen returns true to validate the stream remains open, create a new CryptoOutputStream instance, close it immediately, and assert that isOpen returns false to confirm proper closure behavior. The test method is annotated with Test and Timeout with a value of 120000 milliseconds using TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

Initialize a configurations object to manage configuration builders, then call the XML builder method with a test URL obtained from a configuration assertion utility to create a file-based configuration builder for XML configurations. This test validates the basic value retrieval functionality of a configuration attribute pointer, specifically testing that the getBaseValue method correctly returns the underlying attribute value from a configuration node structure. This test validates that cryptographic operations properly detect and reject tampered authentication data in authenticated encryption modes. Initialize a cipher configuration with OpenSSL implementation properties and prepare test data arrays containing hexadecimal values for various encryption scenarios. Generate random byte arrays for a 32-byte encryption key, input data, 16-byte initialization vector, 16-byte authentication tag, and additional authenticated data of variable length. Create a cipher instance using the configured transformation and properties, then initialize it in encryption mode with the generated key and initialization vector parameters. Update the cipher with the additional authenticated data and perform the final encryption operation to produce the authentication tag. Create a second cipher instance and initialize it in decryption mode with the same key and initialization vector. Initialize a CSV format instance using the default predefined format configuration, then create a null result set reference. The test exercises the CSV format's ability to process null database metadata when configuring headers from result set information, ensuring robust handling of edge cases where database connections or result sets might be unavailable. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

Initialize a string array containing three values representing CSV data columns, then join these values with commas to create a single row of CSV data. Create a character array writer to capture output and establish a try-with-resources block that opens both a CSV parser using the default format to read the joined row data from a string reader, and a CSV printer using the Informix unload format to write to the character array writer. Iterate through each CSV record from the parser, printing each record to the printer using the print record method, and after each record is printed, assert that the printer's record count increments correctly by comparing it to an expected count variable. After the try-with-resources block completes, verify that the character array writer contains exactly 6 characters and assert that the final output string matches the expected format of pipe-delimited values followed by the Informix unload record separator. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that an expression engine can correctly format attribute keys using alternative syntax configuration. Initialize a hierarchical node structure containing table definitions with names, types, and field collections, along with connection settings and a root-level test attribute. Configure an expression engine with custom symbols that use an at-sign prefix for attributes, forward slashes as property delimiters, and square brackets for indexing while removing attribute end markers and escaped delimiters. Call the attribute key formatting method with an empty parent path and a test attribute name, then assert that the result matches the expected at-sign prefixed format. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the capability to load configuration files that include other files through a custom file system implementation. Initialize a properties configuration with a legacy comma delimiter handler and load it from a test properties file, then clear the configuration and add an include property pointing to an include properties file before saving this test configuration to disk. Create a custom default file system that overrides the input stream retrieval method to return a byte array input stream containing test outcome data when the requested URL ends with the include properties filename, otherwise delegating to the parent implementation. Set up configuration parameters for file-based operations and create a file-based configuration builder for properties configurations, configuring it with the test save file location, a base path pointing to the output directory, and the custom file system. Build the configuration from the builder and assert that the configuration contains the expected success value for the test outcome property, demonstrating that the include mechanism works correctly with custom file system implementations. The test uses JUnit for assertions.

Initialize a LayoutTestConfiguration instance and configure it with a LegacyListDelimiterHandler using a comma delimiter, then create a PropertiesConfigurationLayout instance and set it on the configuration, and initialize a PropertiesBuilder instance. Execute the fillLayout helper method which adds a header comment "A header comment", a null comment, a property "prop" with value "value", the TEST_COMMENT, the TEST_KEY with TEST_VALUE, another property "anotherProp" with value "anotherValue", and a footer comment "A footer comment", then loads this data into the layout using the load method with the configuration and builder's reader, asserting that no exception is thrown during the load operation. Create a second PropertiesConfigurationLayout instance using the copy constructor, passing the original layout as a parameter to test the initialization and copying functionality. Assert that the comment retrieved from the second layout using getComment for TEST_KEY equals the comment from the original layout using getComment for the same key, verifying that comments are properly copied during initialization. Modify the original layout by setting a new comment "A new comment" for TEST_KEY using setComment, then assert that the second layout's canonical comment retrieved using getCanonicalComment for TEST_KEY with false parameter equals TEST_COMMENT, confirming that the copied layout maintains its independent state and is not affected by changes to the original. Increment the blank lines before TEST_KEY in the second layout by retrieving the current value using getBlankLinesBefore and adding 1, then setting it back using setBlankLinesBefore, and assert that the blank lines before TEST_KEY in the original layout using getBlankLinesBefore is not equal to the blank lines in the second layout using assertNotEquals, validating that layout modifications are isolated between the original and copied instances. This test uses the JUnit testing framework with the @Test annotation.

This test validates the file inclusion mechanism of a properties configuration when using a custom file system implementation. Initialize a properties configuration object with a legacy comma delimiter handler and load it from test properties, then clear the configuration and add an include property pointing to "include.properties" before saving the test configuration to a file. Create a custom default file system that overrides the input stream method to return a byte array input stream containing "test.outcome = success" when the URL ends with "include.properties", otherwise delegating to the parent implementation. Instantiate a parameters object and configure a file-based configuration builder for properties configuration class, setting the saved test file, a base path from the output directory URI, and the custom file system. Retrieve the configuration from the builder and assert that the string value for "test.outcome" equals "success", verifying that the include file was properly loaded through the custom file system. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the attribute key generation functionality of a default expression engine when configured with alternative syntax symbols. Initialize a hierarchical node structure containing tables with fields and connection settings, along with a corresponding node handler for in-memory operations. Configure an expression engine with custom symbols that use "@" as the attribute start marker, "/" as the property delimiter, and square brackets for indexing, while setting the attribute end marker to null. Call the attribute key method on the engine with an empty base path and "test" as the attribute name. Assert that the returned key equals "@test", confirming that the engine correctly formats attribute keys using the alternative syntax configuration. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the node key generation functionality of a DefaultExpressionEngine when configured with alternative syntax symbols, specifically testing that the engine correctly constructs hierarchical path strings using custom delimiters and symbols. The test examines the nodeKey method of DefaultExpressionEngine with a nested node structure and custom expression symbols, asserting that the generated key matches the expected path format. Initialize the test class with static fields including TABLES, TAB_TYPES, and FIELDS arrays of type String array, String array, and String double array respectively, along with a static root field of type ImmutableNode and a static handler field of type NodeHandler for ImmutableNode, and an instance engine field of type DefaultExpressionEngine. In the setUpBeforeClass method, call the setUpNodes helper method to create a complex hierarchical node structure with tables containing table elements, each having name children and type attributes, plus connection settings, then assign this to the root field and create an InMemoryNodeModel with the root to obtain the NodeHandler via getNodeHandler and assign it to the handler field. Execute the setUpAlternativeSyntax helper method which creates a DefaultExpressionEngineSymbols using a Builder with setAttributeEnd set to null, setAttributeStart set to "@", setPropertyDelimiter set to "/", setEscapedDelimiter set to null, setIndexStart set to "[", setIndexEnd set to "]", then call create to build the symbols and construct a new DefaultExpressionEngine with these symbols, assigning it to the engine field. Call the nodeKey method on the engine instance, passing the first child of the first child of the root node accessed via getChildren().get(0).getChildren().get(0), the string "tables", and the handler, then assert using assertEquals that the returned value equals "tables/table". This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that a configuration system can accurately convert a stored integer value to various numeric data types. Initialize a base configuration with exception throwing enabled for missing properties and comma-based list delimiter handling. Store an integer value in the configuration using a predefined key. Retrieve the stored value and convert it to different numeric types including integer, long, byte, float, double, big integer, and big decimal representations. Assert that each conversion returns the expected numeric value with appropriate precision tolerances for floating-point comparisons. Verify that the configuration can also return wrapped numeric types when a default value is provided. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the attribute key generation functionality of an expression engine when configured with alternative syntax symbols, specifically testing that the attributeKey method correctly formats attribute names using a custom attribute start symbol. Initialize a DefaultExpressionEngine by calling the helper method setUpAlternativeSyntax, which creates a DefaultExpressionEngineSymbols object using the Builder pattern with specific symbol configurations including setting the attribute end to null, attribute start to "@", property delimiter to "/", escaped delimiter to null, index start to "[", and index end to "]", then constructs a new DefaultExpressionEngine instance with these symbols and assigns it to the engine field of the test class. Call the attributeKey method on the engine instance with an empty string as the first parameter and "test" as the second parameter, which should generate an attribute key using the configured alternative syntax. Assert that the returned value equals "@test" using assertEquals, validating that the method correctly prepends the custom attribute start symbol "@" to the attribute name "test" when generating the attribute key. The test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that a PropertiesConfiguration can successfully load include files through a custom FileSystem implementation that intercepts file access requests. Initialize a PropertiesConfiguration object with a LegacyListDelimiterHandler configured with a comma delimiter, then clear the configuration and add a property with key "include" and value "include.properties" before calling the saveTestConfig helper method which creates a FileHandler for the configuration and saves it to TEST_SAVE_PROPERTIES_FILE. Create a DefaultFileSystem subclass that overrides the getInputStream method to return a ByteArrayInputStream containing "test.outcome = success" encoded in UTF-8 when the requested URL ends with "include.properties", otherwise delegating to the superclass implementation. Instantiate a Parameters object and create a FileBasedConfigurationBuilder for PropertiesConfiguration class, then configure the builder using the fileBased method from Parameters to set the file to TEST_SAVE_PROPERTIES_FILE, the base path to ConfigurationAssert.OUT_DIR converted to URI string, and the custom FileSystem implementation. Call getConfiguration on the builder to obtain the final PropertiesConfiguration instance and assert that calling getString with key "test.outcome" returns exactly "success", verifying that the include file was properly loaded through the custom FileSystem's intercepted file access mechanism. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the number conversion capabilities of a base configuration component. Initialize a base configuration object with exception throwing enabled for missing properties and comma-based list delimiter handling. Set a property using a string key with an integer value of 42. Assert that the configuration correctly converts this stored integer value to various numeric types by retrieving it as an int, long, byte, float, double, long with null default, big integer, and big decimal, verifying each conversion returns the expected value with appropriate precision tolerances for floating-point comparisons. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the functionality of printing parsed CSV records using different CSV formats by creating sample data with three string values, parsing it with a default CSV format, and then reprinting it using a different format with pipe delimiters. Initialize a string array containing three sample values and join them with commas to create CSV row data, then set up a character array writer for capturing output. Create a CSV parser using the default format to parse the joined row data from a string reader, and simultaneously create a CSV printer using the Informix unload format that outputs to the character array writer. Iterate through each parsed record from the parser and print it using the printer, verifying that the record count increments correctly after each print operation by asserting the printer's record count matches the expected value. After processing, validate that the output character array writer contains exactly 6 characters and that the final output string matches the expected pipe-delimited format with the appropriate record separator from the Informix unload format. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the configuration system's ability to convert a stored integer value to various numeric data types through type-specific getter methods. Initialize a BaseConfiguration object in the setup method, configure it to throw exceptions on missing properties, and set the list delimiter handler to use comma separation. Store an Integer value of 42 using the setProperty method with the KEY_NUMBER field as the key, which is a static final String field of the test class. Verify the configuration's numeric conversion capabilities by calling getInt and asserting it returns 42 as an integer, then call getLong and assert it returns 42L as a long value. Continue testing type conversions by calling getByte and asserting it returns byte value 42, then call getFloat with a delta tolerance of 0.01f and assert it returns 42.0f. Call getDouble with a delta tolerance of 0.001 and assert it returns 42.0 as a double value. Test the overloaded getLong method by passing null as the default value and assert it returns Long object with value 42L. Validate BigInteger conversion by calling getBigInteger and asserting it returns a new BigInteger constructed with string "42". Finally, call getBigDecimal and assert it returns a new BigDecimal constructed with string "42.0" to verify decimal number conversion. This test uses JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation and assertEquals assertion methods.

Initialize a string writer to capture CSV output, then create a CSV printer using the MongoDB TSV format which uses tab delimiters and double quote characters for escaping. Print a single record containing two values: the first value is a string with an embedded tab character "a\tb", and the second value is a simple string "c". After printing the record, assert that the output string equals the expected format where the first value is quoted due to the embedded tab character, followed by a tab delimiter, then the second unquoted value, and finally the record separator. The test validates that the MongoDB TSV format properly handles and quotes values containing tab characters when they conflict with the delimiter. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a buffered reader correctly handles sequential read operations while maintaining accurate character tracking and lookahead capabilities. Initialize two character arrays to serve as reference and result containers, then create a buffered reader with a simple alphabetic string as input. Set up the reference array with the first three expected characters, perform a partial read operation to extract three characters into the result array, and verify that the correct number of characters were read and that the arrays match. Assert that the last character read is correctly tracked and that the peek functionality returns the next character without advancing the reader position. Update the reference array with the next expected character, perform another single-character read operation, and confirm that the arrays still match and the last character tracking remains accurate. The test uses automatic resource management to ensure proper cleanup of the reader. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a predefined CSV format configuration can be correctly retrieved through both enumeration-based and string-based lookup mechanisms. Initialize the test by calling a helper method that accepts a specific predefined CSV format configuration designed for Excel compatibility and its corresponding string identifier. The helper method performs dual validation by first verifying that the format retrieved through enumeration lookup matches the expected format configuration, and then confirming that the same format can be obtained using string-based lookup with the format name. Assert that both retrieval methods return identical format configurations, ensuring consistency between the enumeration and string-based access patterns for predefined CSV formats. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the read functionality and lookahead capabilities of an extended buffered reader when processing character data in chunks. Initialize two character arrays of size five to serve as reference and result containers, then create an extended buffered reader using a string containing "abcdefg" as the input source. Set up the reference array with the first three characters 'a', 'b', and 'c', then call the read method to populate the first three positions of the result array and assert that exactly three characters were read. Verify that the reference and result arrays match, confirm that the last character read is 'c', and use the peek method to verify that the next character available is 'd' without consuming it. Update the reference array to include 'd' in the fifth position, then read one more character into the fourth position of the result array and assert that exactly one character was read. Finally, verify that the arrays still match and confirm that the last character read is now 'd'. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the configuration system properly throws conversion exceptions when attempting to retrieve typed data from properties containing unconvertible values. Initialize a data configuration with comprehensive test data covering all supported primitive and complex types including booleans, numeric types, dates, URLs, locales, colors, and network addresses, along with their corresponding list and array variants. Add two problematic properties to the configuration: one containing a generic unconvertible value and another containing an invalid string representation that cannot be parsed into any of the expected types. Systematically attempt to retrieve each supported data type as both arrays and lists from these problematic properties, verifying that each retrieval operation correctly throws a conversion exception when the stored value cannot be converted to the requested type. Additionally, test single-value retrievals for date, calendar, and address types with specific format patterns to ensure they also fail appropriately when given unconvertible data. The validation confirms that the configuration system maintains type safety by rejecting invalid conversions rather than returning unexpected results or causing runtime failures. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates the child replacement functionality of an immutable node structure by creating two child nodes with incrementing names and values, constructing a parent node with a default name and value that contains the first child, then calling the replace child method to substitute the original child with the replacement child. Assert that the updated node is a new instance distinct from the original while maintaining the same name and value properties, and verify that the node's children collection contains the replacement child in the correct position. The test uses JUnit framework for assertions.

This test validates the data configuration component's error handling when attempting to convert incompatible property values to various data types. Initialize a data configuration instance with a base configuration that uses comma delimiters, then populate it with extensive test data including boolean, numeric, URI, locale, color, date, and network address properties in multiple formats such as strings, objects, arrays, and lists. Add two problematic properties to the configuration: one containing a generic object instance and another containing an invalid string value. Systematically attempt to retrieve these problematic properties using all available type conversion methods including boolean arrays and lists, byte arrays and lists, short arrays and lists, integer arrays and lists, long arrays and lists, float arrays and lists, double arrays and lists, big integer arrays and lists, big decimal arrays and lists, URL arrays and lists, locale arrays and lists, color arrays and lists, date arrays and lists with pattern formatting, calendar arrays and lists with pattern formatting, and network address conversions. Assert that each conversion attempt throws a ConversionException, validating that the configuration properly rejects invalid data when type conversion fails. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the functionality for replacing an existing child node within a hierarchical tree structure. Initialize two distinct child nodes using a helper that creates uniquely named and valued child elements, then construct a parent node with a default configuration that includes the first child. Execute the child replacement operation by calling the replacement method with the original child as the target and the second child as the replacement. Verify that the replacement operation produces a new node instance that differs from the original while maintaining the same core properties like name and value. Confirm that the child collection of the updated node contains the replacement child in the correct position, ensuring the original child has been successfully substituted. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the preparation of node addition operations using an alternative expression syntax configuration. Initialize an expression engine with custom symbols that use forward slashes as property delimiters, square brackets for indexing, and at-signs to denote attributes, while disabling attribute end markers and escaped delimiters. Prepare an addition operation for a path targeting a test element within the first table's structure, then verify that the new node name matches the expected identifier, confirm it represents a regular node rather than an attribute, and validate that the parent contains the correct table data. Subsequently, prepare another addition operation for a completely new hierarchical path ending with an attribute marker, then confirm the attribute name is correctly identified, verify the path structure contains the expected sequence of intermediate node names, and ensure the parent reference points to the root node. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the expression engine's ability to prepare node addition operations using alternative syntax configurations. Initialize an expression engine with custom symbols that use forward slashes as property delimiters, square brackets for indexing, and at-signs for attribute markers. Set up a hierarchical node structure containing tables with fields and connection settings, along with an in-memory node handler. Call the engine's prepare add method twice with different path expressions - first with a standard element path targeting a test node under the first table, and second with a complete new path ending in an attribute marker. Assert that the first operation returns the correct new node name as "test", confirms it is not an attribute, and validates that the parent contains the expected table value. For the second operation, assert that the new node name is "attr", verify the path nodes contain the expected sequence of intermediate node names, and confirm that the root node serves as the parent for this attribute addition. The test uses JUnit framework for assertions and test execution.

This test validates that configuration values with variable interpolation can be correctly retrieved as various primitive data types and their wrapper equivalents. Initialize a configuration system that throws exceptions for missing properties and uses comma delimiters for lists. Add a numeric property with a simple value, then add another property that references the first property using variable interpolation syntax. Similarly, add a boolean property and create another property that interpolates the boolean value. Retrieve the interpolated numeric value as each primitive type including byte, short, integer, long, float, and double, asserting that each conversion returns the expected numeric result. Also retrieve the interpolated boolean value and verify it returns true. Then validate the same interpolated values can be retrieved as their corresponding wrapper types with null defaults, including Boolean, Byte, Short, Integer, Long, Float, Double, BigInteger, and BigDecimal, confirming that each wrapper conversion produces the correct boxed value. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the configuration system's ability to interpolate variable references and retrieve values as various primitive and wrapper data types. Initialize a base configuration object with exception throwing enabled for missing properties and comma-based list delimiter handling. Add properties to the configuration including a numeric value of one, a string value that references the numeric property through variable interpolation syntax, a boolean value of true, and a boolean string that similarly references the boolean property via interpolation. Exercise the configuration's type conversion capabilities by retrieving the interpolated numeric value as each primitive type including boolean, byte, short, int, long, float, and double, then assert that each returns the expected value of one with appropriate precision for floating-point comparisons. Similarly, retrieve the same interpolated value as wrapper object types including Boolean, Byte, Short, Integer, Long, Float, Double, BigInteger, and BigDecimal using methods that accept default values, and assert that each returns the properly wrapped equivalent of the expected value. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the DataConfiguration class properly throws ConversionException when attempting to convert incompatible property values to various data types, ensuring robust error handling during type conversion operations across all supported data types including primitives, objects, arrays, and lists. Initialize a BaseConfiguration with a DefaultListDelimiterHandler using comma as the delimiter, then wrap it in a DataConfiguration instance which is stored in the conf field of the test class. The setUp method extensively populates this configuration with properties for boolean, byte, short, integer, long, float, double, BigInteger, BigDecimal, URI, URL, Locale, Color, Date, Calendar, InetAddress, and InternetAddress types, including various list representations, string values, object values, arrays, and interpolated values, with specific date formatting configured using the DATE_PATTERN field. Add two problematic properties to the configuration: assign a new Object instance to key1 and the string value "xxxxxx" to key2 using the addProperty method. Execute a comprehensive series of assertThrows assertions that verify ConversionException is thrown when calling each of the DataConfiguration's type-specific getter methods with both key1 and key2, including getBooleanArray, getBooleanList, getByteArray, getByteList, getShortArray, getShortList, getIntArray, getIntegerList, getLongArray, getLongList, getFloatArray, getFloatList, getDoubleArray, getDoubleList, getBigIntegerArray, getBigIntegerList, getBigDecimalArray, getBigDecimalList, getURLArray, getURLList, getLocaleArray, getLocaleList, getColorArray, getColorList, getDateArray, getDateList, getCalendarArray, getCalendarList, along with parameterized methods getDate and getCalendar using DATE_PATTERN, and generic get methods for InetAddress and InternetAddress classes with key1. Each assertion validates that the configuration properly rejects conversion attempts for incompatible values by throwing the expected ConversionException, ensuring type safety and proper error propagation throughout the data conversion subsystem. The testing framework used is JUnit 5, identified by the @Test annotation and assertThrows method.

This test validates the capability to extract trailer comments from CSV data that contains both header and trailer comments. Initialize a CSV parser with input data that includes comment lines at both the beginning and end, using a format configuration that automatically detects headers. Process all records in the CSV by retrieving them completely, which triggers the parser to read through the entire input stream including any trailing comments. Verify that the parser correctly identifies the presence of a trailer comment by checking the trailer comment detection capability. Assert that the extracted trailer comment content matches the expected comment text. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the CSV lexer's ability to correctly handle escaped control characters when using a custom escape character instead of the default backslash. Initialize a Lexer instance by calling the helper method createLexer with the input string "character!rEscaped" and a CSVFormat configured with the DEFAULT format modified to use an exclamation mark as the escape character via withEscape. The createLexer helper method constructs a new Lexer using the provided CSVFormat and an ExtendedBufferedReader wrapping a StringReader of the input string. The input string contains the literal text "character" followed by an exclamation mark (the custom escape character), then the letter "r" (which should be interpreted as a carriage return when escaped), and finally "Escaped". Call the helper method assertNextToken with the expected content "character" concatenated with the CR constant and "Escaped", along with the lexer instance. The assertNextToken helper method internally calls assertContent with the expected content and the result of calling nextToken on the lexer with a new Token instance. The focal method nextToken processes the input stream character by character, recognizing the exclamation mark as an escape character and converting the escaped "r" sequence into an actual carriage return character through the readEscape method, which maps specific escape sequences like "r" to their corresponding control characters such as Constants.CR. Assert that the token content matches exactly the expected string where the escaped sequence "!r" has been properly converted to a carriage return character between "character" and "Escaped". Use the try-with-resources statement to ensure the lexer is properly closed after the test completes. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the CSV trimming functionality when a single value is printed with whitespace padding. Initialize a StringWriter to capture the output, then create a CSVPrinter using the StringWriter and CSVFormat DEFAULT configuration with trimming enabled by calling the withTrim method. Call the print method on the CSVPrinter with the string value " A " which contains leading and trailing spaces. After printing, assert that the StringWriter's toString method returns "A", verifying that the CSVFormat trim method correctly removes the surrounding whitespace from the printed value. The CSVPrinter automatically handles the trimming through the CSVFormat's print method, which internally calls the trim method when the trim flag is enabled. Close the CSVPrinter using the try-with-resources statement to ensure proper resource cleanup. This test uses the JUnit testing framework with the @Test annotation.

This test validates the functionality of preparing node additions using alternative expression syntax within a hierarchical configuration structure, specifically testing the DefaultExpressionEngine's prepareAdd method with custom delimiter and attribute syntax configurations. Initialize a helper method that configures a DefaultExpressionEngine with alternative syntax symbols, setting the attribute start to "@", property delimiter to "/", index start to "[", index end to "]", attribute end to null, and escaped delimiter to null, then assign this engine to the test class field. Call the prepareAdd method on the engine with the root node, the path "tables/table[0]/test", and the handler, capturing the returned NodeAddData object. Assert that the new node name equals "test", verify that isAttribute returns false indicating it is not an attribute node, and confirm that the parent's first child's value equals the first element of the TABLES array. Execute prepareAdd again with the root node, the path "a/complete/new/path@attr", and the handler, then assert that the new node name equals "attr". Invoke the helper method checkNodePath with the data object and the expected path nodes "a", "complete", "new", "path" to validate the intermediate path structure. Assert that the parent node is the same as the root node using assertSame. The checkNodePath helper method compares the expected path nodes array against the actual path nodes returned by getPathNodes, ensuring they match as a list. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a properties configuration layout can correctly parse and organize a simple properties file containing a single key-value pair with an associated comment. Initialize a configuration with legacy comma delimiter handling and create a layout manager to track the structure of properties data. Set up a properties builder and add a comment followed by a property with a test key and value. Load the configuration layout from the builder's reader to parse the properties data. Assert that no header comment exists at the file level, verify that exactly one key is present in the layout and that it matches the expected test key. Confirm that the comment associated with the key is correctly stored and retrievable, validate that no blank lines precede the property, and ensure the property is formatted as a single line. Finally, verify that the configuration can successfully retrieve the correct value for the test key. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the buffered reading functionality with lookahead capabilities in an ExtendedBufferedReader, specifically testing that the reader can correctly read characters into a buffer array while maintaining accurate state tracking of the last character read and peek functionality. Initialize two character arrays named ref and res, each with a length of 5, then create an ExtendedBufferedReader using a helper method with the string "abcdefg" as input, which constructs a new ExtendedBufferedReader wrapping a StringReader with the provided string. Set the first three elements of the ref array to 'a', 'b', and 'c' respectively, then call the read method on the ExtendedBufferedReader with the res array, starting offset 0, and length 3, asserting that it returns 3 to confirm three characters were successfully read. Assert that the ref and res arrays are equal using assertArrayEquals to verify the correct characters were read into the buffer. Call getLastChar on the reader and assert it equals 'c' to confirm the reader correctly tracks the last character that was read. Call peek on the reader and assert it returns 'd' to verify the lookahead functionality shows the next character without consuming it. Set the fifth element (index 4) of the ref array to 'd', then call read again on the reader with the res array at offset 4 and length 1, asserting that it returns 1 to confirm one character was read. Assert that the ref and res arrays are still equal using assertArrayEquals to verify the additional character was correctly placed in the buffer. Finally, call getLastChar again and assert it equals 'd' to confirm the reader's state was properly updated after the second read operation. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a configuration system correctly interpolates variable references within property values and retrieves them as various primitive and wrapper data types. The test exercises the BaseConfiguration class's type conversion capabilities with interpolated values, asserting that string-based property values containing variable references are properly resolved and converted to the expected numeric and boolean types. Initialize a BaseConfiguration instance in the setUp method, configure it to throw exceptions on missing properties, and set the list delimiter handler to use comma separation. Add four properties to the configuration: set "number" to the string "1", set "value" to a string containing a variable reference "${number}", set "boolean" to the string "true", and set "booleanValue" to a string containing the variable reference "${boolean}". Execute a series of assertions to validate primitive type retrieval by calling getBoolean on "booleanValue" and asserting it returns true, then call getByte, getShort, getInt, getLong, getFloat, and getDouble methods on the "value" property, asserting each returns the numeric value 1 with appropriate delta tolerance for floating-point comparisons. Continue with wrapper type validation by calling the same getter methods with a null default parameter on both "booleanValue" and "value" properties, asserting that getBoolean returns Boolean.TRUE, and that getByte, getShort, getInteger, getLong, getFloat, getDouble, getBigInteger, and getBigDecimal methods return their respective wrapper object equivalents of the value 1. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the functionality of replacing an existing child node within an immutable node structure, ensuring that the replaceChild method correctly substitutes one child node with another while maintaining the integrity of the parent node. The test exercises the ImmutableNode class's replaceChild method and validates the operation through assertions that confirm the node structure is properly updated and the replacement occurs as expected. Initialize two child nodes by calling the createChild helper method twice, which increments a childCounter field of the test class and creates ImmutableNode instances using the Builder pattern with names like "Child0", "Child1" and corresponding values like "childValue0", "childValue1". Create a default parent node by calling the createDefaultNode helper method with the VALUE constant, which internally calls another overloaded createDefaultNode method that uses the NAME constant to build an ImmutableNode with default properties. Add the first child node to the parent node using the addChild method, which returns a new ImmutableNode instance containing the child. Execute the focal method replaceChild on the parent node, passing the first child node as the node to be removed and the second child node as the replacement, which programmatically iterates through the parent's children collection and substitutes the old child with the new child while preserving all other children and returning a new ImmutableNode instance. Validate the replacement operation by calling the checkUpdatedNode helper method, which asserts that the original and updated nodes are not the same object reference using assertNotSame, and verifies that the updated node maintains the correct NAME and VALUE constants through assertEquals assertions. Finally, verify the child node structure by calling the checkChildNodes helper method, which confirms that the updated parent node contains the expected children by comparing the first child from the original node's children list (accessed via getChildren and get methods) with the replacement child node.
