Obtain a database connection from the data source and verify it is successfully created. Execute a simple database query using a prepared statement and confirm the result set is returned with accessible data. Repeat the same query execution a second time on the same connection to validate reusability. Close the connection explicitly and verify that attempting to create new statements on the closed connection properly throws an exception indicating the connection is no longer usable. Open a new connection using automatic resource management and repeat the same dual query execution pattern to confirm the data source continues to provide functional connections after the previous connection was closed and that query operations work consistently across different connection instances. The testing uses JUnit framework assertions and exception validation.

This test validates that the CSVFormat class correctly handles duplicate header elements in a deprecated manner by creating a string array containing two identical elements "A" and "A", then using the CSVFormat.DEFAULT static field to call the withHeader method with this duplicate header array to create a new CSVFormat instance. The test verifies that the resulting format preserves the duplicate headers by asserting that the getHeader method returns an array with a length of 2 using assertEquals, and then confirms that the returned header array exactly matches the original input array using assertArrayEquals. This test specifically examines the CSVFormat's ability to store and retrieve header configurations that contain duplicate column names, ensuring that the withHeader method on CSVFormat properly accepts and maintains arrays with repeated string values without modification or deduplication, while the getHeader method accurately returns the stored header array. The testing is performed using the JUnit framework with @Test and @SuppressWarnings("deprecation") annotations.

This test validates that CSV parsing correctly throws an exception when header validation is enabled but the header row contains missing column names. Initialize a string reader containing CSV data with a header row that has an empty column name between populated ones, followed by two data rows with complete values. Configure the default CSV format to use the first row as headers by enabling header parsing. Attempt to parse the input and immediately access the iterator to trigger header validation. Assert that an IllegalArgumentException is thrown during this operation, confirming that the parser properly detects and rejects malformed headers with missing column names when header validation is active. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a managed data source can successfully create a connection factory when configured with an external data source class and transaction manager. Initialize a managed data source with auto-close capabilities, then configure it by setting the external data source to a JDBC data source class name, specifying a driver class, and providing a transaction manager implementation. Call the connection factory creation method and assert that the returned factory is not null, confirming that the data source can properly instantiate and configure the external data source class to create a functional connection factory. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the basic functionality of a database connection pool data source and its ability to handle connection lifecycle operations. Initialize a driver adapter connection pool data source with a test driver, database URL, user credentials, and configuration settings for prepared statement pooling and underlying connection access, then create a shared pool data source wrapper with connection limits, wait timeouts, transaction isolation levels, and auto-commit behavior. Obtain a database connection from the data source and assert it is not null, then create a prepared statement for a simple dual table query and verify it is not null. Execute the query to retrieve a result set, assert the result set is not null, and confirm that it contains at least one row by calling next. Repeat the prepared statement creation and query execution process a second time with the same connection to test statement reuse. Close the connection explicitly and assert that attempting to create a statement on the closed connection throws a SQLException with an appropriate error message. Open a new connection using try-with-resources syntax and verify it is not null, then perform the same dual prepared statement and query execution sequence twice more to ensure the connection pool properly manages new connections. The testing framework used is JUnit.

Initialize a CSV format configuration by starting with the default format and configuring it with a header array containing duplicate string values such as "A" and "A". Call the header configuration method on the default format instance to create a new format with the duplicate header elements. Assert that the resulting format's header array has a length of 2, verifying that duplicate headers are preserved. Assert that the header array from the format matches the original input array exactly, confirming that both the content and order of duplicate elements are maintained. This test validates that the CSV format allows and correctly handles duplicate header names in its deprecated configuration mode, ensuring backward compatibility with legacy header handling behavior. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the connection factory creation behavior of a managed data source when configured with an XA data source class name. Initialize a basic managed data source within a try-with-resources block to ensure proper cleanup. Configure the data source by setting the XA data source property to a JDBC data source class name, specify a driver class name, and assign a transaction manager implementation. Call the create connection factory method on the configured managed data source to trigger the instantiation of the XA data source from the provided class name and the creation of the appropriate connection factory. Assert that the returned connection factory is not null, verifying that the data source successfully creates a connection factory when properly configured with XA data source settings. This test uses JUnit for the testing framework.

This test validates the basic functionality of database connection pooling and prepared statement execution through a DataSource implementation, specifically testing that connections can be obtained, used for SQL queries, properly closed, and that closed connections correctly throw exceptions when accessed. Initialize a DriverAdapterCPDS instance with the TesterDriver, set the URL to "jdbc:apache:commons:testdriver", configure the user as "foo" and password as "bar", disable pooled prepared statements, and allow access to underlying connections, then create a SharedPoolDataSource with the connection pool data source, setting maximum total connections via getMaxTotal, default max wait duration via getMaxWaitDuration, transaction isolation to TRANSACTION_READ_COMMITTED, and default auto-commit to true, assigning this as the DataSource field of the test class. Obtain a connection from the DataSource using getConnection and assert it is not null, then create a PreparedStatement with the SQL query "select * from dual" and assert it is not null, execute the query to get a ResultSet and assert it is not null, call next on the ResultSet and assert it returns true, close the ResultSet and PreparedStatement using try-with-resources, repeat this entire prepared statement execution sequence a second time with the same connection, explicitly close the connection using close, then assert that calling createStatement on the closed connection throws a SQLException with the message "Can't use closed connections" using assertThrows. Open a new connection using try-with-resources from the DataSource and assert it is not null, create a PreparedStatement with "select * from dual" and assert it is not null, execute the query to get a ResultSet and assert it is not null, call next on the ResultSet and assert it returns true, close the ResultSet and PreparedStatement automatically via try-with-resources, repeat this prepared statement execution sequence once more within the same connection scope, then allow the connection to close automatically when exiting the try-with-resources block. This test uses JUnit testing framework with @Test and @Override annotations.

This test validates that a database connection pool can handle concurrent access from multiple threads without timing out under normal conditions. Initialize a connection pool data source with a test database driver, URL, and credentials, then configure it to disable prepared statement pooling and allow access to underlying connections. Set up a shared pool data source that wraps the connection pool data source, configuring it with maximum connection limits, default transaction isolation level, and auto-commit behavior. Override the default maximum wait time to a specific duration to accommodate potential timing variations across different operating systems and virtual machines. Execute a multi-threaded test scenario that simulates concurrent database access with a short sleep duration between operations, ensuring that no connection timeouts occur and that the pool can successfully serve multiple threads simultaneously without blocking or failing. The test uses JUnit as the testing framework.

This test validates the session synchronization behavior when using managed database connections within a transaction context, specifically testing that the transaction manager's synchronization registration mechanism is properly invoked while the transaction synchronization registry remains unused. Initialize a TransactionManagerAdapter field of the test class that creates a TransactionAdapter when begin is called, where the TransactionAdapter's registerSynchronization method sets a transactionManagerRegistered boolean flag to true and its enlistResource method returns true. Initialize a TransactionSynchronizationRegistryAdapter field of the test class where the registerInterposedSynchronization method sets a transactionSynchronizationRegistryRegistered boolean flag to true. Create a BasicManagedDataSource instance and configure it with the transaction manager, transaction synchronization registry, and set the XADataSource property to "notnull". Create a BasicDataSource instance and configure it with driver class name "org.apache.commons.dbcp2.TesterDriver", URL "jdbc:apache:commons:testdriver", maximum total connections of 10, maximum wait duration of 100 milliseconds, default auto-commit to true, default read-only to false, default transaction isolation to TRANSACTION_READ_COMMITTED, default catalog to "test catalog", username "userName", password "password", validation query "SELECT DUMMY FROM DUAL", connection initialization SQL statements as a list containing "SELECT 1" and "SELECT 2", driver class loader as a TesterClassLoader instance, and JMX name "org.apache.commons.dbcp2:name=test". Create a dynamic proxy implementing XADataSource interface that delegates most method calls to the BasicDataSource but handles getXAConnection methods by returning a TesterBasicXAConnection wrapping the BasicDataSource connection. Set this proxy as the XA data source instance on the BasicManagedDataSource. Create a DataSourceXAConnectionFactory instance using the transaction manager and the XA data source proxy. Create a PoolableConnectionFactory instance with the XA connection factory and null object name, then configure it with validation query "SELECT DUMMY FROM DUAL", default read-only to true, and default auto-commit to true. Create a GenericObjectPool of PoolableConnection with the factory, set the factory's pool reference to this pool, and configure the pool with maximum total connections of 10 and maximum wait duration of 1 second. Create a ManagedDataSource instance with the pool and the XA connection factory's transaction registry, then set access to underlying connection allowed to true. Call begin on the transaction manager, obtain a connection from the managed data source using getConnection, assert that the connection is an instance of DelegatingConnection class, close the connection, and call commit on the transaction manager. Assert that transactionManagerRegistered is true and transactionSynchronizationRegistryRegistered is false. Close the BasicDataSource and BasicManagedDataSource instances in the teardown method. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the multi-threaded behavior of a shared pool data source under concurrent access conditions. Initialize a driver adapter connection pool data source with a test driver, JDBC URL, user credentials, and configure it to disable prepared statement pooling while allowing access to underlying connections. Create a shared pool data source that wraps the connection pool data source, setting maximum total connections, default wait duration, transaction isolation level to read committed, and auto-commit to true. Override the default maximum wait duration to 430 milliseconds to accommodate potential timing variations across different JVM implementations, particularly on Windows systems. Execute a multi-threaded test scenario with a 1-millisecond sleep duration, disabling certain boolean flags, and using the configured wait duration to verify that the data source handles concurrent thread access properly without blocking or timing out unexpectedly. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

Initialize a CSV format builder from the default format configuration, then call both the get method and the build method on the same builder instance to retrieve two separate CSV format objects. Assert that these two returned format objects are not the same instance using a reference equality check, which validates that the builder creates distinct format instances rather than returning cached or shared objects. This test ensures the builder pattern correctly produces independent format objects on each invocation. The test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a shared pool data source can properly configure and retrieve its login timeout setting. Initialize a driver adapter connection pool data source with database connection parameters including driver, URL, user credentials, and password, while disabling prepared statement pooling. Create a shared pool data source and associate it with the connection pool data source. Set the login timeout to a specific duration on the shared pool data source, then verify that retrieving the login timeout returns the exact same value that was configured. After testing, close the shared pool data source to clean up resources. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the creation of a connection factory when a BasicManagedDataSource is configured with an XA data source class name, ensuring that the data source can properly instantiate and configure XA data sources for distributed transaction management. The test specifically examines the createConnectionFactory method's ability to dynamically load and instantiate XA data source classes, and asserts that a non-null connection factory is returned to confirm successful configuration. Initialize a BasicManagedDataSource instance within a try-with-resources block to ensure proper resource cleanup. Configure the data source by calling setXADataSource with the canonical name of the JdbcDataSource class, which provides the fully qualified class name that the createConnectionFactory method will use to dynamically load and instantiate the XA data source. Set the driver class name using setDriverClassName with the Driver class name to establish the underlying JDBC driver configuration. Create and assign a new TransactionManagerImpl instance using setTransactionManager to provide the required transaction management capabilities for XA operations. Invoke the createConnectionFactory method on the configured BasicManagedDataSource instance, which will internally check that the transaction manager is set, detect that an XA data source class name is configured, use reflection to load the JdbcDataSource class, instantiate it via its no-argument constructor, create a DataSourceXAConnectionFactory with the transaction manager and XA data source instance, and return the resulting XA connection factory. Assert that the returned connection factory is not null using assertNotNull to verify that the XA data source instantiation and connection factory creation completed successfully. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the Test annotation.

This test validates the multi-threaded behavior of database connection pooling under specific timing constraints, specifically testing that the SharedPoolDataSource can handle concurrent connection requests with minimal wait times without encountering timeout or deadlock issues. Initialize a DriverAdapterCPDS instance and configure it with the TesterDriver, a test JDBC URL of "jdbc:apache:commons:testdriver", username "foo", password "bar", disabled prepared statement pooling, and enabled access to underlying connections. Create a SharedPoolDataSource instance and set the DriverAdapterCPDS as its connection pool data source, then configure it with maximum total connections from getMaxTotal, default maximum wait duration from getMaxWaitDuration, transaction isolation level of TRANSACTION_READ_COMMITTED, and default auto-commit set to true. Cast the DataSource field to SharedPoolDataSource and override the default maximum wait duration to 430 milliseconds to accommodate potential JVM timing variations, particularly on Windows systems where Thread.sleep may take longer than expected. Call the multipleThreads method with a sleep duration of 1 millisecond, both boolean parameters set to false, and the default maximum wait duration of 430 milliseconds to execute the concurrent connection testing scenario. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the login timeout configuration functionality of a shared pool data source component. Initialize a driver adapter connection pool data source with database connection parameters including driver, URL, user credentials, and password, then configure it to disable prepared statement pooling. Create a shared pool data source and associate it with the connection pool data source. Set the login timeout value to 10 seconds on the shared pool data source, then assert that retrieving the login timeout returns the same value of 10, confirming that the timeout configuration is properly stored and retrieved. After test completion, close the shared pool data source to release resources. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a CSV format parser correctly throws an IllegalArgumentException when encountering malformed header data with missing column names. Initialize a string reader containing CSV data with a header row that has an empty column name between populated ones, specifically "a,,c,d,e" followed by two data rows with complete values. Configure the default CSV format to use the first row as headers by calling the header configuration method, then parse the input using the configured format. Assert that attempting to access the parser's iterator throws an IllegalArgumentException, which indicates the format correctly detects and rejects the malformed header structure where column names are missing. The test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the login timeout configuration functionality for a shared pool data source, specifically testing that the setLoginTimeout and getLoginTimeout methods correctly store and retrieve the timeout value. Initialize a DriverAdapterCPDS instance and configure it with the test class fields DRIVER, URL, USER, and PASS which are private static final String fields, then disable pooled prepared statements by calling setPoolPreparedStatements with false. Create a SharedPoolDataSource instance and associate it with the connection pool data source using setConnectionPoolDataSource. Call setLoginTimeout on the SharedPoolDataSource with the integer value 10 to configure the login timeout period. Immediately assert that getLoginTimeout returns the exact value 10 using assertEquals to validate that the timeout configuration was properly stored and can be accurately retrieved. After test execution, clean up resources by calling close on the SharedPoolDataSource instance. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that CSV parsing correctly rejects input data containing duplicate header names when duplicate headers are explicitly disallowed. Initialize a CSV format configuration using the default settings, then enable header parsing and explicitly disable duplicate header names through the format's configuration options. Attempt to parse a CSV string that contains three columns with headers where the first and third column headers are identical, along with two rows of corresponding data values. Assert that this parsing operation throws an IllegalArgumentException due to the duplicate header violation, confirming that the parser properly enforces the duplicate header restriction when configured to do so. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a data source factory can properly configure all supported properties when creating a data source from a reference. Initialize a message logging system and clear any existing messages, then create a reference for a data source class with the factory class name. Retrieve a comprehensive set of test properties covering database connection settings, pooling parameters, validation options, eviction policies, abandonment tracking, statement pooling, JMX configuration, and various timeout values. Add each property as a string reference address to the reference object. Create a factory instance and use it to generate a data source from the reference, ensuring the factory processes all the configuration properties correctly. Verify that the resulting data source has all properties set to their expected values by checking both the data source configuration and its underlying connection pool settings. Confirm that no warning or error messages were logged during the factory creation process, indicating all properties were recognized and applied successfully. Clean up the message logging system after completion. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the CSV format's header retrieval method returns a defensive copy rather than the original header array. Initialize a string array containing three header values such as "one", "two", and "three", then create a CSV format instance using the default format configuration and configure it with the header array using the header configuration method. Retrieve the header array from the format instance using the header getter method and store it in a separate variable representing the copied header. Modify all elements of the copied header array by assigning new values like "A", "B", and "C" to each position. Assert that the arrays are not equal by comparing the original format's header with the modified copy using array equality checking, ensuring the modification did not affect the original format's internal header. Additionally, assert that the two header arrays are not the same object reference using reference equality checking, confirming that the getter method returns a defensive copy rather than exposing the internal array. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

Initialize a transaction manager and begin a transaction during setup, then create two delegating database connections within a try-with-resources block to test shared transaction behavior. Assert that the two connection objects are not equal to each other, but verify that their innermost delegates are equal using the innermost delegate equals method, indicating they share the same underlying connection within the transaction context. Commit the transaction through the transaction manager, then trigger connection state adjustment by calling the get auto-commit method on both connections. Assert that the connections are still not equal to each other, but now verify that their innermost delegates are no longer equal, confirming they use separate underlying connections outside of a transaction. Begin a new transaction, trigger connection state adjustment again by calling get auto-commit on both connections, then assert that the connections remain unequal but their innermost delegates are once again equal, demonstrating that connections share underlying resources when within a transaction boundary. Clean up by committing any active transaction and performing standard teardown. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that database connections properly share their innermost delegates when operating within a transaction context and correctly isolate them when outside of transactions. Initialize a transaction manager and begin a transaction, then create two delegating database connections within a try-with-resources block. Verify that while the connection wrappers themselves are not equal, their innermost delegates are equal when within the active transaction by calling the delegate equality comparison methods. Commit the transaction and trigger connection state adjustment by accessing the auto-commit property on both connections. Assert that the connections now have different innermost delegates since they are no longer within a shared transaction context. Begin a new transaction and again access the auto-commit properties to adjust the connections to the new transaction state. Confirm that the innermost delegates are once again equal within the new transaction context while the wrapper connections remain unequal. The test ensures proper connection sharing behavior across transaction boundaries and validates that connections correctly adapt their internal state when transaction contexts change. Cleanup occurs automatically through the try-with-resources mechanism and transaction manager teardown. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that CSV format configuration rejects carriage return characters as delimiters by verifying an exception is thrown during format construction. Initialize a test that accesses the default CSV format configuration and attempts to create a new format builder instance. Configure the builder to use a carriage return character as the field delimiter by converting the carriage return constant to a string value. Attempt to finalize the format configuration by calling the builder's get method, which should trigger validation of the delimiter setting. Assert that this configuration attempt throws an IllegalArgumentException, confirming that the CSV format properly validates delimiter characters and prevents the use of line break characters like carriage return as field separators. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that setting JNDI environment properties through a properties collection properly clears any previously set individual properties. Initialize a connection pool data source with database driver configuration and connection credentials, then configure a shared pool data source to use this connection pool with prepared statement pooling disabled. Set an individual JNDI environment property with a specific name and value, then verify the property can be retrieved correctly. Create a new properties collection with a different property, then apply this collection to replace the JNDI environment settings. Assert that the previously set individual property is no longer accessible, confirming that applying a properties collection clears existing individual properties rather than merging them. Clean up by closing the shared pool data source after the test completes. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that connection pooling properly handles fast-fail validation when custom disconnection error codes are configured. Initialize a connection pool with a factory that has auto-commit and read-only settings enabled, then configure the pool to validate connections on return and enable fast-fail validation on the factory. Set up a custom list containing a specific error code and assign it as the disconnection codes for the factory. Borrow a connection from the pool and access its underlying test connection, then simulate a fatal database error by setting a failure with an exception that uses the custom error code. Attempt to create a statement from the connection, which should trigger validation and throw an exception due to the simulated failure. Clear the failure condition on the underlying connection and close the pooled connection, which should trigger validation on return that detects the previous fatal error and prevents the connection from being returned to the pool. Assert that both the active and idle connection counts in the pool are zero, confirming that the faulty connection was properly removed rather than returned to the pool. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the JNDI environment property management behavior of a shared pool data source, specifically ensuring that setting a new properties collection clears previously set individual properties. Initialize a driver adapter connection pool data source with database connection parameters including driver, URL, user credentials, and disabled prepared statement pooling, then configure a shared pool data source to use this connection pool. Set an individual JNDI environment property with a key-value pair such as "name" and "king", then assert that retrieving this property returns the expected value "king". Create a new properties object and populate it with a different property like "fish" and "kohi", then apply this entire properties collection to the shared pool data source's JNDI environment. Assert that the previously set individual property is now null, confirming that setting a properties collection replaces rather than merges with existing individual properties. After test completion, close the shared pool data source to release resources. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the roundtrip capability of CSV data processing by ensuring that data can be written and then read back identically. Initialize a string writer to capture output and define sample CSV data containing headers and multiple records with comma-separated values and carriage return line feed separators. Create a CSV printer using the default format configuration and the string writer, then create a CSV parser using the same default format to parse the predefined sample data. Iterate through each parsed record from the parser and print each record to the printer, effectively copying the parsed data to the output writer. After processing all records, close both the printer and parser resources automatically through try-with-resources. Finally, assert that the string content written to the output writer exactly matches the original input data string, confirming that the CSV processing maintains data integrity throughout the write-read cycle. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the CSV parsing framework correctly throws an IllegalArgumentException when attempting to parse CSV data with a header row that contains missing column names. Initialize a StringReader with CSV content containing the string "a,,c,d,e\n1,2,3,4,5\nv,w,x,y,z", which represents a header row with five columns where the second column name is empty (indicated by the double comma between 'a' and 'c'), followed by two data rows with complete values. Access the DEFAULT field of the CSVFormat class, which is a public static final CSVFormat representing the standard comma-separated format with default settings. Call the withHeader method on this format instance to enable automatic header parsing from the first row of the input. Pass the StringReader to the parse method of the configured CSVFormat to create a CSVParser instance. Immediately call the iterator method on the parser to begin processing the CSV data and trigger header validation. Use the assertThrows method to verify that an IllegalArgumentException is thrown during this operation, confirming that the parser correctly detects and rejects the malformed header containing the missing column name in the second position. The test framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation and the assertThrows assertion method.

This test validates that the CSV parser correctly rejects duplicate header names when configured to disallow them. Initialize a CSV format using the default configuration, then configure it to enable header parsing and explicitly disable duplicate header names by setting the allow duplicate header names flag to false. Provide CSV input data containing three columns where the first and third column headers are identical (both named "a"), with the middle column named "b", followed by two data rows with values "1,2,3" and "x,y,z". Attempt to parse this malformed CSV data using the CSV parser's static parse method, passing the input string and the configured format. Assert that an IllegalArgumentException is thrown during the parsing operation, confirming that the parser properly validates and rejects CSV data with duplicate header names when this validation is enabled. The test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the fast fail validation behavior of a poolable connection factory when custom disconnection SQL codes are configured. Initialize a generic object pool with a poolable connection factory that uses a test driver connection factory with a JDBC URL like "jdbc:apache:commons:testdriver", setting default auto-commit and read-only to true. Configure the pool to test connections on return, then retrieve the factory from the pool and enable fast fail validation. Create a list of custom disconnection SQL codes containing "XXX" and assign it to the factory's disconnection codes collection. Borrow a poolable connection from the pool and extract its innermost delegate as a test connection. Set up a fatal SQL exception on the native connection with state code "XXX" matching the configured disconnection code, then assert that calling create statement on the connection throws a SQL exception due to the fatal condition. Clear the failure condition on the native connection and close the poolable connection, which should trigger validation on return due to the test-on-return setting. Assert that the pool has zero active connections and zero idle connections, confirming that the connection with the fatal exception was properly rejected and not returned to the pool. Clean up by closing the pool in teardown. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the behavior of database connection sharing within transactional contexts by verifying that connections properly share their innermost delegates during active transactions and revert to separate delegates when transactions are completed. Initialize the test by calling setUp which invokes the parent setUp method and begins a new transaction using the transactionManager begin method. Create two DelegatingConnection instances named connectionA and connectionB by casting the results of newConnection method calls to DelegatingConnection types, managing them within a try-with-resources block for automatic cleanup. Assert that the two connection objects are not equal to each other using assertNotEquals for both connectionA compared to connectionB and connectionB compared to connectionA. Verify that the connections share the same innermost delegate during the active transaction by calling assertTrue on connectionA innermostDelegateEquals method with connectionB getInnermostDelegate as the argument, and similarly assertTrue on connectionB innermostDelegateEquals method with connectionA getInnermostDelegate as the argument. Commit the current transaction using transactionManager commit method. Trigger connection state adjustment by calling getAutoCommit method on both connectionA and connectionB to force them to adapt to the completed transaction state. Assert that without an active transaction, the connections no longer share innermost delegates by calling assertNotEquals for both connection comparisons and assertFalse on both innermostDelegateEquals method calls with the opposite connection's innermost delegate. Begin a new transaction using transactionManager begin method. Again trigger connection state adjustment by calling getAutoCommit on both connections to make them adapt to the new transaction. Verify that the connections once again share innermost delegates within the new transaction by asserting assertNotEquals for the connection objects themselves and assertTrue for both innermostDelegateEquals method calls. Clean up resources in tearDown by checking if transactionManager getTransaction returns a non-null value, committing the transaction if present using transactionManager commit, and calling the parent tearDown method. This test uses the Test annotation from a testing framework.

This test validates the JNDI environment property management functionality in a database connection pooling system, specifically testing that setting JNDI environment properties via a Properties object clears any previously set individual properties on the SharedPoolDataSource. Initialize a DriverAdapterCPDS instance and configure it with the DRIVER, URL, USER, and PASS test class fields which are private static final String constants, then disable prepared statement pooling by calling setPoolPreparedStatements with false. Create a SharedPoolDataSource instance and associate it with the configured DriverAdapterCPDS using setConnectionPoolDataSource. Set an individual JNDI environment property on the SharedPoolDataSource by calling setJndiEnvironment with the string literal "name" as the key and "king" as the value, then assert that getJndiEnvironment returns "king" when queried with the "name" key using assertEquals to validate the property was stored correctly. Create a new Properties object and add a property with key "fish" and value "kohi" using setProperty, then call setJndiEnvironment on the SharedPoolDataSource passing this Properties object to replace all existing JNDI environment properties. Assert that getJndiEnvironment returns null when queried with the previously set "name" key using assertNull to verify that the individual property was cleared when the Properties object was applied. Close the SharedPoolDataSource in the teardown method to release resources. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

Initialize a string writer to capture output and define CSV data containing three rows with comma-separated values including headers "a,b,c", data "1,2,3", and "x,y,z" with carriage return and line feed separators. Create a CSV printer using the string writer and default CSV format, then create a CSV parser using the same CSV data string and default format within a try-with-resources block. Iterate through each CSV record from the parser and print each record to the CSV printer using the print record method. After processing all records, assert that the string writer's output exactly matches the original CSV data string to verify that the CSV data can be successfully written and then read back to produce identical content. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

Initialize a CSV format using the default configuration and create a string writer to capture output. Set up a CSV string containing four rows of comma-separated values with pairs like "a1,b1" through "a4,b4", and create a corresponding two-dimensional string array with the same data for comparison. Create a CSV printer using the format and string writer, then create a CSV parser from the input string using the same format. Verify the printer's initial state by asserting that its record count is zero. Use the printer to output all records from the parser by calling the print records method with the parser as input. Close both the printer and parser resources. Parse the string writer's output back into a new CSV parser using the same format, retrieve all records as a list, and assert that the list is not empty. Finally, compare the expected two-dimensional array against the actual parsed records using a utility comparison method with a comparison parameter of negative one. This test uses JUnit as the testing framework.

This test validates the wrapper functionality of a database result set delegation mechanism. Initialize a test connection with basic credentials and create a delegating connection wrapper around it, then mock a result set and wrap it using the delegation wrapping utility to create a delegating result set. Call the wrapping method to create another delegating result set from the connection and mocked result set. Verify that unwrapping the delegating result set with various interface types returns the correct underlying components - assert that unwrapping with the general result set interface returns the delegate itself, unwrapping with the specific delegating result set type also returns the delegate, and unwrapping with the exact class type of the mocked result set returns the original mock. Confirm that unwrapping with an incompatible type like string returns null. Test the wrapper detection capability by asserting that the delegate correctly identifies itself as a wrapper for the result set interface, the delegating result set type, and the specific mock class type, while confirming it does not identify as a wrapper for incompatible types like string. This test validates the fast fail validation mechanism for database connections when custom SQL codes are configured to identify fatal disconnection errors. This test validates that connection pool closure properly handles exceptions thrown by individual connections during the shutdown process. This test validates the connection properties parsing functionality of a database connection pool, specifically testing how the BasicDataSource class handles various formats of connection property strings and ensures proper property replacement behavior. This test validates the behavior of connection pool lifecycle management when stopping and restarting a data source. Close the data source which should physically close idle pooled connections while leaving active checked-out connections unaffected. Assert that the first delegating connection remains open but the second inner connection is now physically closed, and verify the pool has no idle connections. Restart the data source to create a new connection pool, obtain two new connections from the refreshed pool, and close them to return them to the new pool. Finally, close the original first connection which should now be physically closed since it belongs to the old pool that was destroyed during the restart. The test uses JUnit framework for assertions and test execution.

Initialize a string reader with CSV data containing values separated by double pipe delimiters and ending with the delimiter sequence, specifically "a||b||c||d||||f||". This test validates that a database connection pool properly handles and reports invalid SQL statements in its connection initialization collection by verifying that appropriate exceptions are thrown with descriptive error messages. Clean up resources in the tearDown method by calling the superclass tearDown method, closing the BasicDataSource using the close method, and setting the data source field to null. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation and assertThrows and assertTrue assertion methods.

Initialize a basic data source with test driver configuration including connection pooling settings, validation queries, and JMX naming, then configure it to allow access to underlying connections and set the maximum total connections to 2. This test validates the prepared statement pooling functionality of a shared pool data source by exercising callable statement creation and reuse patterns with different callback implementations. Initialize a driver adapter connection pool data source with a test driver, database URL, user credentials, and disabled prepared statement pooling, then configure a shared pool data source with connection pooling parameters including maximum total connections, wait duration, transaction isolation level, and auto-commit settings. Execute the test behavior three times using different callable statement callback implementations that represent various parameter configurations for statement preparation. For each callback, create a new driver adapter with enabled prepared statement pooling and a maximum of 10 prepared statements, then establish a shared pool data source configured similarly to the setup. Obtain a connection from the non-pooling data source, set it on the callback, and create two callable statements sequentially, executing queries on each and capturing their delegate hash codes to verify they are different instances since pooling is disabled. Next, obtain a connection from the pooling-enabled data source, create two more callable statements through the same callback, execute their queries, and capture hash codes to verify they are identical instances, confirming that prepared statement pooling is functioning correctly. Assert that connections, statements, and result sets are not null, that result sets contain data, that hash codes differ when pooling is disabled, and that hash codes match when pooling is enabled. The test uses JUnit framework annotations and assertions.

This test validates that callable statement pooling behaves correctly when enabled versus disabled in a database connection pool. Initialize a connection pool data source with database driver configuration, credentials, and statement pooling disabled, then create a shared pool data source with transaction settings and connection limits. Execute the core validation logic three times using different callback strategies for preparing callable statements with varying parameter signatures. Verify that connections are successfully established, callable statements are created properly, and result sets contain data by checking for successful query execution and result navigation. Assert that when statement pooling is disabled, consecutive callable statements have different hash codes indicating new statement creation, while when statement pooling is enabled, consecutive callable statements share the same hash code confirming statement reuse. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the least recently used eviction behavior of a prepared statement pool within a database connection pooling system. Initialize the data source with a maximum of three open prepared statements, then establish a database connection and verify it is not null. Create three prepared statements with different SQL queries selecting literal values, extracting their innermost delegate instances for direct access to the underlying prepared statement objects. Close each prepared statement in sequence with brief delays between closures to ensure distinct timestamps for proper LRU ordering. Create a fourth prepared statement which should trigger eviction of the oldest cached statement from the pool due to the three-statement limit. Assert that the first statement's inner delegate throws an SQL exception when attempting to clear parameters, confirming it has been properly closed and evicted, while verifying the second and third inner delegates can still successfully clear parameters. Create a fifth prepared statement using the same SQL as the first to confirm the evicted statement does not return from the pool, then assert the new inner delegate is a different instance than the original first statement. Verify that the second inner delegate now throws an SQL exception due to LRU eviction while the third inner delegate remains operational. This test uses JUnit framework with standard assertions and exception testing.

Initialize a BasicDataSource using the createDataSource helper method, then configure it with driver class name "org.apache.commons.dbcp2.TesterDriver", URL "jdbc:apache:commons:testdriver", maximum total connections of 2, default auto-commit as true, default read-only as false, default transaction isolation as TRANSACTION_READ_COMMITTED, default catalog, username "userName", password "password", validation query "SELECT DUMMY FROM DUAL", connection initialization SQLs as a list containing "SELECT 1" and "SELECT 2", driver class loader as TesterClassLoader, and JMX name "org.apache.commons.dbcp2:name=test". Set the data source to allow access to underlying connections and configure maximum total connections to 2. Obtain two DelegatingConnection instances by calling getConnection twice on the data source, then retrieve their innermost delegate connections using getInnermostDelegate. Assert that the second inner connection is not closed using assertFalse with isClosed. Close the second delegating connection using close, then assert again that the second inner connection remains not closed. Call close on the data source to shut down the pool, which should physically close idle connections while leaving checked-out connections unaffected. Assert that the first delegating connection is not closed using assertFalse with isClosed, then assert that the second inner connection is now closed using assertTrue with isClosed. Verify that the number of idle connections is 0 using assertEquals with getNumIdle. Restart the data source by calling start to create a new pool, then obtain two new connections and close them both. Finally, close the first original connection, which should trigger physical closure of the orphaned connection from the old pool, and assert that the first inner connection is now closed using assertTrue with isClosed. Clean up by calling the superclass tearDown method, closing the data source, and setting it to null. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the pooling behavior of callable statements in database connection pools, specifically testing that prepared statement pooling works correctly when enabled and is bypassed when disabled. Initialize a DriverAdapterCPDS instance with the TesterDriver, set the URL to jdbc:apache:commons:testdriver, configure user credentials as foo and bar, disable pooled prepared statements, and allow access to underlying connections, then create a SharedPoolDataSource with the connection pool data source, set maximum total connections using getMaxTotal, configure default max wait duration using getMaxWaitDuration, set transaction isolation to TRANSACTION_READ_COMMITTED, and enable default auto-commit. Execute the testPoolPreparedCalls method which calls a helper method doTestPoolCallableStatements three times with different AbstractPrepareCallCallback implementations: CscbString, CscbStringIntInt, and CscbStringIntIntInt. The helper method creates a new DriverAdapterCPDS with identical database configuration but enables pooled prepared statements and sets maximum prepared statements to 10, then creates a SharedPoolDataSource configured similarly to the test setup. First, obtain a connection from the original DataSource ds field, set the connection on the callback, assert the connection is not null, create two callable statements using the callback's getCallableStatement method, assert each statement is not null, capture their delegate hash codes using getDelegateHashCode, execute queries on both statements, assert the result sets are not null and contain at least one row, then verify the hash codes are different since statement pooling is disabled. Next, obtain a connection from the pooling-enabled data source, repeat the same process of creating two callable statements and executing queries with assertions, but verify the hash codes are equal since prepared statement pooling is enabled and should reuse the same underlying statement. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that a prepared statement pool correctly implements least-recently-used eviction behavior when the maximum pool size is exceeded. Configure the data source to allow a maximum of three open prepared statements, then establish a database connection and verify it is valid. Create three distinct prepared statements with different query strings, extracting references to their underlying delegate implementations for later validation. Close each statement with brief delays between closures to ensure different timestamps, allowing all three to enter the pool as idle statements. Create a fourth prepared statement which should force the oldest statement out of the pool due to the size limit, then verify the first statement's delegate has been properly closed by attempting to call a method on it and expecting a database exception. Confirm that the second and third statement delegates remain operational by successfully calling methods on them. Create a fifth prepared statement using the same query as the first to verify that a new delegate is created rather than reusing the evicted one, then confirm the second statement delegate is now closed while the third remains open. This test uses JUnit framework.

This test validates the Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction behavior of a prepared statement pool when it reaches capacity, specifically testing that the oldest cached statements are properly closed and evicted when new statements exceed the pool limit. Initialize the test by calling the setUp method which enables pooled prepared statements and sets the maximum open prepared statements to 2, then override this by setting the data source maximum open prepared statements to 3. Obtain a database connection using the getConnection method and assert it is not null. Create three prepared statements with distinct SQL queries selecting literal values 'a', 'b', and 'c' from dual, extracting the innermost delegate PreparedStatement from each DelegatingPreparedStatement wrapper to access the actual pooled statement instances. Close the first statement, sleep for 100 milliseconds to ensure different timestamps, close the second statement, sleep again for 100 milliseconds, then close the third statement to populate the pool with three idle statements. Create a fourth prepared statement with SQL selecting 'd' from dual, which should force the oldest statement (the first one) out of the pool due to the 3-statement limit, and assert this new statement is not null. Verify the LRU eviction by asserting that calling clearParameters on the first inner statement throws a SQLException with the message "expecting SQLExcption - statement should be closed", while confirming the second and third inner statements remain open by successfully calling clearParameters on them. Create a fifth prepared statement reusing the original 'a' query and extract its innermost delegate, then assert that this new inner statement is not the same object as the original first inner statement to confirm the old statement was not reused. Finally, assert that calling clearParameters on the second inner statement now throws a SQLException indicating it has been closed due to LRU eviction, while verifying the third inner statement remains open by successfully calling clearParameters. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the equality behavior of CSV format objects when quote characters are explicitly set to null. This test validates the creation of a basic data source through a factory method when no connection factory class name is explicitly configured. Initialize a test that validates the equality behavior of CSVFormat instances when both have null quote characters, specifically testing the deprecated functionality. This test validates the CSV printer's behavior when writing records without quote mode enabled. Initialize a CSV format builder using the Excel preset, configure it with a null string representation of "N/A" and enable ignoring surrounding spaces, then build the format instance. Create a string buffer to capture the output and instantiate a CSV printer with the buffer and format using a try-with-resources statement to ensure proper cleanup. Call the print record method on the printer with an array containing null, the string "Hello", another null, and the string "World" as values. After the printer automatically closes, assert that the buffer's string representation equals "N/A,Hello,N/A,World\r\n", verifying that null values are correctly converted to the specified null string, non-null values are preserved, and the Excel format's carriage return plus line feed record separator is appended. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that header configuration creates an independent copy of the provided header array rather than maintaining a reference to the original. Apply the header configuration to a default CSV format using the header modification capability, which should internally create a copy of the provided array. Verify that the configured format returns the same header values by comparing the arrays element-wise for equality. Confirm that the format maintains data independence by asserting that the returned header array is not the same object reference as the original input array, ensuring that subsequent modifications to either array will not affect the other. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

Initialize a StringReader with CSV content containing a comment line starting with hash, followed by a header row with values a, b, c, and two data rows with values 1, 2, 3 and x, y, z respectively. Create a CSVParser using the CSVFormat DEFAULT format configured with a comment marker set to hash character and header parsing enabled by calling withCommentMarker and withHeader methods. Use a try-with-resources statement to automatically close the parser after obtaining an Iterator from the parser by calling the iterator method. Finally, call assertThrows with NoSuchElementException class and a method reference to the iterator's next method to verify that attempting to retrieve the next element from a closed parser's iterator throws the expected exception. This test validates the behavior of CSV parser resource management and iterator state after parser closure, ensuring that iterators become unusable once their associated parser is closed. The testing framework used is JUnit.

Initialize a test to validate CSV printing behavior when no quote mode is explicitly configured, ensuring that null values are properly converted to a specified null string representation and that surrounding spaces are ignored during processing. This test validates CSV printing functionality when no quote mode is explicitly configured. Initialize a test to verify that backslashes in CSV data are treated as literal characters rather than escape characters when no escape character is configured in the CSV format. Create a string containing CSV data with the value "a,\\,,b\\\\,,", which represents fields separated by commas where some fields contain literal backslashes and empty values. Call the isEscapeCharacterSet method on the format instance and assert that it returns false, confirming that no escape character is configured. Use the createLexer helper method to instantiate a Lexer object, passing the CSV data string and the format configuration. Assert that the second token has type TOKEN and content "\\", confirming that a single backslash is treated as literal content rather than an escape character. Assert that the third token has type TOKEN and empty content "", representing the empty field between consecutive commas. Assert that the fourth token has type EORECORD and content "b\\", indicating the end of the first record with a field containing a literal backslash. Assert that the fifth token has type TOKEN and content "\\", again confirming that backslashes are treated literally. Assert that the sixth and final token has type EOF and empty content "", signifying the end of the input stream. The test validates that when escape character processing is disabled, backslashes in CSV data are preserved as literal characters rather than being interpreted as escape sequences. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that CSV parsing functionality correctly handles a null format parameter by defaulting to standard parsing behavior. Initialize a test to verify that CSVPrinter correctly handles database result sets with varying maximum row limits by creating a StringWriter for output capture and establishing an H2 in-memory database connection using the helper method getH2Connection which loads the H2 driver and connects to a test database with credentials. This test validates the CSV parsing behavior when a null format parameter is provided to the parse method, ensuring that null format defaults to the standard CSV format for proper record parsing. This test validates that CSV format configuration can properly extract header names from an enumeration class. Initialize a CSV format using the default configuration and configure it to use an enumeration class as the header source by calling the header configuration method with the enumeration class type. Retrieve the header array from the configured format and verify that it contains the expected string values corresponding to the enumeration constants, specifically checking that the array matches the exact sequence of names from the enumeration. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the equality behavior of CSV format objects when their quote characters differ. Initialize a CSV format instance using a factory method that creates a format with a single quote character as the delimiter, then use its builder to set the quote character to a double quote and retrieve the resulting format as the right-hand comparison object. Create a second CSV format by taking the builder from the right format, modifying its quote character to an exclamation mark, and retrieving that as the left-hand comparison object. Assert that the two format objects are not equal using a helper method that performs bidirectional inequality checks, verifying that formats with different quote character settings are properly distinguished by the equals implementation. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that CSV format configurations with different quote characters are properly recognized as unequal when compared. Initialize a CSV format configuration with a single quote character as the delimiter and a double quote character as the quote character, then create a second format by copying the first configuration and modifying it to use an exclamation mark as the quote character instead. Assert that the two format configurations are not equal to each other, verifying that the equality comparison correctly identifies the difference in quote character settings. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that CSV parsing correctly handles files with byte order marks when using a reader-based input stream. Initialize a byte order mark input stream from a CSV resource file containing header data, then wrap it with an input stream reader using UTF-8 encoding. Create a CSV parser using the builder pattern, configuring it with the reader and Excel format that includes header processing. Iterate through each parsed record and assert that the date column value is not null, ensuring the parser can successfully extract header-based data despite the presence of the byte order mark. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

Initialize two CSV format instances to test the equality behavior when quote policies differ, where the first format is created with a single quote delimiter, double quote character, and quote mode set to ALL, and the second format is derived from the first but with the quote mode changed to MINIMAL. Assert that the two formats are not equal by calling a helper method that performs bidirectional inequality assertions, verifying that formats with different quote modes are properly distinguished. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that parsing a CSV file with the Informix unload CSV format correctly handles malformed records and throws an expected exception on the third row. Initialize a CSV parser using the Informix unload CSV format configuration and a test file containing three rows of data with timestamp, widget type, password-like content, numeric values, and truncated text fields. Parse the first record and verify it contains the expected timestamp, Android widget class name, password string with special characters, zero value, and truncated password text across five columns. Parse the second record and confirm it has a similar structure with a different timestamp, same widget type, password content with different special characters, zero value, and password text ending with escaped backslashes. Attempt to parse the third record and assert that an IOException is thrown, indicating the parser correctly identifies and rejects malformed data at the expected failure point. The test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that two CSV format configurations with different quote policies are properly recognized as unequal. Initialize a CSV format with a single quote delimiter, then configure it with double quote characters and set the quote mode to quote all fields. Create a second format by modifying the first format to use minimal quoting instead of quoting all fields. Verify that the two formats are not considered equal by asserting their inequality in both directions. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test verifies that two CSVFormat instances with different quote characters are not considered equal, ensuring the equals method correctly distinguishes between formats based on their quote character settings. Initialize a CSVFormat instance by calling newFormat with a single quote character as the delimiter, then use the builder method to create a builder, call setQuote with a double quote character, and call get to obtain the configured format, storing this as the right format. Create a second CSVFormat instance by calling builder on the right format, then call setQuote with an exclamation mark character, and call get to obtain the modified format, storing this as the left format. Use a helper method that calls assertNotEquals twice to verify that the right format is not equal to the left format and that the left format is not equal to the right format, ensuring bidirectional inequality validation. The helper method internally uses Assertions.assertNotEquals from the JUnit testing framework to perform the actual equality assertions. This test is annotated with @Test and uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the CSV parser's ability to handle Byte Order Mark (BOM) encoded input streams when parsing CSV files with headers. Initialize a BOM input stream by creating a stream from a CSV resource file located at "org/apache/commons/csv/CSVFileParser/bom.csv" using the system class loader, then wrap this stream in an input stream reader configured with UTF-8 encoding. Create a CSV parser using the builder pattern, setting the reader to the BOM-aware input stream reader and configuring the format to use Excel format with header parsing enabled. Execute the parsing operation by iterating through each record in the parser using a for-each loop, and for each record encountered, assert that the value retrieved from the "Date" column is not null to verify that the BOM handling does not interfere with proper header recognition and data extraction. The test uses automatic resource management through try-with-resources to ensure proper cleanup of both the reader and parser resources. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that CSV parsing correctly handles carriage return line feed line endings by processing a multi-line CSV string containing mixed data values. Initialize a parser using a builder pattern with a character sequence that includes carriage return line feed sequences separating multiple records with varying field counts and content types including empty values. Configure the parser to process the input string and retrieve all parsed records into a collection. Assert that exactly four records are extracted from the input, confirming that the parser properly recognizes carriage return line feed combinations as valid record separators and correctly segments the data despite the mixed field structure. The testing is performed using JUnit framework.

Initialize a CSV parser using a builder pattern with a character sequence containing comma-separated values that include carriage return and line feed endings, specifically a string with values "foo", "baar", "hello", "world", and "kanu" separated by CRLF sequences. Create the parser within a try-with-resources block to ensure proper resource management and automatic cleanup. Call the get records method on the parser to retrieve all parsed CSV records as a list. Assert that the resulting list contains exactly four records, validating that the parser correctly handles carriage return line feed line endings and properly separates the CSV data into the expected number of records. The test uses JUnit as the testing framework.

This test validates that a CSV parser can correctly handle Byte Order Mark (BOM) encoded files when using a Reader-based input stream, specifically testing the parser's ability to read CSV data with headers from a BOM-encoded file and access column values by header name. Initialize a BOMInputStream by calling the helper method createBOMInputStream with the resource path "org/apache/commons/csv/CSVFileParser/bom.csv", which uses ClassLoader.getSystemClassLoader().getResource to locate the resource and opens its input stream, then wraps it in a BOMInputStream. Create an InputStreamReader from this BOMInputStream using UTF_8_NAME charset encoding. Build a CSVParser instance using CSVParser.builder(), configure it by calling setReader with the InputStreamReader and setFormat with EXCEL_WITH_HEADER format, then call get to obtain the parser instance. Use a try-with-resources block to ensure both the Reader and CSVParser are automatically closed. Iterate through all records in the parser using forEach, and for each record, call assertNotNull on the result of record.get("Date") to verify that the "Date" column value is not null, ensuring the parser correctly reads the BOM-encoded CSV file and can access header-named columns. This test uses JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the rollback utility's handling of null database connections. Initialize the test by calling the database utility's rollback method with a null connection parameter to verify that the utility can gracefully handle null input without throwing exceptions or causing errors. The test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the database rollback functionality can safely handle null connection inputs without throwing exceptions. Initialize the test by calling the rollback utility method with a null connection parameter, then verify that the operation completes successfully without any errors being thrown. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a CSV parser correctly handles carriage return line feed (CRLF) line endings when parsing CSV data with multiple records. Initialize a string containing CSV data with CRLF line endings, specifically "foo
baar,
hello,world
,kanu", which represents comma-separated values where each field or record is terminated with carriage return followed by line feed characters. Within the try block, call the getRecords method on the parser instance to retrieve all parsed CSV records as a List of CSVRecord objects.
