Create a piped input stream connected to the piped output stream and continuously read from it until all data is consumed, effectively draining the process output. Wait for the process to complete within a specified timeout period using the result handler, then retrieve the exit value to verify successful process termination. The test uses JUnit 5 framework with conditional execution disabled on Windows operating systems.

This test validates the execution watchdog functionality by testing both process termination scenarios and watchdog timeout behavior through iterative execution with progressively increasing timeout values. Initialize integer variables for start position at 0, execution seconds at 1, offset multiplier at 1, maximum retries at 180, and counters for process termination and watchdog kills both starting at 0. Create a CommandLine instance using the pingScript field of the test class and add an argument by converting the sum of seconds plus 1 to a string using the addArgument method. Record the current system time in milliseconds as the start time, then enter a loop from the start offset to the maximum retries value. Within each iteration, create an ExecuteWatchdog instance with a timeout calculated as seconds multiplied by 1000 plus the current offset multiplied by the offset multiplier, then set this watchdog on the exec field of the test class using setWatchdog. Execute the command line using the execute method on exec within a try-catch block, where successful execution increments the process terminated counter and breaks the loop if this counter exceeds 5. When an ExecuteException is caught, assert that the watchdog killed the process using assertTrue with the killedProcess method and increment the watchdog killed process counter. After the loop completes, calculate the average execution time by dividing the elapsed time by the sum of both counters, then print statistics including processes terminated, processes killed, multiplier, max retries, and average elapsed time. Assert that the process terminated counter is greater than 0 with the message "Not a single process terminated on its own" and assert that the watchdog killed process counter is greater than 0 with the message "Not a single process was killed by the watch dog". The test method uses the Disabled annotation with the message "The test is fragile and might fail out of the blue" and the Test annotation, utilizing the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the command line parsing functionality by creating a command line object from a Windows-style command string and verifying the extracted arguments. This test validates the string representation functionality of a command line parser by creating command line objects with various argument configurations and verifying their toString output format. This test validates the string representation functionality of command line parsing by creating command line objects with different argument configurations and verifying their formatted output. This test validates the asynchronous execution of a Unix command with stream redirection and process monitoring capabilities, specifically testing the execution of the `/bin/ls /opt` command while redirecting only stdout to a piped output stream and ensuring proper process completion handling. Initialize a CommandLine object by calling the parse method with the string `/bin/ls`, then add the argument `/opt` using the addArgument method to create a command that lists the contents of the `/opt` directory. Create a PipedOutputStream to capture the process's standard output and a ByteArrayOutputStream to capture standard error, then instantiate a PumpStreamHandler with these streams to handle the process's output redirection. Set the stream handler on the executor using the setStreamHandler method, then create a DefaultExecuteResultHandler to manage asynchronous process execution callbacks. Execute the command asynchronously by calling the execute method with the command line and result handler, which starts the process in a separate thread and immediately returns control to the main thread. Create a PipedInputStream connected to the PipedOutputStream and continuously read from it using the read method in a while loop until the stream is exhausted (read returns -1), effectively consuming all output from the process. After the read loop completes, call the waitFor method on the result handler with a WAIT timeout value (which is a field of the test class) to block until the process completes or the timeout expires. Finally, call the getExitValue method on the result handler to retrieve the process exit code, which will throw an IllegalStateException if the process has not yet completed, thereby validating that the process finished successfully within the timeout period. The test is annotated with @Test and @DisabledOnOs(OS.WINDOWS) to indicate it should not run on Windows systems, and uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that command line objects produce equivalent string representations when arguments are added using different chaining approaches. Initialize two command line instances with the same executable name "useradd", then add identical arguments to both using different method call patterns - one instance should add each argument with separate method calls using a flag "-g", a group name "tomcat", and a username "foo", while the other should chain the first two arguments in a single fluent call followed by adding the final argument separately. Assert that both command line objects generate identical string representations when their toString methods are called, verifying that the internal argument storage and string conversion behavior remains consistent regardless of how the arguments were added to the command line builder. This test validates the command line parsing functionality for a Windows-specific executable path with complex arguments containing quoted configuration parameters. This test validates that command line construction produces equivalent string representations regardless of whether arguments are added individually or through method chaining. This test validates the robustness of CSV format handling by performing randomized testing specifically on the MySQL CSV format configuration. This test validates that command line construction properly handles complex arguments including JVM options with quoted parameters when quote handling is disabled. This test validates the command line argument handling functionality of a command line builder component. This test validates the command line parsing functionality with variable expansion capabilities by creating substitution maps containing environment variables like Java home directory paths, application main class names, and file objects representing XML and text files. This test validates that two different approaches for building command line arguments produce equivalent string representations when using the CommandLine class from the Apache Commons Exec library. This test validates the timeout configuration functionality for stream handling operations. Initialize a stream handler and verify that the initial timeout is set to zero duration. This test validates the functionality of adding complex command line arguments containing special characters and quoted parameters to a CommandLine object, specifically testing that the addArguments method correctly handles an array of arguments with JVM options and the toStrings method accurately represents the complete command line. This test validates command line parsing functionality with variable expansion capabilities, specifically testing how the CommandLine class handles placeholder substitution in command strings and arguments using various substitution map configurations. Initialize a HashMap named substitutionMap containing key-value pairs where JAVA_HOME maps to /usr/local/java, appMainClass maps to foo.bar.Main, file1 maps to a File object for ./pom.xml, and file2 maps to a File object for .\temp\READ ME.txt, then create an incompleteMap HashMap containing only the JAVA_HOME mapping. Call the parse method on CommandLine with the command string containing placeholders ${JAVA_HOME}/bin/java ${appMainClass} without providing a substitution map, then assert that the getExecutable method returns a string starting with ${JAVA_HOME} and assert that getArguments returns an array containing the single element ${appMainClass}. Call parse with the complete substitutionMap, then assert that getExecutable does not contain the ${JAVA_HOME} placeholder using assertFalse, verify that the executable contains the substring local at a position greater than zero using assertTrue and indexOf, and confirm that getArguments returns an array containing foo.bar.Main. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the basic construction and string representation functionality of a command line parser when initialized with a simple executable name. This test validates the stop timeout configuration functionality of a PumpStreamHandler, which manages stream pumping threads for process execution, by testing the setStopTimeout method's ability to accept various input types and convert them to appropriate Duration values. This test validates that a process execution watchdog correctly terminates a long-running process when it exceeds a specified timeout threshold. This test validates that a color representation in the CIE Luv color space produces the correct string format when converted to text. This test validates the cyclic redundancy check calculation functionality for PNG image processing. Initialize a CRC calculator and create a small byte array containing four zero-valued elements. This test validates that a photometric interpreter for floating-point image data correctly tracks and returns the maximum X and Y coordinates of pixels that have been processed. This test validates the CRC calculation functionality of a PNG CRC component by exercising its core checksum computation methods. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a photometric interpreter correctly tracks and reports the maximum coordinate boundaries encountered during pixel interpretation operations. This test validates the creation and structure of a fully transparent 32-bit RGBA ICO file format where alpha channel transparency is properly handled during bitmap generation and file construction. Generate a 32-bit RGBA bitmap using the GeneratorFor32BitBitmaps class by calling the generate32bitRGBABitmap method with parameters 0x00000000 for the first color value, 0x00FFFFFF for the second color value, 0 for an integer parameter, and true for a boolean parameter, which produces a bitmap array where every pixel is fully transparent. Use the helper method writeICONDIR to write the ICO directory header by passing the binary output stream along with values 0 for reserved field, 1 for type field, and 1 for count field, which writes the 6-byte ICO file header structure using write2Bytes calls for each field. Execute the helper method writeBITMAPINFOHEADER to create the bitmap info header by passing the binary output stream with values 16 for width, 32 for height (double the actual height as per ICO format requirements), 1 for color planes, 32 for bit count, and 0 for compression, colors used, and colors important parameters, which writes the 40-byte BITMAPINFOHEADER structure using write4Bytes and write2Bytes calls for the various bitmap metadata fields. The test method includes a commented-out call to the helper method writeAndReadImageData that would normally verify the generated ICO file by writing it to a temporary file and reading it back using the Imaging class, but this validation step is disabled because fully transparent pixels cause the alpha channel to be ignored during the verification process. This test validates the maximum coordinate tracking functionality of a photometric interpreter for floating-point image data by verifying that the interpreter correctly reports the highest x and y coordinates where pixels have been processed. This test validates the value retrieval functionality of a TIFF raster data component by comparing floating-point and integer value access methods across all pixel coordinates. This test validates that image parsing functionality can handle corrupted icon directory entries by verifying that the system ignores malformed metadata and successfully reads the actual bitmap data. Assert that the directory exists and is indeed a directory. Retrieve all files from this directory and iterate through each one, filtering to process only files with PNG extensions in lowercase. For each valid PNG file, perform a loop of ten iterations where you read the image into a buffered image object using the imaging library's image reading functionality, assert that the resulting image is not null, create a temporary file with a unique name incorporating the original filename and iteration number, write the buffered image to this temporary file in PNG format using the imaging library's write functionality, and use this newly written file as input for the next iteration. This process tests the stability of the read-write cycle by ensuring that images can be repeatedly processed without corruption or failure. The test uses JUnit framework for assertions and test execution.

This test validates the LZW compression and decompression roundtrip functionality for TIFF image data by ensuring that compressed data can be decompressed and recompressed to produce identical results. The test exercises the TiffImageParser collectRawImageData method and the MyLzwDecompressor and MyLzwCompressor classes through a series of compression operations, validating the integrity of the LZW algorithm implementation with assertEquals assertions. Initialize the test by calling the getTiffImages helper method to retrieve a list of TIFF image files, then iterate through each file in the collection. For each image file, create a ByteSource instance using the file static method with the current image file as the parameter. Instantiate a TiffImageParser and call its collectRawImageData method with the ByteSource and a new TiffImagingParameters object to extract raw image data as a list of byte arrays. For each byte array in the extracted data, invoke the decompressRoundtripAndValidate helper method which performs the core validation logic. Within the helper method, set the LZW_MINIMUM_CODE_SIZE constant to 8 and create an empty ArrayList to store integer codes. Implement a MyLzwDecompressor Listener with code and init callback methods, where the code method adds each received code to the codes list. Create a ByteArrayInputStream from the source byte array and instantiate a MyLzwDecompressor with the minimum code size, ByteOrder BIG_ENDIAN, true for the third parameter, and the decompression listener. Call the decompress method on the decompressor with the input stream and source array length to produce the decompressed byte array. Implement a MyLzwCompressor Listener with clearCode, dataCode, eoiCode, and init methods that track compression codes and validate them against the previously captured decompression codes. Instantiate a MyLzwCompressor with the same parameters as the decompressor plus the compression listener, then call its compress method with the decompressed data to produce a compressed byte array. Assert that the compressed array length equals the original source array length using assertEquals, then iterate through each byte position and assert that each byte in the compressed array matches the corresponding byte in the original source array using assertEquals. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework as indicated by the Test and Disabled annotations.

This test validates the creation and properties of a physical scale object configured for meter-based units. Create a physical scale instance using the factory method for meter-based creation, passing horizontal and vertical units per pixel values of 1.0 and 2.0 respectively. Assert that the resulting physical scale object correctly identifies itself as being in meter units by verifying the meter units check returns true. Confirm that the scale object properly distinguishes its unit type by asserting that the radian units check returns false. Validate that the horizontal units per pixel property returns the expected value of 1.0 within a defined delta tolerance. Finally, verify that the vertical units per pixel property returns the expected value of 2.0 within the same delta tolerance. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the WebP image parser correctly rejects attempts to read WebP files as BufferedImage objects by throwing an appropriate exception with a descriptive error message. Initialize a File object by retrieving the resource path for an empty WebP test image file located at "/images/webp/empty/empty-100x100.webp" from the WebPReadTest class resources, then create a new WebPImageParser instance to serve as the parser under test. The getBufferedImage method is the focal point of this test, representing the parser's attempt to convert a WebP image file into a Java BufferedImage object, which is currently unsupported functionality that should fail gracefully with an informative error message rather than succeeding or throwing an unclear exception. After confirming the exception is thrown, assert that the exception's message contains the exact text "Reading WebP files is currently not supported" using the assertTrue method to validate that users receive clear feedback about the limitation. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that attempting to read image data from a WebP file format correctly throws an unsupported operation error. Attempt to extract buffered image data from the byte source using the parser, which should fail with an imaging exception since WebP reading functionality is not currently implemented. This test validates the iterative reading and writing functionality of PNG image files by processing multiple PNG files through repeated read-write cycles to ensure data integrity is maintained across operations. The test examines the Imaging class's getBufferedImage and writeImage methods by loading PNG files from a test directory, performing ten consecutive read-write operations on each file, and asserting that valid BufferedImage objects are produced at each iteration. Initialize a string variable with the path to the PNG test images directory by calling FilenameUtils.separatorsToSystem on the concatenated ImagingTestConstants.TEST_DATA_SOURCE_FOLDER and "/images/png/3", then create a File object from this path and assert that it exists and is a directory using assertTrue. Retrieve all files in the directory using listFiles and iterate through each file, skipping any that are not regular files or do not have a ".png" extension in lowercase. For each valid PNG file, execute debug logging using Debug.debug methods to output the current image file being processed. Set the current file as the starting point and perform ten iterations where each iteration calls Imaging.getBufferedImage on the current file to load it as a BufferedImage, then assert the returned image is not null using assertNotNull. Create a temporary file using Files.createTempFile with a name constructed from the original filename, iteration number, and ".png" extension, then write the BufferedImage to this temporary file using Imaging.writeImage with the ImageFormats.PNG format parameter. Update the current file reference to point to the newly created temporary file for the next iteration, effectively creating a chain of ten read-write operations that tests the stability of the PNG encoding and decoding process. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the parsing of an 8-bit per pixel icon image without a transparency mask. Initialize a byte array output stream and create a big-endian binary output stream wrapper around it. Write the icon file header by outputting the magic number, total file size, image type identifier for a 16x16 8-bit image, and the image data size. Generate the 8-bit pixel data by iterating through a predefined 16x16 image array, writing maximum intensity values for non-zero pixels and a specific lower value for zero pixels. Flush the output stream and pass the resulting byte array along with foreground and background color values to a helper method that reads the image data back using the imaging library, verifies the parsed image is not null, confirms the dimensions match the original array, and validates the pixel values against expected foreground and background colors. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the bidirectional conversion between RGB and HSL color representations by exercising the color conversion utility methods. Initialize a loop that iterates through a collection of sample RGB integer values representing various colors. For each RGB value, call the color conversion utility to transform the RGB integer into an HSL color object, then immediately convert the resulting HSL object back to an RGB integer using the reverse conversion method. Output debug information displaying both the HSL color object and the converted RGB value in decimal and hexadecimal formats. Assert that the original RGB value matches the round-trip converted RGB value by comparing their hexadecimal string representations after masking both values with a white color mask to ensure only the relevant color bits are compared. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the parsing of an 8-bit per pixel ICNS icon image without a mask by constructing a binary ICNS file format and verifying the resulting buffered image. Initialize foreground and background color values as black and light gray respectively, then create a byte array output stream wrapped with a big-endian binary output stream. Write the ICNS magic number, total file size, image type identifier for 16x16 8-bit images, and chunk size to establish the file header structure. Generate the 8-bit image data by iterating through a 16x16 pixel grid, writing 255 for non-zero pixels in the reference image array and 43 for zero pixels to create the color palette indices. Flush the output stream and pass the resulting byte array along with the foreground and background colors to a helper method that reads the binary data using an imaging library to create a buffered image. Assert that the resulting image is not null, verify its dimensions match the expected 16x16 size, and validate that the pixel colors correspond correctly to the foreground and background values based on the original image data. This test uses JUnit framework.

This test validates the bidirectional conversion accuracy between RGB and HSL color representations by ensuring that converting from RGB to HSL and back to RGB preserves the original color values. Initialize a collection of sample RGB color values that represent various color scenarios, then iterate through each RGB value to perform the conversion workflow. Assert that the original RGB value matches the round-trip converted RGB value by comparing their hexadecimal string representations after masking to ensure only the relevant color bits are considered, confirming that no precision is lost during the conversion process. The test uses JUnit as the testing framework.

This test validates the creation and configuration of a PhysicalScale object using meter units, ensuring that the factory method correctly initializes the scale with the specified horizontal and vertical pixel ratios and properly sets the unit type to meters rather than radians. Initialize a PhysicalScale instance by calling the createFromMeters method with horizontal units per pixel value of 1.0 and vertical units per pixel value of 2.0, which internally constructs a new PhysicalScale object using the METER_UNITS constant along with the provided pixel ratio values. Assert that the resulting PhysicalScale object correctly identifies itself as using meter units by calling isInMeters and verifying it returns true, then confirm it does not use radian units by calling isInRadians and asserting it returns false. Validate the horizontal pixel scaling by calling getHorizontalUnitsPerPixel and asserting the returned value equals 1.0 within the delta tolerance, then verify the vertical pixel scaling by calling getVerticalUnitsPerPixel and asserting the returned value equals 2.0 within the same delta tolerance. The test uses JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation and assertion methods.

This test validates the bidirectional color conversion functionality between RGB and HSL color spaces to ensure data integrity is preserved during round-trip conversions. The test iterates through a collection of sample RGB integer values stored in the SAMPLE_RGBS field of the test class, converting each RGB value to HSL format using the ColorConversions class's convertRgbToHsl method, which returns a ColorHsl object containing hue, saturation, and lightness components as double values, then immediately converts the resulting HSL color back to RGB format using the convertHslToRgb method to verify the conversion accuracy. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the comprehensive parsing and image processing capabilities of a JPEG image parser across multiple input files. This test validates the parsing and rendering of an 8-bit per pixel ICNS icon image without a mask by constructing a synthetic ICNS file and verifying the resulting BufferedImage matches expected pixel values. Initialize integer variables for foreground color as 0xff000000 and background color as 0xffcccccc, then create a ByteArrayOutputStream and wrap it with a big-endian AbstractBinaryOutputStream using the bigEndian method. Write the ICNS file structure by calling write4Bytes with IcnsImageParser ICNS_MAGIC constant, followed by the total file size calculated as 4 plus 4 plus 4 plus 4 plus 16 times 16 bytes, then write the ICNS_16x16_8BIT_IMAGE type from IcnsType using getType method, and finally write the image data size as 4 plus 4 plus 16 times 16. Generate the 8-bit image data by iterating through a 16x16 pixel grid using nested loops for y and x coordinates from 0 to 15, writing 0xff byte values where the IMAGE array element is non-zero and 43 byte values where it is zero. Call flush on the binary output stream to ensure all data is written, then invoke the helper method writeAndReadImageData with parameters "8bpp-image-no-mask", the byte array from toByteArray, and the foreground and background color values. The helper method uses Imaging getBufferedImage to parse the raw ICNS data with filename "description.icns", asserts the resulting BufferedImage is not null using assertNotNull, verifies the image width equals IMAGE array's first dimension length and height equals IMAGE array length using assertEquals, and calls verify method to validate pixel colors against foreground and background values. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the JPEG image parsing functionality by processing parameterized image file inputs through a comprehensive workflow. Retrieve comprehensive image information from the file using the imaging utility, then assert that the returned image info object is not null to verify successful parsing. This test validates the image processing capabilities of the Imaging utility class by exercising metadata extraction, ICC profile retrieval, image information gathering, and buffered image creation operations on TIFF image files. This test validates the ability to store and retrieve numeric values at specific coordinates within a raster data structure that supports multiple samples per pixel. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the ability to embed and retrieve physical scale metadata in PNG images using meter-based units. Initialize a PNG image parser and create imaging parameters with a physical scale configuration specifying horizontal and vertical units per pixel in meters using small decimal values. Generate test image data with ascending pixel values in a square format, then convert this raw pixel data into a buffered image representation. Write the image to a byte array output stream using the parser with the configured physical scale parameters, capturing the resulting PNG byte data. This test validates the functionality of setting and retrieving raster data values using both floating-point and integer methods in a TIFF raster data structure. The test creates a TiffRasterDataInt instance with dimensions specified by the test class fields width and height, and 2 samples per pixel, then iterates through each coordinate position to verify that setValue and setIntValue methods correctly store data and that getValue and getIntValue methods accurately retrieve the stored values. Initialize a TiffRasterDataInt instance using the width and height fields from the test class along with a samples per pixel value of 2. Create nested loops to iterate through each y coordinate from 0 to height and each x coordinate from 0 to width. For each coordinate pair, calculate an index value using the formula y multiplied by width plus height. Call the setValue method on the instance with the current x and y coordinates, sample index 1, and the calculated index plus 0.4 as a float value. Immediately retrieve the stored value using getValue with the same coordinates and sample index, cast the result to an integer, and assert that it equals the original index value with the message "Set/get value test failed". Next, call setIntValue with the same coordinates, sample index 1, and the calculated index as an integer. Retrieve this value using getIntValue with matching parameters and assert that the returned value equals the index with the message "Set/get int value test failed". This test validates the comprehensive image processing capabilities of the Apache Commons Imaging library by verifying that TIFF image files can be successfully parsed and their metadata, information, and pixel data can be extracted without errors. This test validates the ability to extract and read metadata from a WebP image file that contains embedded EXIF data. Generate a 256x256 pixel array with ascending ARGB values where each pixel's color components are calculated from the sum of its coordinates modulo 256, then convert this raw pixel data into a buffered image. This test validates the functionality of writing and reading PNG images with physical scale metadata specified in meters, ensuring that the scale information is correctly preserved during the image processing cycle. This test validates the core image processing functionality of an imaging library by exercising metadata extraction, image information retrieval, ICC profile access, and buffered image creation operations on PSD format files. Iterate through each File in the images list, and for each iteration, call Debug debug with the string "imageFile" and the current File object to log the file being processed. This test validates the comprehensive image processing capabilities of the Apache Commons Imaging library when handling PSD (Photoshop Document) image files, specifically testing that metadata extraction, image information retrieval, ICC profile access, and buffered image generation all function correctly without errors or null returns. Initialize a BMP RGB writer instance and create a buffered image with dimensions of 2x2 pixels using color type 5. This test validates the creation and properties of a physical scale object configured with radian units. This test validates the EXIF rewriter's ability to update Microsoft XP metadata fields in JPEG images. Initialize an image with existing EXIF data and clean it by removing XMP and IPTC metadata to prevent interference with XP tag visibility on Windows systems. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the creation and configuration of a PhysicalScale object using radian units, ensuring that the factory method correctly initializes the scale with the specified horizontal and vertical units per pixel values. Initialize a PhysicalScale object by calling the createFromRadians method with horizontal units per pixel value of 2.0 and vertical units per pixel value of 1.0, which creates a new PhysicalScale instance configured with radian units and the specified scaling factors. Assert that the resulting PhysicalScale object is not configured for meter units by calling isInMeters and verifying it returns false. Assert that the PhysicalScale object is correctly configured for radian units by calling isInRadians and verifying it returns true. Validate that the horizontal scaling is properly set by calling getHorizontalUnitsPerPixel and asserting the returned value equals 2.0 within the delta tolerance. Validate that the vertical scaling is properly set by calling getVerticalUnitsPerPixel and asserting the returned value equals 1.0 within the delta tolerance. The test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

This test validates the image data extraction functionality for RGB bitmap writing by verifying that pixel data is correctly converted and formatted. Initialize an RGB bitmap writer and create a small buffered image with specific dimensions and color type. Extract the raw image data from the buffered image using the bitmap writer's data extraction capability. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the capability to modify and rewrite metadata tags within image files containing existing metadata information. Initialize an image processing environment by obtaining an image file that contains metadata and cleaning it to remove any conflicting metadata formats like XML and IPTC data. Extract the metadata from the cleaned image and convert it to a format suitable for manipulation, then create a metadata rewriter component and obtain an output configuration from the extracted metadata. Finally, validate that the rewritten image contains the expected metadata values by extracting the metadata from the modified image data and verifying that all directories contain the correct author, comment, subject, and title values that were added during the modification process. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the proper handling of icon images that have both 1-bit-per-pixel mask data and 8-bit-per-pixel mask data within the same icon file. Create a binary output stream and construct an icon file by writing the magic header followed by the total file size, then add a 16x16 1-bit image entry with its type identifier and size, followed by image data representing all black pixels and a 1-bit mask indicating full opacity for all pixels. Next, append an 8-bit mask entry with its type identifier and size, writing mask data that creates a pattern of fully opaque and fully transparent pixels based on a predefined image pattern. Flush the stream and pass the resulting byte array along with black foreground and background colors to a helper method that reads the constructed icon data back as an image, verifies the image is not null, confirms the dimensions match the expected 16x16 size, and validates the pixel values against the expected pattern using the provided colors. The test uses JUnit for assertions.

This test validates the image data extraction functionality of a BMP RGB writer by verifying that pixel data is correctly converted to the BMP format's byte array representation and that the writer's configuration properties are properly set. Initialize a BmpWriterRgb instance, then create a BufferedImage with dimensions of 2 by 2 pixels and a type value of 5, which represents a specific image format configuration. Call the getImageData method on the BmpWriterRgb instance, passing the BufferedImage as a parameter to extract the raw pixel data as a byte array, where this method processes each pixel from bottom to top, extracting RGB values and padding rows to 4-byte boundaries as required by the BMP format specification. Assert that the getBitsPerPixel method returns exactly 24, confirming the writer is configured for 24-bit RGB color depth without alpha channel support. Assert that the getPaletteSize method returns 0, verifying that no color palette is used since RGB format stores colors directly rather than using indexed colors. Assert that the returned byte array has a length of exactly 16 bytes, which accounts for the 2x2 pixel grid with 3 bytes per pixel plus padding to align each row to 4-byte boundaries. Finally, assert that the byte array contents exactly match a new byte array containing sixteen zero values, confirming that the default black pixels in the BufferedImage are correctly converted to the expected BMP format representation. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the ability to store and retrieve numeric values at specific coordinates within a raster data structure that supports floating-point data storage. Initialize a raster data container with predefined dimensions and configure it to handle multiple samples per pixel. Verify that each retrieved value matches the originally stored value, ensuring data integrity for both floating-point and integer storage operations. Assert that the set and get operations maintain perfect fidelity across all coordinate positions in the raster. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the functionality of rewriting EXIF metadata in JPEG images by modifying Microsoft XP tag fields while preserving image integrity. Initialize a helper method to clean an image by first calling cleanImage with the result of getImageWithExifData, which removes XMP metadata using JpegXmpRewriter removeXmpXml method and then removes IPTC metadata using JpegIptcRewriter removeIptc method, returning the cleaned byte array. Extract the TIFF metadata from the cleaned image by calling Imaging getMetadata method and converting it to TiffImageMetadata using the toTiffMetadata helper method, which casts JpegImageMetadata to extract EXIF data or directly returns TiffImageMetadata if already in that format. Remove existing Microsoft XP tag fields by calling removeField on the root directory for TIFF_TAG_ARTIST, then systematically remove and add Microsoft XP tag fields: remove EXIF_TAG_XPAUTHOR and add it back with the AUTHOR constant value, remove EXIF_TAG_XPCOMMENT and add it with the COMMENT constant, remove EXIF_TAG_XPSUBJECT and add it with the SUBJECT constant, and remove EXIF_TAG_XPTITLE and add it with the TITLE constant. Create a ByteArrayOutputStream and call updateExifMetadataLossy on the ExifRewriter with the cleaned image bytes, output stream, and modified output set to generate the updated image. Finally, validate the modifications by calling the checkFields helper method with the resulting byte array, which extracts metadata from the updated file, iterates through all TiffDirectory instances to collect field values for each Microsoft XP tag, and asserts that the collected values contain the expected AUTHOR, COMMENT, SUBJECT, and TITLE constants using assertTrue assertions. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the ICNS image parser's handling of 1-bit-per-pixel icon masks versus 8-bit-per-pixel masks for 16x16 images. Initialize foreground and background color values as black hexadecimal integers, then create a byte array output stream with a big-endian binary output stream wrapper. Write the ICNS magic header and file size calculation to establish the file format structure. Construct a 1-bit-per-pixel image and mask section by writing the appropriate ICNS type identifier and data size, followed by image data representing all black pixels and mask data representing full opacity using nested loops to generate 16x16 pixel arrays with 0xff byte values. Add an 8-bit-per-pixel alpha mask section by writing its type identifier and size, then iterate through a predefined image array to write transparency values where non-zero pixels receive full opacity (0xff) and zero pixels receive full transparency (0x00). Flush the binary output stream and invoke a helper method to write the constructed byte array data and read it back as a buffered image using the imaging library. The helper method asserts that the resulting image is not null, verifies the image dimensions match the expected 16x16 size, and calls a verification method to validate pixel values against the foreground and background colors. This test uses JUnit framework annotations and assertions.

This test validates the image processing capabilities of an imaging library by exercising metadata extraction, image information retrieval, and buffered image creation operations on PAM format image files. Initialize debug logging to track the test execution, then retrieve a collection of PAM image files from the test resources. For each image file in the collection, enable debug output to log the current file being processed, then call the imaging library's metadata extraction method to obtain image metadata and assert that the returned metadata object is not an instance of the File class. Finally, call the buffered image creation method to generate a BufferedImage representation of the file and assert that the resulting buffered image object is not null. The test uses JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that an image processing library can successfully extract metadata, image information, and buffered image data from a collection of PAM format image files. Initialize debug logging to track the test execution, then retrieve a collection of PAM image files from the test resources. For each image file in the collection, enable debug output to log the current file being processed, then extract the image metadata using the imaging library's metadata extraction capability and verify that the returned metadata is not incorrectly typed as a file object.
