Call the assertCounts method with parameters 0, 1, 1, and the result of PathUtils delete method applied to the temporary directory path resolved with the file name, which validates that zero directories, one file, and one total item were deleted during the operation. The test leverages a helper method that performs the core deletion logic and assertion validation, ensuring that the file deletion process works correctly when force deletion is enabled. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the file system containment checking functionality to ensure that the directoryContains method correctly identifies when files are not contained within specific directories. The test verifies that the FileUtils directoryContains method returns false for files that exist outside of or in sibling directories to the specified directory parameter. Initialize the test environment using the setUp method which creates a hierarchical directory structure with directory1 and directory2 as subdirectories of the top temporary directory field annotated with @TempDir, and directory3 as a subdirectory of directory2, then create file1 within directory1, file2 within directory2, and file3 directly in the top directory, using FileUtils touch method to create these files on the file system. Execute the focal method FileUtils directoryContains four times with different directory and file combinations to test negative containment scenarios. Assert that directoryContains returns false when checking if directory1 contains file2, verifying that a file in a sibling directory is not considered contained. Assert that directoryContains returns false when checking if directory2 contains file1, confirming the reverse sibling directory scenario also returns false. Assert that directoryContains returns false when checking if directory1 contains file3, validating that a file in the parent directory is not considered contained within a subdirectory. Assert that directoryContains returns false when checking if directory2 contains file3, ensuring consistent behavior across different subdirectories when checking for parent directory files. The test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the file moving functionality by ensuring that a file can be successfully relocated from one path to another with replacement behavior. Create two temporary files using predefined naming patterns, then execute a move operation that transfers the first file to the location of the second file while enabling replacement of the existing target file. Verify that the move operation returns the correct destination path by asserting that the returned path matches the target location. Clean up the moved file by deleting it from the destination location, and ensure that any test fixtures are properly removed both before and after the test execution. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the file movement functionality of an unchecked file operations utility. Initialize two temporary files using a file prefix and suffix configuration, creating source and destination file paths in the filesystem. Execute the file move operation by calling the utility's move method with the source file, destination file, and a replace existing copy option to handle potential conflicts. Assert that the move operation returns the destination path as expected, confirming the file was successfully relocated. Clean up the test environment by deleting the moved file to restore the filesystem state, and perform additional cleanup of any remaining test fixtures including file paths, directory paths, and symbolic links. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the file moving functionality of the FilesUncheck utility class, specifically testing that the move method correctly relocates a file from one path to another and returns the target path. Initialize the test by calling the deleteFixtures method which removes any existing files at NEW_FILE_PATH, NEW_DIR_PATH, and NEW_FILE_PATH_LINK using Files.deleteIfExists to ensure a clean test environment. Create two temporary files by calling FilesUncheck.createTempFile twice, passing the PREFIX and SUFFIX fields from the test class as parameters to generate unique temporary file paths. Execute the core functionality by calling FilesUncheck.move with the first temporary file as the source, the second temporary file as the target, and StandardCopyOption.REPLACE_EXISTING as the copy option to allow overwriting the target file. Assert that the move method returns the target path by using assertEquals to compare the returned value with the second temporary file path, validating that the move operation completed successfully and returned the correct destination path. Clean up the test environment by calling FilesUncheck.delete on the target file to remove the moved file, then execute the deleteFixtures teardown method again to ensure all test artifacts are removed. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that file modification time retrieval functionality works correctly when provided with a URI reference to an existing file location. Obtain the current working directory path and convert it to a URI format, then invoke the path utility functionality to retrieve the last modified timestamp for that URI location. Assert that the returned modification time value is not null, confirming that the utility can successfully extract temporal metadata from URI-based file references. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the file utilities component correctly rejects attempts to delete a directory when given a file path instead. Initialize two test files within a temporary directory structure, generating test data content for each file using buffered output streams, then clean and recreate the directory structure to ensure a fresh state with the test files properly established. Call the directory deletion method with one of the test file paths as the argument, which should represent a file rather than a directory. Assert that an IllegalArgumentException is thrown when the deletion method encounters a file path where it expects a directory path, confirming that the utility properly validates input types and prevents incorrect file system operations. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates the file utility's directory containment checking functionality by verifying that directories correctly report when they do not contain specific files. Initialize a temporary directory structure with multiple nested directories and several files distributed across different locations, including files placed in sibling directories and at the root level. Create the directory hierarchy by establishing parent and child directory relationships, then generate individual files within various directories to create a mixed file system layout. Call the directory containment utility method multiple times with different directory and file combinations where the files are intentionally located outside the specified directories. Assert that each containment check returns false, confirming that the utility correctly identifies when a directory does not contain a given file, including cases where files exist in sibling directories or at different hierarchy levels. The testing framework used is JUnit 5.

This test validates that the PathUtils utility can successfully retrieve the last modified time for a file system path when provided as a URI, ensuring the file time retrieval functionality works correctly with URI-based path representations. The test calls a helper method current which internally invokes PathUtils.current to obtain the current working directory as a Path object, then converts this Path to a URI using the toUri method and passes it to PathUtils.getLastModifiedFileTime to retrieve the file's last modification timestamp. The test asserts that the returned file time is not null using assertNotNull, validating that the getLastModifiedFileTime method successfully processes the URI parameter and returns a valid timestamp object rather than failing or returning null. This test is annotated with @Test and uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a writer splitter can handle null constructor arguments gracefully without throwing exceptions. Initialize a writer splitter using a null array of writers within a try-with-resources block, then call methods to append a character and flush the output to verify the splitter operates without errors. Next, initialize another writer splitter using a null collection of writers within a separate try-with-resources block, and again call methods to append a character and flush to ensure proper handling. Finally, assert that the test completed successfully to confirm both null constructor scenarios were handled appropriately. The testing framework used is JUnit.

This test validates the path utility's ability to retrieve last modified time information from a URI representation of a file system path. Initialize the test by obtaining the current working directory path through the path utility, then convert this path to its URI representation. Call the path utility's method to get the last modified file time using the URI as input, and assert that the returned file time object is not null to verify that the utility successfully retrieves temporal metadata from URI-based file references. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that TeeWriter constructors handle null input parameters gracefully without throwing exceptions. Initialize a TeeWriter instance using the constructor that accepts a Writer array parameter, passing null as the argument, and wrap it in a try-with-resources block to ensure proper resource management. Call the append method on the writer instance with a character value like 'a', then invoke the flush method to complete the write operations. Repeat this process by creating another TeeWriter instance using the constructor that accepts a Collection of Writer objects, again passing null as the parameter, and perform the same append and flush operations within a try-with-resources block. Assert that the test execution completes successfully with a boolean true value to confirm that no exceptions were thrown during the null parameter handling. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the file content comparison functionality by exercising the PathUtils fileContentEquals method across various file states and edge cases, using assertions to verify correct equality detection and exception handling for invalid inputs. Initialize two Path objects by creating File instances within the temporaryFolder field (a File type field of the test class annotated with TempDir) using getName method results, then assert that fileContentEquals returns true when both parameters are null, and use the assertFileContentNotEquals helper method to verify inequality when comparing a path with null, which internally calls fileContentEquals with both parameter orders and asserts false for the null comparison while asserting true for self-comparisons. Assert that fileContentEquals returns true when comparing two non-existent file paths, then verify that comparing directory paths throws an IOException using assertThrows. Create three distinct file paths within the temporary folder using Paths get method with getName-derived filenames, copy class resources from java.lang.Object.class to two of these paths and java.util.Collection.class to the third using PathUtils copyFile method, then assert that fileContentEquals returns false when comparing files with different content and true when comparing files with identical content or the same file with itself. Create two empty files using Files createFile method and use the assertFileContentEquals helper method to validate equality, which internally verifies that fileContentEquals returns true for all permutations of the two paths including self-comparisons. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the Test annotation and assertion methods.

This test validates that the FileUtils deleteDirectory method correctly rejects attempts to delete a directory when given a file path instead of a directory path, ensuring proper input validation and error handling. The test specifically verifies that an IllegalArgumentException is thrown when the deleteDirectory method is called with a file parameter, confirming that the method enforces the distinction between files and directories in its API contract. Initialize the test environment by setting up two File objects as fields of the test class: testFile1 pointing to "file1-test.txt" and testFile2 pointing to "file1a-test.txt", both located within a temporary directory represented by the tempDirFile field. Store the initial file sizes in testFile1Size and testFile2Size fields of type long. In the setUp method, verify that the parent directories exist for both test files, and if not, fail the test with an appropriate error message. Create both test files by opening BufferedOutputStream instances wrapping Files.newOutputStream for each file's path, then populate them with test data using TestUtils.generateTestData, passing the output stream and corresponding file size. Delete the entire temporary directory using FileUtils.deleteDirectory, recreate it with mkdirs, then regenerate both test files with the same process of verifying parent directory existence, creating output streams, and populating with test data using TestUtils.generateTestData. Execute the core test behavior by calling FileUtils.deleteDirectory with testFile1 as the argument, which represents a file rather than a directory. Assert that this method call throws an IllegalArgumentException using assertThrows, validating that the deleteDirectory method properly rejects file inputs and enforces that only directory paths are acceptable parameters. The test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that TeeWriter constructors handle null input gracefully without throwing exceptions when subsequently used for basic writing operations. Initialize a TeeWriter instance using the constructor that accepts a Writer array parameter, passing null as the argument, and wrap this initialization in a try-with-resources block to ensure proper resource management. Within the first try block, call the append method on the TeeWriter instance with the character 'a' as the argument, then invoke the flush method to complete the writing operations. Create a second TeeWriter instance using the constructor that accepts a Collection of Writer objects, again passing null as the parameter, and wrap this in another try-with-resources block. Within the second try block, repeat the same operations by calling append with character 'a' followed by flush to verify that both constructor variants handle null inputs without throwing exceptions. After both try-with-resources blocks complete successfully, assert that true equals true with the message "Dummy to show test completed OK" to confirm the test executed without any exceptions being thrown. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

This test validates that directory deletion functionality properly rejects attempts to delete a file when a directory is expected. Initialize a test environment with a temporary directory structure and create two test files with generated content, ensuring the parent directories exist and are properly set up. Clean the temporary directory and recreate the test files to establish a known state. Attempt to delete a directory by passing a file reference instead of a directory reference, and assert that this operation throws an illegal argument exception to confirm the validation logic correctly identifies and rejects inappropriate input types. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates the behavior of a symbolic link file filter when processing a regular directory that is not a symbolic link. Initialize a symbolic link file filter instance, along with temporary files and directories including target files, symbolic links to files, target directories, symbolic links to directories, and missing file references, using platform-specific symbolic link creation strategies that mock symbolic links on Windows systems due to privilege requirements and create real symbolic links on other operating systems. Call the filter's accept method with the target directory path and a null attributes parameter, then assert that it returns a TERMINATE file visit result. Subsequently, call the filter's matches method with the same target directory path and assert that it returns false, confirming that regular directories are not considered symbolic links by the filter. After test execution, clean up the created temporary files and directories by deleting the symbolic link directories, target directories, symbolic link files, and target files. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a symbolic link file filter correctly handles regular directories by rejecting them as non-symbolic links. Initialize a test environment with a symbolic link filter that can distinguish between symbolic links and regular filesystem entries, along with temporary files, directories, and symbolic links for both files and directories, using platform-appropriate symbolic link creation mechanisms that mock symbolic links on Windows systems due to privilege requirements. Create a regular directory within the test filesystem structure. Apply the filter's acceptance method to the regular directory path and assert that it returns a termination result, then verify that the filter's matching capability correctly identifies the regular directory as not being a symbolic link by asserting false for the match result. Clean up all created test files and directories after validation. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates directory deletion functionality with a single file of size 1 byte using forced deletion mode. Initialize a temporary directory path and copy a binary test file from the test resources directory into the temporary location, specifically a file named with a size indicator. Execute the path deletion utility on the resolved file path within the temporary directory and assert that the deletion operation returns expected counts of zero, one, and one for the respective metrics tracked by the deletion process. The test uses JUnit as the testing framework.

This test validates that file moving functionality works correctly when the standard rename operation fails and must fall back to a copy-and-delete strategy. Initialize a temporary directory structure with test files containing generated data of predetermined sizes, then clean and recreate the directory to ensure a fresh state for testing. Create a destination file path within the temporary directory and construct a specialized source file reference that deliberately overrides the rename behavior to always return false, simulating a scenario where the source and destination are on different filesystems or the rename operation is otherwise blocked. Execute the file move operation using the utility method, which should detect the failed rename and automatically perform a copy-and-delete sequence instead. Assert that the destination file exists after the operation completes and verify that the original source file has been properly removed, confirming that the fallback mechanism successfully transferred the file content and cleaned up the source. This test uses JUnit framework for test execution and assertions.

This test validates that the SymbolicLinkFileFilter correctly identifies and rejects regular directories that are not symbolic links when used in file tree traversal scenarios. The test exercises the filter's accept and matches methods on a real directory path, asserting that the filter returns TERMINATE for file visitor operations and false for path matching to confirm proper filtering behavior. Initialize the test environment by setting up a SymbolicLinkFileFilter instance stored in the filter field of the test class, which is either a real SymbolicLinkFileFilter.INSTANCE on non-Windows systems or a mock filter created by the createMockFilter helper method on Windows systems that overrides the isSymbolicLink method to return true only for paths containing "Link" in their string representation. Create a temporary target file using File.createTempFile with TARGET_SHORT_NAME and TARGET_EXT constants, then establish its parent directory and create a real directory using Files.createDirectories with the DIRECTORY_NAME constant, storing the resulting directory path in the targetDirPath field of the test class. Call the filter's accept method with the targetDirPath and null as the second parameter, then assert using assertEquals that the result equals FileVisitResult.TERMINATE to verify the filter properly terminates traversal for non-symbolic-link directories. Invoke the filter's matches method with the targetDirPath parameter and assert using assertFalse that the result is false to confirm the filter correctly identifies the regular directory as not matching the symbolic link criteria. Clean up resources in teardown by calling delete on testLinkDirFile, targetDirFile, testLinkFile, and testTargetFile to remove all created files and directories. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the line feed retention behavior of a Windows line ending input stream when reading byte-by-byte. Initialize a helper method that creates a Windows line ending input stream from a character sequence input stream built with UTF-8 encoding, configured with a retention flag set to false. Call the helper method twice with different string inputs: first with a string containing carriage return and line feed sequences like "a\r\n\r\n", and second with a simple single character string like "a". Within the helper method, create a byte buffer and read individual bytes from the stream until end-of-stream is reached, then convert the accumulated bytes back to a UTF-8 string. Assert that the first call returns the original string with line feeds preserved, and assert that the second call returns the single character unchanged. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the file moving functionality when the standard rename operation fails and the system must fall back to a copy-and-delete strategy, specifically testing the FileUtils moveFile method's ability to handle cross-filesystem scenarios and ensuring proper file transfer with cleanup of the original source file. Initialize a File destination object within the temporary directory field tempDirFile with the filename "move2.txt", then create an anonymous File subclass extending from the testFile1 field's absolute path that overrides the renameTo method to always return false, simulating a failed rename operation that would occur when moving files across different filesystems. Call the FileUtils moveFile method with the anonymous source File and the destination File to trigger the copy-and-delete fallback mechanism when the initial rename attempt fails. Assert that the destination file exists using assertTrue with the message "Check Exist" to verify the file was successfully copied to the target location, then assert that the source file no longer exists using assertFalse with the message "Original deleted" to confirm the original file was properly removed after the successful copy operation. The test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that the file utilities component properly handles IO exceptions when attempting to read lines from a file with restricted permissions on POSIX file systems. Initialize a temporary directory structure and create two test files with generated test data during setup, then clean and recreate the directory with fresh test files. Create a new test file within the temporary directory using utility methods and populate it with 100 bytes of test data. Set the file's POSIX permissions to completely restrict all access using an empty permission string. Attempt to read lines from the restricted file using the file utilities read lines method and assert that an IOException is thrown due to the permission restrictions. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework with conditional execution based on POSIX file permission support.

This test validates that the WindowsLineEndingInputStream correctly preserves line feed characters when processing byte-by-byte input, specifically testing the stream's ability to retain carriage return and line feed sequences without modification. The test exercises the WindowsLineEndingInputStream class through a helper method that simulates reading individual bytes from the stream and verifies that the output matches the original input exactly. Initialize the test by calling the helper method roundtripReadByte twice with different input strings and a false boolean parameter, where the first call uses the string "a

" containing carriage return and line feed sequences, and the second call uses the simple string "a" without any line ending characters. The helper method creates a WindowsLineEndingInputStream wrapping a CharSequenceInputStream that is built from the input string using UTF-8 encoding, then reads the stream byte-by-byte using the read method in a loop until end-of-stream is reached, collecting each byte into a buffer array of size 100. Assert that the first roundtripReadByte call returns exactly "a

" using assertEquals, validating that the carriage return and line feed sequences are preserved unchanged. Assert that the second roundtripReadByte call returns exactly "a" using assertEquals, confirming that simple strings without line endings pass through unmodified. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation and assertEquals assertion method.

This test validates that character sequence appending with index boundaries works correctly for appendable output handling. Initialize an appendable wrapper around a string-based writer and configure it during setup along with an exception instance and a broken writer scenario for comprehensive testing coverage. Call the append functionality twice in sequence, each time providing a single character string with start and end index boundaries to extract just the first character, then chain the operations together to build a combined result. Assert that the final output contains the expected concatenated characters, confirming that indexed character sequence appending operates correctly and produces the proper accumulated string content. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the file utility's move operation when the underlying rename operation fails and must fall back to a copy-and-delete strategy. Initialize a temporary directory structure and create two test files with generated test data, storing their sizes for later reference. Set up a source file object that overrides the rename method to always return false, simulating a scenario where the file cannot be renamed directly such as when moving across different filesystems. Create a destination file path within the temporary directory. Execute the file move operation using the file utility, passing the specially configured source file and the destination path. Assert that the destination file exists after the move operation completes, then verify that the original source file no longer exists, confirming that the copy-and-delete fallback mechanism worked correctly when the direct rename approach failed. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates the indexed character sequence appending functionality of the UncheckedAppendable wrapper class, specifically testing that multiple chained append operations with start and end indices correctly concatenate character sequences and produce the expected output string. Initialize a private IOException field with the message "test exception", create a private UncheckedAppendable field wrapping a BrokenWriter instance constructed with the exception, and establish another private UncheckedAppendable field wrapping a StringWriter instance during setup. Execute the test by calling the append method on the UncheckedAppendable instance backed by StringWriter, passing the character sequence "a" with start index 0 and end index 1, then immediately chain another append call with character sequence "b" using the same indices 0 and 1. Assert that the toString method on the UncheckedAppendable instance returns exactly "ab", validating that the indexed append operations correctly extracted and concatenated the first character from each input sequence. The test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that the FileUtils readLines method properly throws an IOException when attempting to read from a file with no read permissions on POSIX-compliant file systems, ensuring robust error handling for permission-denied scenarios. The test is annotated with @Test and @EnabledIf with the condition "isPosixFilePermissionsSupported" to ensure it only runs on systems that support POSIX file permissions. Initialize a new File object using the TestUtils newFile method with the tempDirFile field of type File from the test class and the filename "cant-read.txt". Create the file with 100 bytes of content by calling TestUtils createFile method with the file object and the size value 100. Remove all file permissions by calling Files setPosixFilePermissions method on the file's path, passing PosixFilePermissions fromString method with the string "---------" which represents no read, write, or execute permissions for owner, group, or others. Assert that an IOException is thrown when calling FileUtils readLines method with the file object by using assertThrows with IOException class as the expected exception type. The testing framework used is JUnit 5, as evidenced by the @Test annotation and assertThrows method.

This test validates that file reading operations properly handle permission-denied scenarios on POSIX file systems by throwing appropriate exceptions when access is restricted. Initialize a temporary directory environment with test files and their associated size tracking. Create a new file within the temporary directory and populate it with a small amount of test data. Remove all read, write, and execute permissions from the file using POSIX permission settings to simulate an inaccessible file scenario. Attempt to read the lines from the permission-restricted file and assert that an IO exception is thrown due to the access denial. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework with conditional execution based on POSIX file permission support.

This test validates the ability to read the complete contents of a file and convert it to a string representation. Initialize a temporary directory and create a test file within it, then populate the file with generated test data of a predetermined size using a buffered output stream, while also preparing byte and character arrays filled with test data patterns. Clear any thread-local storage to ensure a clean testing environment. Open the test file using a buffered reader and pass it to a utility method that converts the entire reader contents into a string format. Assert that the resulting string is not null and verify that the length of the converted string exactly matches the original file size to confirm complete and accurate data conversion. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates XML writer encoding behavior when no explicit encoding is specified but various default encodings are provided. Initialize a test using predefined Unicode text content and call the XML writer validation helper method five times with different parameter combinations: first with no encoding and no default encoding specified, then with no encoding but with UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-16BE, and ISO-8859-1 as default encodings respectively. The helper method creates XML content using the provided text and encoding parameters, determines the effective encoding by defaulting to UTF-8 when both encoding and default encoding are null or using the specified default encoding when the primary encoding is null, then validates that the generated XML content matches the expected encoding behavior. Assert that the XML writer correctly handles encoding defaults and produces properly encoded output for each scenario. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the indexed character sequence appending functionality of an unchecked appendable wrapper. Initialize an IO exception with a test message, create a broken unchecked appendable wrapping a broken writer that will throw the exception, and create a string-based unchecked appendable wrapping a string writer for successful operations. Call the indexed append method on the string appendable twice, first appending a single character from index 0 to 1 of one character sequence, then chaining another indexed append of a different single character from the same index range. Assert that the resulting string representation of the appendable contains the concatenated characters from both append operations. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the functionality of reading a file through a Reader and converting its contents to a String using IOUtils utility methods. The test specifically exercises the IOUtils toString method with a Reader input to ensure it correctly reads file content and returns it as a String with proper size validation. Initialize the test environment by setting up a temporary directory using the temporaryFolder field of type File annotated with TempDir, then create a test file named "file2-test.txt" within this directory and populate it with test data of size FILE_SIZE using TestUtils generateTestData method through a BufferedOutputStream. Additionally, initialize two arrays: a byte array of size 200 filled with -1 values except for the first 80 elements which are set to their index values, and a char array with the same configuration. Before executing the test, call the beforeAll method which invokes IO clear to exercise thread local recycling without adverse side effects. In the test method annotated with Test, create a BufferedReader from the test file path using Files newBufferedReader, then pass this Reader to IOUtils toString method to convert the file contents into a String. Assert that the returned String is not null using assertNotNull, and verify that the String length equals FILE_SIZE using assertEquals with the message "Wrong output size" to ensure the complete file content was properly read and converted. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation and assertion methods.

This test validates that checksum calculation properly handles null checksum algorithm inputs by throwing an appropriate error. Initialize a temporary directory structure with test files containing generated data of predetermined sizes, then clean and recreate the directory with fresh test files. Create a new test file within the temporary directory and write a sample text string to it using ASCII encoding. Attempt to calculate a checksum of the file by passing a null checksum algorithm parameter, and assert that this operation throws a null pointer exception to ensure proper input validation. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the reset functionality properly converts checked exceptions to unchecked exceptions when the underlying reader encounters an error. Initialize a buffered reader wrapper that converts checked IO exceptions to unchecked ones, using a reader that will throw an exception when reset is attempted. Create the reader wrapper using a builder pattern with the problematic reader as the underlying source. Within a try-with-resources block, create another reader wrapper using a closed reader instance, then explicitly close it. Call the reset method on the exception-throwing reader and assert that it throws an unchecked IO exception rather than the original checked exception. The test framework used is JUnit 5.

This test validates that line feed characters are properly retained when processing text input through a byte-reading stream mechanism. Initialize a helper that processes text containing carriage return and line feed sequences by creating a specialized input stream that handles Windows-style line endings, then read the content byte-by-byte into a buffer and convert it back to a string representation. Execute this process twice: first with text containing multiple carriage return and line feed combinations, and second with simple text without line endings. Assert that the output exactly matches the original input in both cases, confirming that line feed characters are preserved during the byte-level reading operation. The testing uses JUnit framework.

This test validates the default encoding behavior of XML writing functionality when no explicit encoding is specified, ensuring that various character encodings are properly handled and applied as defaults. The test exercises XML writer components by testing encoding resolution logic with different standard character sets and verifies that the correct effective encoding is used through assertion mechanisms. Initialize the test by accessing the TEXT_UNICODE field which is a String type field of the test class containing Unicode text content. Execute a helper method five times with different parameter combinations, first calling it with the Unicode text, null for encoding, and null for default encoding, then subsequently with the same text and null encoding but specifying UTF_8, UTF_16, UTF_16BE, and ISO_8859_1 standard charset names as default encodings respectively. The helper method creates XML content using the createXmlContent method with the provided text and encoding parameters, determines the effective encoding by defaulting to UTF_8 when both encoding and default encoding are null or using the specified default encoding when encoding is null, then validates the XML content through the checkXmlContent method using the generated XML, effective encoding, and default encoding parameters. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that XML writing functionality correctly handles default encoding behavior when no explicit encoding is specified. Initialize the test by utilizing predefined Unicode text content from the test class fields. Execute the XML writer validation process multiple times, first with no encoding parameters specified, then with various standard character encodings including UTF-8, UTF-16, UTF-16BE, and ISO-8859-1 as default encoding options while keeping the primary encoding parameter null. For each validation iteration, generate XML content using the Unicode text and encoding configuration, determine the effective encoding by defaulting to UTF-8 when no encoding is provided or using the specified default encoding otherwise, and verify that the resulting XML content matches the expected encoding behavior. Assert that the XML writer properly applies encoding defaults and produces correctly encoded output across all tested character set scenarios. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the checksum utility's error handling when provided with a null checksum algorithm parameter. Initialize a temporary directory structure and create two test files with generated data content, ensuring the parent directories exist before file creation and recreating the directory structure after cleanup. Create a new test file within the temporary directory and write a sample text string containing an Einstein quote to it using ASCII encoding. Call the file utility's checksum method with the created file and a null checksum algorithm parameter, then assert that a NullPointerException is thrown to verify proper null parameter validation. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates that the UncheckedBufferedReader properly converts checked IOExceptions to UncheckedIOExceptions when the reset method fails on a closed or broken reader. Initialize an UncheckedBufferedReader using the builder pattern with a ClosedReader INSTANCE field as the underlying reader within a try-with-resources block, then immediately call the close method on this reader to ensure it is in a closed state. Next, call the assertThrows method to verify that invoking the reset method on the ucBrokenReader field (which was configured in the setup with a BrokenReader that throws an IOException with the message "test exception") throws an UncheckedIOException, confirming that the UncheckedBufferedReader's reset method properly wraps the underlying IOException in an UncheckedIOException as intended by its design to provide unchecked exception handling for buffered reader operations. The test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the IOUtils utility's ability to convert a Reader into a String representation. This test validates the append functionality of a file writer with encoding when working with an existing file that already contains content. This test validates the file utility's ability to list both files and directories within a nested directory structure using wildcard filters. This test validates the file listing functionality of a file utilities component to ensure it returns only files and excludes directories when filtering directory contents. Call the FileUtils listFilesAndDirs method with subDir1 as the starting directory, using WildcardFileFilter builders to create filters where the first filter matches files with any extension using the wildcard pattern *.* and the second filter matches any directory using the wildcard pattern *, storing the returned Collection of File objects. Assert that subDir2 is present in the collection using assertTrue with the message "Should contain the directory." to confirm nested directories are found. Validate that the text file someFile appears in the collection using assertTrue with the message "Should contain the file." to verify files matching the pattern are included. Finally, assert that subDir3 exists in the collection using assertTrue with the message "Should contain the directory." to ensure all subdirectories are properly detected. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the file writing functionality when the append option is disabled, ensuring that existing file content is completely overwritten rather than appended to. This test validates that a checksum input stream throws an IOException when attempting to read beyond its configured threshold. Initialize a CRC32 checksum instance and create a byte array of 9 elements, then construct a checksum input stream using the builder pattern with the byte array as the data source, the CRC32 instance as the checksum calculator, an expected checksum value of 1, and a count threshold of 1 byte. After the exception, assert that the byte count has incremented to 1 and the remaining bytes is now 0, confirming the stream properly tracks consumption even when throwing the threshold violation exception. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates the file listing functionality to ensure that only files (not directories) are returned when filtering directory contents. Initialize a File object representing the temporary directory from the test class field tempDirFile, then create a subdirectory named "TEST" within this directory using the mkdir method and assert that the directory creation succeeds with assertTrue. This test validates that a checksum-enabled input stream properly throws an exception when attempting to read beyond its configured threshold. This test validates the file writing utility's behavior when the append option is disabled, ensuring that existing file content is completely replaced rather than appended to. This test validates that a ChecksumInputStream throws an IOException when attempting to read from a stream that has reached its count threshold, specifically testing the scenario where the checksum verification fails after the threshold is exceeded. Initialize a CRC32 checksum instance and create a byte array of length 9, then construct a ChecksumInputStream using the builder pattern by calling builder on the ChecksumInputStream class, setting the byte array as the input source with setByteArray, configuring the checksum with setChecksum using the CRC32 instance, setting the expected checksum value to 1 using setExpectedChecksumValue with a byte cast, establishing a count threshold of 1 with setCountThreshold, and obtaining the configured stream with get. Within a try-with-resources block, first assert that getByteCount returns 0 to verify the initial state, then assert that getRemaining returns 1 to confirm one byte remains to be read before the threshold. Call the read method with no arguments and use assertThrows to verify it throws an IOException, which occurs because the afterRead method detects that the byte count has reached the threshold of 1 and the actual checksum value does not match the expected value of 1, triggering the checksum verification failure. After the exception, assert that getByteCount now returns 1 to confirm the byte was counted, and assert that getRemaining returns 0 to verify no bytes remain within the threshold. The testing framework used is JUnit 5, identified by the Test annotation and assertThrows method.

This test validates the force deletion capability for read-only directories on macOS systems. Execute a force deletion operation on the read-only directory and assert that the nested file, parent directory, and temporary directory wrapper are all successfully removed and no longer exist. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates that a file writer with encoding can be constructed using a charset encoder and produces the same output as a standard file writer. This test validates the force deletion functionality for read-only directories on macOS systems, specifically testing that the FileUtils forceDelete method can successfully remove directories and files even when they have read-only permissions set. Convert the destination file to a File object, set it to read-only using setReadOnly, then assert that the file can be read but cannot be written using canRead and canWrite respectively. Call the delete method on the directory and capture the returned PathCounters object, then assert that the directory counter equals 1 and the file counter equals 1, followed by asserting that both the file and directory no longer exist using exists. In the second block, repeat the initial sanity checks for directory structure and parent-child relationship, but this time convert the directory to a File object and set the directory itself to read-only. Assert that the directory can be read but cannot be written, then verify it exists before deletion. Call FileUtils.forceDelete on the directory object to perform the actual force deletion operation being tested, then assert that the destination file, directory file object, and TempDirectory all no longer exist using exists. The test method is annotated with @Test and @EnabledOnOs with value OS.MAC, indicating it only runs on macOS systems, and uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates that a file writer with encoding can be constructed using both direct constructor and builder pattern approaches while maintaining consistent encoding behavior. This test validates the force deletion functionality for read-only directories on macOS systems using temporary file system resources. This test validates that file writing operations produce identical results when using the same default character encoding through both direct constructor instantiation and builder pattern approaches. This test validates that FileWriterWithEncoding can be constructed using both direct constructor and builder pattern approaches with string file paths and Charset objects, ensuring consistent encoding behavior across different instantiation methods. This test validates the string-to-writer copy functionality of a utility class by setting up a temporary file system environment and exercising file-based string copying operations. This test validates the available method functionality of UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream, ensuring it correctly reports the number of bytes available for reading and throws an IOException when called on a closed stream. Initialize the test by creating a temporary file using Files.createTempFile with the test class simple name and a .tst extension, write the DATA constant bytes to this file using UTF-8 encoding, create a FileInputStream from the temporary file, and construct an UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream using the builder helper method which returns a new UnsynchronizedBufferedInputStream.Builder instance, setting the input stream to the file input stream and calling get to build the buffered input stream. This test validates the force deletion functionality for unwritable directories containing files on macOS systems, specifically testing that the FileUtils forceDelete method can successfully remove directories even when their write permissions have been disabled. This test validates the byte order mark input stream's ability to detect and handle UTF-8 BOMs when the BOM is queried before reading stream content. Initialize a file tailer with a 50 millisecond delay duration and configure it to not ignore file touch events, then create an empty test file and start the tailer in a separate thread with a test listener that captures file content. This test validates the user experience of copying a directory structure to a non-existing destination location. This test validates that appending lines to an existing file preserves the original content while adding new lines. This test validates the functionality of reading a Byte Order Mark (BOM) from an input stream before consuming the actual data content. Initialize a byte array containing the ASCII characters 'A', 'B', and 'C' as the base data content. Use a helper method createUtf8Input to construct an InputStream that prepends the UTF-8 BOM bytes (0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF) to the base data by creating a new byte array with the BOM bytes at the beginning followed by the original data, then wrapping it in a ByteArrayInputStream. Create a BOMInputStream using the builder pattern by calling BOMInputStream.builder().setInputStream() with the UTF-8 input stream and invoking get() to construct the instance. Call hasBOM() and assert it returns true using assertTrue with the message "hasBOM()" to confirm a BOM is present. Call hasBOM() with ByteOrderMark.UTF_8 as a parameter and assert it returns true using assertTrue with the message "hasBOM(UTF-8)" to verify the specific UTF-8 BOM is detected. Sequentially call read() four times on the BOMInputStream, asserting that the first three calls return the integer values 65, 66, and 67 (corresponding to 'A', 'B', 'C') using assertEquals, and the fourth call returns -1 using assertEquals to indicate end of stream. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that EndianUtils methods properly reject invalid byte array operations by throwing IllegalArgumentException when attempting to read from or write to an empty byte array. Initialize an empty byte array with zero length to represent an invalid buffer state that cannot accommodate any data operations. Use assertThrows to verify that IllegalArgumentException is thrown when calling readSwappedInteger with the empty byte array and offset zero, confirming the method properly validates buffer capacity before attempting to read a 4-byte integer. Verify that readSwappedShort throws IllegalArgumentException with the empty array and zero offset, ensuring 2-byte short read operations are properly rejected. Assert that readSwappedUnsignedInteger throws IllegalArgumentException when attempting to read an unsigned integer from the empty array at offset zero, confirming proper validation of unsigned integer operations. Verify that readSwappedUnsignedShort throws IllegalArgumentException when called with the empty array and zero offset, ensuring unsigned short read operations are rejected on insufficient buffer capacity. Assert that writeSwappedInteger throws IllegalArgumentException when attempting to write integer value zero to the empty array at offset zero, validating that write operations properly check buffer capacity. Verify that writeSwappedLong throws IllegalArgumentException when attempting to write long value zero to the empty array at offset zero, ensuring long write operations are rejected on insufficient buffer space. Assert that writeSwappedShort throws IllegalArgumentException when attempting to write short value zero to the empty array at offset zero, confirming that short write operations properly validate buffer capacity before execution. The testing framework used is JUnit 5, identified by the Test annotation and assertThrows method.

This test validates the behavior of a byte order mark input stream when reading data that does not contain a BOM prefix. This test validates the file writing utility's ability to append lines to an existing file without overwriting previous content. Read the entire file content back as a string and assert that the actual file contents exactly match the expected concatenated result, verifying that both the original content and newly appended lines are present in the correct order. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that file writing functionality works correctly when no character encoding is explicitly specified, allowing the system to use default encoding behavior. This test validates the functionality of reading from a BOMInputStream when no Byte Order Mark is present in the input data. This test validates the file line appending functionality where new content is added to an existing file without overwriting the original content. The test specifically examines the FileUtils writeLines method with append mode enabled and verifies through string comparison that both original and new content are preserved in the correct format. Initialize a new File object using the TestUtils newFile method with the tempDirFile test class field of type File and the filename "lines.txt", then write an initial string "This line was there before you..." to this file using the FileUtils writeStringToFile method. Create a List of String objects containing two elements: "my first line" and "The second Line" using the Arrays asList method. Call the FileUtils writeLines method with five arguments: the file object, null for encoding, the list of lines to append, null for line ending, and true to enable append mode, which programmatically adds the provided lines to the end of the existing file content while preserving the original text. This test validates the behavior of FileWriterWithEncoding when null CharsetEncoder values are provided through different construction methods, ensuring that the writer defaults to the system's default encoding and produces identical output to a standard FileWriter. Initialize a temporary folder with two test files named testfile1.txt and testfile2.txt, and create a 1024-character string containing repeating patterns of "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQabcdefgihklmnopq" as test content. Create three FileWriterWithEncoding instances sequentially: first using the direct constructor with the file path and a null CharsetEncoder cast, second using the builder pattern with setFile method and default settings, and third using the builder with setFile and explicitly setting a null CharsetEncoder via setCharsetEncoder. For each FileWriterWithEncoding instance, call the helper method successfulRun which creates a standard FileWriter for the first test file and uses the provided FileWriterWithEncoding for the second test file, writes the test payload to both files using writeTestPayload, compares the files using checkFile to ensure identical content, and asserts that both files exist using assertTrue. This test validates that a Tailer correctly re-reads file content when the file's timestamp is updated without content changes, specifically testing the touch file operation behavior when ignoreTouch is set to false. Initialize a delay duration of 50 milliseconds and create a File object named tailer1-testReissueOnTouch.txt within the temporaryFolder, then call the helper method createFile to generate an empty file with zero bytes, which creates the file using BufferedOutputStream, writes test data via TestUtils.generateTestData, and verifies the file exists with the correct size. Create a TestTailerListener instance to capture file events and lines, then build a Tailer using the builder pattern with setFile specifying the created file, setTailerListener providing the listener, setDelayDuration set to Duration.ofMillis with the delay value, setStartThread configured to false for manual thread control, and setIgnoreTouch set to false to enable re-reading on timestamp changes. This test validates the file writer with encoding component's behavior when constructed with null charset encoder parameters through multiple instantiation approaches. Create three separate file writer instances using different construction methods: first, instantiate a file writer with encoding by passing a file path and an explicitly null charset encoder parameter; second, use the builder pattern to create a writer with just the file path set; and third, use the builder pattern again but explicitly set the charset encoder to null before building. For each writer instance, execute a successful run operation that writes the prepared test content to the target file, creates a standard file writer for comparison purposes, writes the same content to both files, and verifies that both files exist and contain identical content. Assert that the files are successfully created and contain the expected data after each writer operation completes. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the byte array reading functionality with bounds checking for a random access file input stream. Initialize a random access file input stream using a builder pattern, configuring it with a random access file created in read-only mode from a data file and setting the close-on-close behavior to true. Create a byte buffer with a length of 12 bytes to hold the data to be read. Call the read method on the input stream with the buffer, starting offset of zero, and the buffer length, then assert that the number of bytes read equals the expected data length of 12. Finally, assert that the available long method returns the correct remaining bytes in the file by comparing it to the total data file length minus the bytes already read. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a queue-based input stream can properly handle bulk read operations when data is not immediately available and must wait for incoming data. Initialize a custom blocking queue that uses countdown latches to coordinate timing between read and write operations, ensuring the queue will block on polling until data becomes available. Create a queue input stream with an extended timeout duration and obtain its corresponding output stream. Execute the read operation asynchronously by launching a background task that waits for the input stream to begin polling, then writes test data to the output stream and signals completion. Perform a bulk read operation on the input stream using a byte array buffer, which should block until the background write operation provides the data. Assert that the number of bytes read matches the expected input length and that the reconstructed string content matches the original test data exactly. Verify that the asynchronous write operation completes without throwing any exceptions. The validation spans multiple inputs through parameterization. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates the boundary-checking functionality of reading byte arrays from a RandomAccessFileInputStream, specifically testing that the stream correctly reads a specified number of bytes into a buffer and accurately tracks remaining available bytes. Initialize a RandomAccessFileInputStream using the builder pattern by calling the builder method, then invoke the setRandomAccessFile method with the result of calling the createRandomAccessFile helper method which creates a RandomAccessFile in READ_ONLY mode using the DATA_FILE_NAME constant, followed by calling setCloseOnClose with true to ensure the underlying file closes when the stream closes, and finally call get to construct the stream instance within a try-with-resources block. This test validates that reading data from a file-based input stream with specified buffer bounds correctly retrieves the expected content and accurately reports remaining available data. Initialize a specialized input stream that wraps a file opened in read-only mode, configuring it to automatically close the underlying file when the stream is closed. Create a byte buffer with a length matching the expected data size, then read data from the stream into this buffer using the bounded read operation that specifies the starting offset and number of bytes to read. This test validates file age comparison functionality by checking whether files are newer or older than various time references across multiple time precision values. Initialize a temporary directory and create three test files with specific modification timestamps that establish a chronological order from oldest to newest, along with an invalid file reference that does not exist on the filesystem. Set up various time representations including dates, instants, zoned date-times, offset date-times, local date-times, local dates, and local times that correspond to specific moments in the file timeline. Execute file age comparison operations to determine if files are newer than other files and various time formats, asserting that older files return false when checked against newer references and newer files return true when compared against older references. Perform the inverse validation by checking if files are older than the same set of references, confirming that older files return true and newer files return false when compared appropriately. Verify that operations with non-existent files handle edge cases correctly by returning false for some comparisons and throwing exceptions for others. Test exception handling by confirming that null parameters and invalid file references trigger the appropriate null pointer and unchecked IO exceptions. The validation spans multiple time precision inputs through parameterization. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This parameterized test validates the bulk reading behavior of a queue input stream when data is not immediately available and the stream must wait for incoming data. Initialize two countdown latches to coordinate timing between threads, then create a custom linked blocking queue that overrides the poll method to signal when polling begins and wait for data to be written before proceeding. Build a queue input stream with the custom blocking queue and set a one-hour timeout, then obtain its corresponding queue output stream. Launch an asynchronous task that waits for the polling signal, writes the parameterized input data as UTF-8 bytes to the output stream, and signals completion. From the main thread, perform a bulk read operation on the input stream using a byte array sized to match the input data length, which will trigger the waiting behavior when no data is immediately available. Assert that the number of bytes read equals the input data length, verify that the reconstructed string from the read bytes matches the original input data, and confirm that the asynchronous writing task completes without throwing exceptions. This test uses JUnit 5 with parameterized testing via MethodSource annotation.

This test validates the bulk reading functionality of QueueInputStream when data is not immediately available and the stream must wait for data to be written asynchronously. The test uses parameterized input data and verifies that the QueueInputStream can properly handle waiting scenarios by reading the exact amount of data written to its associated QueueOutputStream. Begin by using the assumeFalse method to skip execution if the input data string is empty, then create two CountDownLatch instances named onPollLatch and afterWriteLatch, both initialized with a count of one to coordinate thread synchronization. Create a custom LinkedBlockingQueue of Integer type that overrides the poll method to count down the onPollLatch and then wait for the afterWriteLatch before proceeding with the original poll operation, simulating a delay in data availability. Initialize a QueueInputStream using the builder pattern, setting the custom blocking queue as the backing queue and configuring a timeout of one hour using Duration.ofHours, then wrap this in a try-with-resources block for automatic cleanup. Within the try block, call the newQueueOutputStream method on the QueueInputStream to obtain a connected QueueOutputStream instance. Create a CompletableFuture that runs asynchronously and waits for the onPollLatch to count down, then writes the input data bytes to the QueueOutputStream using the write method with UTF_8 encoding, and finally counts down the afterWriteLatch to signal completion. Create a byte array with length matching the input data length, then call the read method on the QueueInputStream with the byte array, offset zero, and the array length as parameters to perform the bulk read operation. Assert that the number of bytes read equals the input data length using assertEquals, then convert the read bytes back to a string using UTF_8 encoding and assert that the output string matches the original input data using assertEquals. Finally, assert that the CompletableFuture completes without throwing any exceptions using assertDoesNotThrow with the future.get method call. This test uses JUnit 5 framework with parameterized testing via ParameterizedTest and MethodSource annotations.

This test validates that CSV parsing correctly handles null column names in headers when configured to allow missing column names. Initialize a CSV format with default settings, enable header parsing, configure null string handling to treat the literal string "null" as null values, and allow missing column names in the header line. Create a CSV input containing a header row with three columns where the middle column is the literal string "null" followed by two data rows with corresponding values. Parse this CSV input using the configured format, then iterate through the parsed records to access the first record. This test validates the file utility methods for comparing file modification times against various temporal reference points using parameterized millisecond values. Initialize a temporary directory and create three test files with specific modification times calculated from the parameterized millisecond input, where an old file receives the base millisecond value, a reference file gets double that value, and a new file receives quadruple the value, with special handling for macOS Java 8 compatibility by adding an extra second. Generate empty test data for each file using buffered output streams and set their last modified times using the calculated file time values. Create various temporal objects from a test timestamp including Date, Instant, ZonedDateTime, OffsetDateTime, LocalDateTime, LocalDate, and time-related objects like midnight LocalTime and UTC OffsetTime, plus a LocalDate one day in the future. Exercise the file utility's newer comparison method by asserting that the old file returns false when compared against the reference file and all temporal objects except when using LocalDate with midnight time combinations, and verify the new file returns true for most comparisons except when compared against future dates. Validate exception handling by asserting that null pointer exceptions are thrown for null file or temporal parameters, and unchecked IO exceptions occur when comparing against non-existent files. This test validates the tee writer functionality that duplicates character output to multiple destination writers simultaneously. Initialize three string builder writers where two serve as output destinations and one acts as an expected reference for comparison. Create a tee writer configured with the two destination writers and a null value, using a try-with-resources block for automatic cleanup. Write individual integer values from 0 to 19 to both the tee writer and expected writer, then assert that both destination writers contain identical content matching the expected output. Populate a character array with values from 20 to 29 and write the entire array to both writers, followed by assertions verifying content equality. Append individual character values from 0 to 19 using the append method, then verify content consistency across all writers. Create a new character array with values from 20 to 29, convert it to a string, and append it to both writers, followed by content verification. After shutting down the executor, assert that the future indicates it was successfully cancelled and that no tasks remained in the executor's queue. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the JEXL script parser correctly identifies and rejects variable redeclaration within the same scope. Initialize a string containing a JEXL script that declares a variable within a try-with-resources block and then attempts to redeclare the same variable within the same block scope. Call the JEXL engine's script creation method with this source string and a parameter name, expecting it to throw a parsing exception. Assert that a JexlException.Parsing exception is thrown, then verify that the exception message contains text indicating that the variable is already declared. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates the string concatenation functionality of a JEXL expression evaluator. Initialize a map-based JEXL context and populate it with two string variables, setting one to "Hello" and another to "World". Create and evaluate a JEXL expression that concatenates the first variable, a space character, and the second variable using the plus operator. Assert that the evaluated result equals the expected concatenated string "Hello World" by comparing the actual output from the expression evaluation against the expected value. The test uses JUnit as the testing framework.

This test validates the execution of a JEXL for-each loop script that iterates over a collection and accumulates values into a variable, ensuring both the script's return value and the modified context variable reflect the correct computation. The test creates a JexlScript using the JEXL engine's createScript method with a for-each loop syntax that iterates through a list variable, adding each element to an accumulator variable named x, then executes this script within a MapContext containing specific input values and verifies the accumulated result through assertions. Initialize a MapContext instance and populate it by calling the set method twice: first to assign a list variable to an Object array containing the integer values 2 and 3, and second to assign an x variable to the Integer value 1 as the initial accumulator. Create a JexlScript by calling the createScript method on the JEXL engine with a string containing the for-each loop syntax that declares a loop variable named in to iterate over the list, with a block that adds each in value to the x variable. Execute the script by calling the execute method on the JexlScript instance, passing the configured MapContext as the execution context, which programmatically processes the for-each iteration by adding each list element to the accumulator variable and returns the final computed value. Assert that the returned Object equals Integer value 6 using assertEquals with the message "Result is wrong" to validate the script's return value represents the correct sum of 1 plus 2 plus 3. Assert that the context's x variable retrieved via the get method also equals Integer value 6 using assertEquals with the message "x is wrong" to confirm the accumulator variable was properly modified during script execution. The testing framework used is JUnit, identified by the Test annotation.

Initialize a JEXL expression engine with safety and strict mode disabled, then execute a helper method that creates and runs a nested lambda script containing conditional logic that checks if a variable's value is not NaN and less than or equal to zero, returning different string literals based on the condition. The helper method constructs a JEXL script source containing nested lambda expressions where the inner lambda accesses a variable from a map context, performs a null comparison against NaN, and returns either 'foo' or 'bar' based on the conditional evaluation. Create a map context containing a variable assignment framework with a null value, compile the script using the engine, execute it to obtain a nested script result, then execute the returned script with the prepared context to get the final result. Assert that the final execution result is not null to verify the nested lambda script executed successfully and produced a valid output. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the cancellation behavior of a JEXL script execution engine when running an infinite loop within a callable context. Initialize a semaphore with zero permits and create a test context, then bind the semaphore to the context using a variable name. Create a JEXL script that releases the semaphore and then calls a method that runs indefinitely, and convert this script into a callable object using the context. Set up a single-threaded executor service and submit the callable for execution, capturing the returned future. Assert that attempting to retrieve the result with a timeout of 100 milliseconds throws a TimeoutException, confirming the script is indeed running indefinitely. Cancel the future with interruption enabled, then shut down the executor service immediately and capture any remaining tasks. Finally, assert that the future reports as cancelled and verify that no tasks remained in the executor's queue when it was shut down. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the type coercion behavior of a JEXL expression evaluator when performing comparison operations between string and numeric literals. Initialize a map-based JEXL context to serve as the variable environment for expression evaluation. Execute a series of comparison expressions that mix string and numeric operands, including greater than, greater than or equal, less than, and less than or equal operations with representative values like string '2' compared to integer 1, and integer 2 compared to string '1'. For each expression evaluation, create a JEXL expression object from the string representation, evaluate it against the context, and assert that the actual boolean result matches the expected outcome, verifying that the expression evaluator correctly converts between string and numeric types during comparison operations. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that do-while loop constructs properly execute their expressions during iteration and return correct final values. Initialize a script engine and create a script containing a do-while loop that increments a variable from an initial value until it reaches a threshold, then establish a context with the starting variable value and execute the script to verify both the returned result and the final variable state match the expected threshold. Create another script with a variable declaration inside the loop body and execute it to confirm the loop processes correctly with internal variable modifications. Finally, construct a script that combines a do-while loop with an explicit return statement to validate that the loop executes completely before the return value is processed, ensuring the variable reaches its expected final state while the script returns the specified value. The testing is performed using JUnit framework.

This test validates that an expression evaluation engine correctly performs type coercion when comparing string and numeric values using comparison operators. Initialize a context for variable management, then systematically evaluate expressions that compare string representations of numbers with actual numeric values using greater than, greater than or equal, less than, and less than or equal operators. Assert that each comparison returns the expected boolean result, verifying that the engine properly converts string values to numbers before performing the comparison operations. The validation covers both directions of comparison where strings are compared to numbers and numbers are compared to strings, ensuring bidirectional type coercion works correctly across all comparison operators. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the execution behavior of do-while loop constructs within JEXL script expressions. Initialize a JEXL script containing a do-while loop that increments a variable from 1 until it reaches 10, then create a map-based context and set an initial variable value of 1. Execute the script with the context and assert that both the returned result and the context variable equal 10. Create a second script with a local variable declaration and a do-while loop that increments until reaching 23, execute it, and verify the result equals 23. Reset the context variable to 1, then create a third script that performs a do-while increment loop followed by an explicit return statement with value 42. Execute this final script and assert that the context variable reaches 23 while the script's return value equals 42, demonstrating that do-while loops properly modify variables and that explicit return statements override loop results. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that do-while loop constructs with false conditions execute correctly and return appropriate values. Create a script engine and construct a script containing a do-while loop with an empty body and a false condition, then execute it with an empty context and verify that the result is null since no value is produced. Next, create another script that contains the same do-while loop structure followed by a numeric literal, execute it with the same context, and assert that the returned value matches the literal value, confirming that execution continues after the loop and returns the subsequent expression result. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that JEXL expression evaluation correctly performs type coercion when comparing string and numeric values using comparison operators, ensuring that string representations of numbers are automatically converted to their numeric equivalents for accurate comparison results.
