This validation ensures the string formatting logic handles the subnet calculations and data presentation without runtime errors. The testing is performed using JUnit framework.

This test validates the FTP timestamp parsing functionality when dealing with future dates and the slop factor tolerance mechanism that prevents incorrect year rollback for timestamps slightly ahead of the current time. Initialize a Calendar instance and set its seconds and milliseconds to zero, then create two additional timestamps by cloning the calendar and adding one hour to create a near-future time and adding an additional day to create a far-future time beyond the slop tolerance. Create a new FTPTimestampParserImpl instance and enable lenient future dates by calling setLenientFutureDates with true to activate the slop factor mechanism. Obtain the recent date format string from the parser using getRecentDateFormatString and create a SimpleDateFormat instance with this pattern. Format the one-hour-ahead timestamp using the SimpleDateFormat format method, then parse this formatted string back using the parser's parseTimestamp method which internally handles the slop factor logic by adding a day to the current time before comparison. Assert that the parsed calendar's year equals the original calendar's year using assertEquals with a delta of zero, validating that the timestamp within the slop range is correctly interpreted as belonging to the current year rather than being rolled back. Format the one-day-plus-one-hour-ahead timestamp and parse it similarly with parseTimestamp, then assert that the parsed calendar's year is exactly one year behind the original calendar's year using assertEquals with an expected difference of one, confirming that timestamps beyond the slop factor are correctly interpreted as referring to the previous year. Wrap the parsing operations in a try-catch block to handle ParseException and call fail with the message "Unable to parse" if any parsing errors occur. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

This test validates the string joining utility's behavior when provided with null or empty delimiters across various array configurations. Initialize several predefined string arrays including a standard array list, empty array, null array, and mixed content array, along with expected output strings for concatenation without separators. Execute the string utility's join method with a null object array and null delimiter, asserting that it returns null. Call the join method with the standard array and null delimiter, then with an empty string delimiter, verifying both produce the expected concatenated text without separators. Test joining null and empty arrays with null delimiters, asserting both return empty strings. Verify that joining an empty array with an empty string delimiter also returns an empty string. Finally, test the join method with a mixed array using an empty delimiter and specific start and end indices, confirming it returns an empty string when the range excludes the final element. This test uses JUnit framework for assertions.

This test validates that file modification time retrieval works consistently across multiple requests with different endpoint checking configurations. Configure the endpoint checking setting based on the provided parameter, then establish a secure FTP connection using predefined authentication credentials. Retrieve the modification time information for a specific text file twice in succession, ensuring that both requests return valid file metadata objects and that the string representations of these objects are identical, demonstrating consistent behavior regardless of how many times the same file's modification time is queried. Finally, properly disconnect from the server to clean up the connection. This test uses JUnit 5 with parameterized testing to validate the behavior across multiple endpoint checking configurations.

This test validates the creation and configuration of NTP version 4 packets and verifies that reference ID strings are correctly formatted based on stratum levels and reference source types. The test exercises the NtpV3Impl class implementation of the NtpV3Packet interface, specifically testing the setVersion, setStratum, setReferenceId, and getReferenceIdString methods to ensure proper reference ID string representation for different NTP server configurations. Initialize a new NtpV3Impl object and assign it to an NtpV3Packet reference to create the test message. Call setVersion on the message with the constant VERSION_4 from NtpV3Packet to configure it as an NTP version 4 packet. Call setStratum with the value 3 to set the stratum level to 3, indicating a secondary time server. Call setReferenceId with the hexadecimal value 0x81531472 to set a numeric reference identifier. Assert that getReferenceIdString returns the string "81531472" to verify that stratum 3 servers display reference IDs as hexadecimal strings. Call setVersion again with VERSION_4 to maintain version 4 configuration. Call setStratum with the value 1 to change the stratum to 1, indicating a primary time server. Call setReferenceId with the hexadecimal value 0x55534E4F which corresponds to the ASCII encoding of "USNO". Assert that getReferenceIdString returns the string "USNO" to verify that stratum 1 servers interpret reference IDs as ASCII strings when they represent valid text. Call setReferenceId with the hexadecimal value 0x47505300 which corresponds to the ASCII encoding of "GPS" with a null terminator. Assert that getReferenceIdString returns the string "GPS" to verify that another common stratum 1 reference source identifier is correctly interpreted as an ASCII string. This test uses the standard JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that the message threading functionality correctly handles an empty collection of messages by returning null. Initialize a threading component and create an empty array of threadable message objects, then convert this empty array into a list representation. Call the threading method with this empty list of messages to process the threading algorithm. Assert that the result is null, confirming that the threading operation properly recognizes when no messages are provided and returns an appropriate null response rather than attempting to process an empty dataset. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the FTPS client's ability to retrieve file modification time information consistently across multiple requests with varying endpoint checking configurations. Initialize a parameterized test that accepts a boolean value indicating whether endpoint checking should be enabled, then configure the client's endpoint checking setting accordingly and enable trace logging for the test execution. Establish a connection to an FTPS server using a client login method, then perform two consecutive modification time queries on the same file path, using "/file.txt" as the target file. Assert that both modification time file objects returned are not null, and verify that their string representations are identical to ensure consistent behavior across repeated requests. Finally, disconnect the client to clean up the connection resources. This test uses JUnit 5 with parameterized testing, method source data providers, and timeout constraints.

This test validates that the FingerClient class properly handles disconnected state scenarios by ensuring NullPointerException is thrown when query operations are attempted without an established network connection. Initialize a new FingerClient instance without connecting it to any finger server, leaving it in a disconnected state where internal network resources remain uninitialized. Execute four separate assertion calls using assertThrows to verify that NullPointerException is consistently thrown when attempting to invoke query operations on the disconnected client: first call the query method with a false boolean parameter for short output format, then call query with a true boolean parameter for long output format, followed by calling the two-parameter query method with false and an empty string user parameter, and finally call the two-parameter query method with true and an empty string user parameter. Each assertThrows call validates that the FingerClient's query methods, which internally attempt to access network streams and connection resources that are null when disconnected, properly fail with NullPointerException rather than allowing invalid operations to proceed or throwing different exception types. The query methods being tested are designed to perform finger protocol queries against connected hosts, where the boolean parameter controls output verbosity and the string parameter specifies the target user, but when called on a disconnected client they should immediately fail due to missing network connection state. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

This test validates the string matcher factory method for creating a trim matcher and its character matching behavior against a character buffer. Initialize a trim matcher by calling the factory method on the string matcher class, then assert that subsequent calls to the same factory method return the same singleton instance using reference equality. Using a predefined character buffer, systematically test the matcher's behavior by calling the match method at various positions within the buffer, specifically testing positions 2 through 10, and assert that the method returns 0 for non-matching positions and 1 for positions containing whitespace characters that would be trimmed by standard string trimming operations. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that binary file uploads work correctly through the file transfer protocol across multiple test files. Initialize a client connection with a timeout configuration and establish communication with a server running on a designated port. For each of the first six files in a predefined collection, perform an upload operation by creating a temporary destination file in the server directory, opening an input stream from the source file, and transferring the file content using binary mode to the localhost server. After each transfer, pause briefly to allow the server to complete its file operations, then verify that the destination file was successfully created and that its content exactly matches the original source file. Clean up the temporary destination file after each validation. The test uses server configuration including port settings, directory paths, file prefixes, and a collection of test files, along with a counter to track remaining tests for proper resource cleanup. After all tests complete, teardown closes the server connection and removes any remaining test files. This test uses JUnit framework.

This test validates the behavior of string array joining functionality when using null or empty delimiters to concatenate array elements without separators. The test exercises the StringUtils join method with various array configurations and null or empty string delimiters, using equality and null assertions to verify correct concatenation behavior. Initialize the test by accessing several test class fields of type String array including ARRAY_LIST, NULL_ARRAY_LIST, EMPTY_ARRAY_LIST, and MIXED_ARRAY_LIST which are private static final fields of the test class, along with the String field TEXT_LIST_NOSEP that represents the expected concatenated result without separators. Call the StringUtils join method first with a null Object array cast and null delimiter, then assert that the result is null using assertNull. Next, call StringUtils join with the ARRAY_LIST field and null delimiter, then assert that the result equals TEXT_LIST_NOSEP using assertEquals to verify that array elements are properly concatenated without any separator when the delimiter is null. Call StringUtils join again with ARRAY_LIST and an empty string delimiter, then assert the result equals TEXT_LIST_NOSEP to confirm that empty string delimiters produce the same concatenation behavior as null delimiters. Call StringUtils join with NULL_ARRAY_LIST and null delimiter, then assert the result is an empty string to verify that arrays containing only null elements produce empty concatenated strings. Call StringUtils join with EMPTY_ARRAY_LIST and null delimiter, then assert the result is an empty string to validate that empty arrays produce empty concatenated results. Call StringUtils join with EMPTY_ARRAY_LIST and empty string delimiter, then assert the result is an empty string to confirm consistent behavior with empty arrays regardless of delimiter type. Finally, call StringUtils join with MIXED_ARRAY_LIST, empty string delimiter, start index 0, and end index of MIXED_ARRAY_LIST length minus 1, then assert the result is an empty string to verify that partial array joining with empty delimiters works correctly when excluding the last element. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

This test validates TFTP binary file upload functionality by exercising a client-server file transfer scenario across multiple test files. Initialize a TFTP client with a timeout configuration and establish a connection to a local TFTP server running on a designated port. For each of the first six files in a predefined file array, perform a binary mode upload operation by creating a temporary output file in the server directory, opening a file input stream from the source test file, and invoking the client's send file method to transfer the data to the localhost server. After each transfer, pause briefly to allow the server to complete file buffer operations and close the output stream. Assert that the uploaded file exists in the server directory and verify that the content of the uploaded file matches exactly with the original source file using a content comparison utility. Clean up each temporary uploaded file after verification. Upon completion of all test iterations, perform teardown by closing the TFTP server instance and deleting all test files from the file system. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the FTP server's ability to consistently retrieve file modification time metadata through the MDTM command, specifically testing whether repeated calls to the mdtmFile method return identical file information objects. Initialize the test by configuring the endpoint checking capability using the setEndpointCheckingEnabled method with the provided boolean parameter value, then invoke trace logging to mark the beginning of test execution with the message ">>testMdtmFile". Execute a helper method that establishes an FTPS client connection through the loginClient method, then performs the core test behavior by calling the mdtmFile method twice on the FTPSClient instance using the pathname "/file.txt" to retrieve FTPFile objects representing the file's modification time metadata. Assert that both returned FTPFile objects are not null using assertNotNull, then validate that the string representations of both FTPFile objects are identical using assertEquals to ensure consistent metadata retrieval across multiple calls. Complete the test execution by disconnecting the FTPS client in a finally block to ensure proper resource cleanup, then invoke trace logging to mark the end of test execution with the message "<<testMdtmFile". The test utilizes the USER_PROPS_RES and SERVER_JKS_RES String fields from the test class for configuration resources. This test employs JUnit 5 testing framework with ParameterizedTest, MethodSource, and Timeout annotations for parameterized execution and timeout control.

This test validates that a socket client can establish connections through a SOCKS proxy server. Initialize a SOCKS proxy object using a proxy host and port configuration, then configure the socket client to use this proxy for network connections. Establish a connection to a destination host and port through the configured proxy, and assert that the connection is successfully established by verifying the client's connected state. Finally, disconnect the socket client to clean up the connection. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that date truncation and rounding operations work correctly during daylight saving time transitions, specifically addressing a known issue with timezone handling. Initialize the test environment by setting the default timezone to Mountain Time and creating a date formatter configured for that timezone, then construct a series of timestamps representing October 31st, 2004 at various times during the DST transition period, including midnight, 1 AM, and progressively more precise times with added minutes, seconds, and milliseconds. Verify that the formatter correctly displays each timestamp with the expected timezone offset, then demonstrate the underlying timezone problem by showing how setting calendar minutes to the same value unexpectedly shifts the time by one hour due to DST handling. Test the truncation functionality by calling the truncate method with each calendar field level from milliseconds down to date, asserting that each operation removes the appropriate precision while preserving higher-order time components. Similarly, test the rounding functionality across the same calendar field levels, verifying that values round down appropriately when below the midpoint threshold. The test uses predefined date formatters, calendar representations, and timezone configurations, with cleanup ensuring timezone settings are reset after execution. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates the user experience of establishing a network connection through a SOCKS proxy server, specifically testing the SocketClient class's ability to configure and utilize proxy settings for socket-based connections. Initialize a Proxy object with type SOCKS using an InetSocketAddress constructed from the test class fields PROXY_HOST (a String) and PROXY_PORT (an integer), then call the setProxy method on the SocketClient instance sc (a field of the test class) to configure the proxy settings. Execute the connect method on the SocketClient with the destination parameters DEST_HOST (a String field) and DEST_PORT (an integer field) to establish a connection through the configured SOCKS proxy. Assert that the isConnected method returns true to validate that the connection was successfully established through the proxy. Finally, call the disconnect method to terminate the connection and clean up the socket resources. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the binary file upload functionality of a TFTP client by iterating through multiple test files and ensuring successful transmission in binary mode. The test method testTFTPBinaryUploads uses a helper method testUpload to systematically upload the first six files from the FILES array, which is a static final File array field of the test class, using TFTP.BINARY_MODE as the transfer mode. Initialize a TFTPClient instance within a try-with-resources block, call open to establish the connection, and set the socket timeout to 2000 milliseconds using setSoTimeout. Create a target File object in the SERVER_DIR directory with a name constructed from the FILE_PREFIX field concatenated with "upload", then delete any existing file at that location and assert using assertFalse that the file does not exist to ensure a clean test environment. Open a FileInputStream for the source file and call sendFile with the target filename, binary mode, input stream, localhost as the server address, and SERVER_PORT as the destination port to perform the actual file transfer. Introduce a 100-millisecond delay using Thread.sleep to allow the server sufficient time to complete file buffer operations and finalize the transfer. Assert using assertTrue that the uploaded file exists at the target location, then verify file integrity by asserting with assertTrue that the contentEquals method returns true when comparing the original source file with the uploaded target file, providing an error message that includes the specific file being tested. Clean up by deleting the uploaded file after each iteration. The teardown method decrements the testsLeftToRun static field and conditionally closes the tftpS TFTPServer instance and deletes all files in the FILES array when no tests remain. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that a socket client can successfully establish connections through a SOCKS proxy server. Initialize a SOCKS proxy configuration using predefined proxy host and port values, then configure the socket client to use this proxy for its connections. Establish a connection to a destination host and port through the configured proxy, and verify that the connection is successfully established by checking the connection status. Finally, disconnect from the destination to clean up the connection. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that network time protocol timing calculations handle the edge case where the originate timestamp is zero, which prevents accurate delay and offset computations. Initialize a new network time protocol packet and create timing information with that packet using a zero return time value. Trigger the computation of timing details to process the packet data and calculate network delay and offset values. Verify that both the network delay and clock offset are null since they cannot be computed without a valid originate timestamp. Confirm that the return time remains zero as expected. Assert that exactly one comment is generated during processing and verify that this comment contains text indicating the zero originate time error condition that prevents delay and offset calculations. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the subnet utility's ability to correctly identify whether a specific IP address falls within a subnet range when inclusive host counting is enabled. Initialize a subnet utility instance with a CIDR notation representing a single host address like "192.168.0.15/32", then configure the utility to include network and broadcast addresses in its host count calculations by setting the inclusive host count flag to true. Retrieve the subnet information object from the utility, which contains the calculated network parameters and range validation methods. Finally, assert that the subnet information correctly identifies that the original IP address "192.168.0.15" is within the valid range of the subnet, which should return true since the /32 subnet represents exactly that single address and inclusive counting is enabled. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the date truncation and rounding utilities' behavior during daylight saving time transitions in the Mountain Time zone. Initialize the default time zone to America/Denver and create a date formatter with timezone-aware formatting that includes milliseconds and timezone offset. Construct a series of date objects representing October 31, 2004 at various times during the DST transition, starting with midnight, then 1:00 AM, 1:02 AM, 1:02:03 AM, and 1:02:03.004 AM, using millisecond timestamps to ensure precision. Verify the formatter correctly displays each date with the expected Mountain Time offset using equality assertions. Create a calendar instance to demonstrate the known DST issue where setting minutes to the same value causes an hour shift, asserting that the time increases by one hour unexpectedly. Execute the date utilities' truncate method with the most precise date object across different calendar field levels including millisecond, second, minute, hour of day, hour, and date, asserting that each truncation returns the expected date object with precision removed at the specified level. Similarly, invoke the round method with the same date and calendar field parameters, verifying that rounding down produces identical results to truncation for this particular date sequence. After each test execution, reset the default timezone and date formatter timezone to their original values for cleanup. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that binary file downloads work correctly through the file transfer protocol by iterating through a collection of test files and downloading each one in binary mode. Initialize a client connection with a timeout configuration and establish communication with a server running on the local host at a designated port. For each test file, create a temporary output file in the server directory with a download prefix, ensuring any existing file at that location is first removed. Execute the file transfer by requesting the original file by name from the server and writing the received content to the output location using binary transfer mode. Verify that the downloaded file was successfully created and that its content exactly matches the original source file byte-for-byte. Clean up by removing the downloaded file after each transfer validation. The test uses server configuration including port settings, directory paths, file collections, and connection management, with cleanup occurring after all test iterations complete by closing the server connection and removing test files. This test uses JUnit framework.

This test validates the TFTP binary file download functionality by verifying that multiple files can be successfully downloaded from a TFTP server using binary transfer mode. The test iterates through the first six files from the FILES array (a static final File array field of the test class) and calls the helper method testDownload with TFTP.BINARY_MODE and each file to verify proper binary mode file transfers and content integrity validation. The helper method creates a new TFTPClient instance, opens it, sets a socket timeout of 2000 milliseconds, creates an output file in the SERVER_DIR (a static final File field of the test class) with a name prefixed by FILE_PREFIX (a static final String field of the test class) followed by "download", deletes any existing output file, and asserts that the output file does not exist to ensure a clean state. The helper method then opens a FileOutputStream for the output file and calls receiveFile on the TFTPClient with the original file name, the specified transfer mode, the output stream, "localhost" as the server address, and SERVER_PORT (a static final int field of the test class) as the port number. After the file transfer, the helper method asserts that the output file exists to confirm successful creation, asserts that the downloaded file content equals the original file content using the contentEquals method to validate transfer integrity, and deletes the downloaded output file for cleanup. In the teardown method, the testsLeftToRun static field is decremented, and when it reaches zero or below, the tftpS TFTPServer field is closed if not null, and all files in the FILES array are deleted to clean up test resources. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that file uploads work correctly when using ASCII text mode for file transfer operations. Initialize a file transfer client with appropriate timeout settings and establish a connection to a local server running on a designated port. For each of the first six test files in a predefined collection, perform an upload operation by reading the source file content and transmitting it to the server using ASCII mode, specifying a target filename with an upload prefix in the server directory. After each transfer, allow a brief pause for the server to complete file processing and buffer operations, then verify that the uploaded file was successfully created on the server and that its content exactly matches the original source file. Clean up the uploaded file after each validation to prepare for the next iteration. The test uses server configuration including a port number, server directory path, filename prefix, and a collection of test files, and performs cleanup by closing the server connection and deleting test files when all tests complete. This test uses JUnit framework.

This test validates the date truncation and rounding functionality during daylight saving time transitions, specifically testing the DateUtils truncate and round methods to ensure they handle timezone changes correctly without introducing hour shifts. Initialize the default timezone to America/Denver Mountain Time using TimeZone.setDefault, then create a SimpleDateFormat with pattern "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS XXX" and configure it to use the Denver timezone. Construct five Date objects representing specific moments on October 31, 2004 during the DST transition: create the base date using timestamp 1099206000000L for 01:00:00.000, subtract 3600000 milliseconds to get 00:00:00.000, then add 120000, 3000, and 4 milliseconds respectively to create dates at 01:02:00.000, 01:02:03.000, and 01:02:03.004. Verify the date formatting by asserting each formatted date string equals the expected timezone-adjusted values "2004-10-31 00:00:00.000 -06:00" through "2004-10-31 01:02:03.004 -06:00" with descriptive assertion messages. Demonstrate the timezone problem by creating a Calendar instance, setting its time to the 01:00:00.000 date, calling set with Calendar.MINUTE using the same minute value, and asserting the resulting time equals the original time plus 3600000 milliseconds to show the hour shift issue. Test the DateUtils truncate method by calling it with the most precise date and each Calendar field constant (MILLISECOND, SECOND, MINUTE, HOUR_OF_DAY, HOUR, DATE), asserting each result equals the corresponding expected truncated date with descriptive messages like "Truncate Calendar.MILLISECOND". Similarly test the DateUtils round method using the same date and Calendar field constants, asserting each rounded result matches the expected values with messages like "Round Calendar.MILLISECOND". The test class contains TimeZone fields TIME_ZONE_DEFAULT and TIME_ZONE_MET, Date fields for various test dates, Calendar fields for corresponding calendar instances, and DateFormat fields dateParser and dateTimeParser that are configured in the setUp method. After each test execution, call afterEachResetTimeZones to restore the default timezone and reset the dateTimeParser timezone. This test uses the JUnit testing framework with @Test annotation.

This test validates ASCII mode file uploads through a TFTP client-server communication system. Initialize a TFTP client with a socket timeout of 2000 milliseconds and iterate through the first six files from a predefined file array. For each file, create a temporary upload destination file in the server directory with an "upload" prefix, ensuring any existing file at that location is deleted first. Open a file input stream for the source file and invoke the client's send file method using ASCII transfer mode, targeting localhost on the configured server port. After transmission, pause execution briefly to allow the server to complete file buffer operations and verify that the destination file was created successfully. Assert that the uploaded file exists and that its content matches the original source file exactly, then clean up by deleting the temporary file. After all tests complete, perform teardown by closing the TFTP server instance and deleting all test files from the file array. This test uses JUnit framework.

This test validates subnet calculation functionality for edge cases involving very large address counts that exceed integer limits. Initialize a subnet utility with a zero-prefix CIDR notation representing the entire IPv4 address space, enable inclusive host counting to include network and broadcast addresses, and retrieve the subnet information. Verify that the network mask is correctly calculated as all zeros and that the long address count returns the full 32-bit address space size. Confirm that attempting to get the address count as an integer throws a runtime exception due to the value exceeding integer maximum limits. Create another subnet utility with a single-bit prefix CIDR notation, enable inclusive host counting, retrieve the subnet information, and verify the network mask and long address count for half the address space. Again confirm that getting the integer address count throws a runtime exception. Finally, disable inclusive host counting for the same subnet to exclude network and broadcast addresses, retrieve the updated subnet information, and verify that the address count now fits within integer limits and returns successfully without throwing an exception. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the NTP packet implementation's ability to handle version 4 protocol configuration and reference identifier string conversion. Initialize an NTP version 3 packet implementation, then configure it to use NTP version 4 protocol and set the stratum level to 3 with a hexadecimal reference identifier value like 0x81531472. Assert that the reference identifier string returns the expected hexadecimal representation "81531472". Reconfigure the packet by setting the version to 4 again, updating the stratum to 1, and setting the reference identifier to a value representing "USNO" (0x55534E4F). Verify that the reference identifier string correctly converts to the ASCII string "USNO". Finally, update the reference identifier to represent "GPS" (0x47505300) and assert that the string conversion produces "GPS". This test uses the standard JUnit testing framework.

This test validates TFTP binary file download functionality by iterating through a collection of test files and verifying successful retrieval from a TFTP server. Initialize a TFTP client with a socket timeout of 2000 milliseconds, then for each of the first six files in the test file array, perform a binary mode download operation by creating an output file in the server directory with a download prefix, ensuring any existing output file is deleted first and asserting its absence. Execute the file receive operation using the client to download the specified file from localhost on the configured server port in binary transfer mode, writing the received data to the output file stream. Assert that the output file was successfully created after the download completes, then verify that the downloaded file content is identical to the original source file using a content comparison method. Clean up by deleting the downloaded output file after each successful verification. After all tests complete, perform teardown by closing the TFTP server instance if it exists and deleting all test files from the file collection. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the ASCII mode file upload functionality of a TFTP client by iterating through multiple test files and verifying successful transmission to a TFTP server. The test exercises the TFTPClient's sendFile method in ASCII mode against various file sizes and confirms that uploaded files maintain content integrity through byte-by-byte comparison assertions. Initialize a loop that iterates from index 0 to 5, accessing the first six elements from the FILES array which is a static final File array field of the test class containing predefined test files. For each iteration, call the helper method testUpload with parameters TFTP.ASCII_MODE and the current file from the FILES array. Within the helper method, create a new TFTPClient instance using a try-with-resources block, then call open to establish the connection and setSoTimeout with a value of 2000 milliseconds to configure the timeout. Create a File object representing the upload destination by combining the SERVER_DIR static final File field and a filename constructed from the FILE_PREFIX static final String field concatenated with "upload". Call delete on the destination file to clean up any previous test artifacts, then assert with assertFalse that the file does not exist to ensure a clean starting state. Open a FileInputStream for the source file within another try-with-resources block, then call sendFile on the TFTPClient with the destination filename, the ASCII mode parameter, the input stream, "localhost" as the server address, and SERVER_PORT which is a static final int field of the test class. After the file transfer, call Thread.sleep with 100 milliseconds to allow the server time to complete file operations and buffer flushing. Assert with assertTrue that the destination file now exists to confirm the upload succeeded, then assert with assertTrue that contentEquals returns true when comparing the original source file with the uploaded destination file to verify content integrity. Finally, call delete on the destination file to clean up the test artifact. In the tearDown method, decrement the testsLeftToRun static int field of the test class, and if the value reaches zero or below, close the tftpS TFTPServer static field if it is not null, then iterate through all files in the FILES array and call delete on each to remove test artifacts. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the behavior of subnet address counting functionality when dealing with very large subnet ranges that exceed integer limits, specifically testing the NET-521 issue related to address count overflow handling. Initialize a SubnetUtils instance with the CIDR notation "0.0.0.0/0" representing the entire IPv4 address space, then call setInclusiveHostCount with true to include network and broadcast addresses in the count, and retrieve the SubnetInfo object using getInfo. Assert that getNetmask returns "0.0.0.0" as the netmask for this all-encompassing subnet, then assert that getAddressCountLong returns the long value 4294967296L representing the total IPv4 address space, and verify that calling getAddressCount throws a RuntimeException since this count exceeds Integer.MAX_VALUE. Create a second SubnetUtils instance with "128.0.0.0/1" representing half the IPv4 address space, set inclusive host count to true, and obtain its SubnetInfo object. Assert that getNetmask returns "128.0.0.0" for this subnet, verify getAddressCountLong returns 2147483648L for this half-space range, and confirm getAddressCount throws RuntimeException due to integer overflow. Finally, call setInclusiveHostCount with false to exclude network and broadcast addresses from the count, retrieve the updated SubnetInfo, and assert that getAddressCount now returns the integer value 2147483646 since excluding the two boundary addresses brings the count within integer range. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

This test validates the ability to parse member listing entries from an MVS FTP server response. Initialize a parser for MVS FTP entries and configure it to handle member list type responses by setting the appropriate type and regex pattern for member listings. Iterate through a collection of sample member list entries that represent valid formatting scenarios, and for each entry, invoke the parsing functionality to convert the raw listing text into a structured file representation. Assert that each parsing operation successfully produces a non-null result, indicating the entry was properly interpreted, and perform additional validation to ensure the parsed file contains the expected raw listing content and extracted name information. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the subnet utility's handling of large address counts and inclusive host counting behavior for edge-case CIDR notations. Initialize a subnet utility with the CIDR notation "0.0.0.0/0" representing the entire IPv4 address space, enable inclusive host counting to include network and broadcast addresses, and retrieve the subnet information object. Assert that the network mask equals "0.0.0.0" and the long address count equals 4294967296, then verify that calling the integer address count method throws a RuntimeException due to the count exceeding integer limits. Create another subnet utility with "128.0.0.0/1" representing half the IPv4 space, enable inclusive host counting, and obtain its subnet information. Assert the network mask equals "128.0.0.0" and the long address count equals 2147483648, again confirming that the integer address count method throws a RuntimeException. Finally, disable inclusive host counting for the same subnet to exclude network and broadcast addresses, retrieve the updated subnet information, and assert that the integer address count now returns 2147483646 without throwing an exception since the reduced count fits within integer bounds. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

Initialize an MVS FTP entry parser and configure it for member list parsing by setting its type to the member list constant and its regex pattern to the member list regex pattern. Iterate through a collection of good sample member list entries, parsing each entry string using the parser's parse FTP entry method to generate an FTP file object. For each parsed entry, assert that the resulting FTP file object is not null with a failure message indicating which test string failed to parse, then invoke additional validation by calling a helper method that verifies the parsed file's raw listing and name properties are not null. This test validates the parser's ability to correctly process member list entries from MVS FTP servers and extract basic file metadata. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that authentication fails when attempting to login with an invalid username that does not exist in the system. Initialize a fresh email client connection by resetting any existing state and establishing a new connection to the mail server, then verify the connection is properly established and in the correct authorization state. Attempt to authenticate using a non-existent username paired with a valid password, and assert that the login operation returns false, confirming that the system properly rejects authentication attempts with invalid user credentials. The test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the parsing functionality for MVS FTP member list entries to ensure proper extraction of file metadata from mainframe directory listings. The test creates an MVSFTPEntryParser instance, configures it with MEMBER_LIST_TYPE using the setType method, and sets the parsing pattern with MEMBER_LIST_REGEX using the setRegex method to prepare it for processing member list format entries from MVS FTP servers. The test then iterates through a collection of valid member list sample strings stored in the goodsamplesMemberList field of the test class, which contains String type test data representing properly formatted member list entries.
