Create a substitution processor using this mapping, then attempt to replace variables in a simple text string that contains no variable markers or placeholders. Assert that the original text remains completely unchanged after processing, confirming that the substitution mechanism does not modify strings when no variables are present to replace. Additionally, verify that the substitution operation reports no changes were made to the text during processing. Clean up the variable mapping after testing completes. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the recursive variable substitution functionality of a string templating system, specifically testing how nested placeholder variables are resolved through multiple levels of indirection and how default values are handled when variables are undefined. Initialize a HashMap field of the test class containing string key-value pairs, starting with basic mappings for "animal" set to "quick brown fox" and "target" set to "lazy dog" during setup. Modify the values map to create a complex nested substitution hierarchy by setting "animal" to a placeholder referencing "critter", "target" to reference "pet", "pet" to reference "petCharacteristic" followed by "dog", "petCharacteristic" to "lazy", and "critter" to a template combining three separate placeholders for "critterSpeed", "critterColor", and "critterType" with values "quick", "brown", and "fox" respectively. Call the helper method doTestReplace with the expected result "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.", the template string "The ${animal} jumps over the ${target}.", and true for substring testing, which creates a StrSubstitutor instance with the values map and performs comprehensive validation by testing the replace method across multiple input types including String, character array, StringBuffer, StringBuilder, StrBuilder, and MutableObject, asserting that each produces the expected fully-resolved result and verifying that substring operations on ranges excluding the first and last characters also work correctly, while also testing the replaceIn methods that modify the input objects in-place and return boolean success indicators. Update the "pet" value to include a default value syntax with "petCharacteristicUnknown:-lazy" and repeat the same helper method call to verify that undefined variables with default values are properly handled during recursive substitution. Clean up by setting the values field to null during teardown. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the string substitution functionality when no variable placeholders are present in the input text. Initialize a hash map containing string key-value pairs with entries for "animal" mapped to "quick brown fox" and "target" mapped to "lazy dog". Create a string substitutor instance using this map as the variable source. Call the replace method on the substitutor with the input string "The balloon arrived." which contains no variable placeholders. Assert that the returned result equals the original input string unchanged, demonstrating that text without variables passes through unmodified. Additionally, create a string builder with the same input text, invoke the replace-in-place method on it, assert that the method returns false indicating no replacements were made, and verify the string builder's content remains identical to the original input. Clean up by nullifying the values map. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the idle duration calculation behavior of a pooled object wrapper in its initial state immediately after creation. Initialize a default pooled object instance wrapping a generic object, then introduce a thread sleep of 200 milliseconds to ensure sufficient time has passed for duration calculations. Retrieve the idle duration from the pooled object and assert that it is not negative, confirming that the time calculation logic handles the initial state correctly without producing invalid negative durations. Assert that the idle duration is not zero, verifying that some measurable time has elapsed since object creation. Finally, assert that the idle duration is less than or equal to the active duration by comparing their values, which validates the expected relationship between these two duration metrics in the pooled object's initial state where all timestamp instants default to the creation time. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the behavior of a generic keyed object pool when an exception occurs during object destruction while returning an object that fails validation. Initialize a simple factory and a generic keyed object pool using the factory, then configure the factory to throw exceptions on destroy operations and enable validation, while setting the pool to test objects on return. Borrow two string objects using the key "one" from the pool, then configure the factory to mark objects as invalid to simulate validation failure. Return the first borrowed object to the pool, which should trigger validation failure and subsequent destruction that throws an exception. Assert that the pool maintains one active object and zero idle objects for the specific key "one", and verify the same counts for the overall pool state, confirming that the object remains active despite the failed return operation due to the destruction exception. After test completion, clear and close the pool, nullify references, query the JMX management server for any remaining registered pool instances, unregister any found pools, and assert that no pools remain registered. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework with timeout annotation.

This test validates the functionality of call stack creation and manipulation through the CallStackUtils utility class by testing two different configurations of call stack instances and verifying their behavior through stack trace operations. The test exercises the newCallStack method from CallStackUtils with varying boolean parameters and uses assertion logic to confirm that call stacks can properly capture, print, and clear stack trace information. Initialize the test by accessing the MESSAGE_FORMAT field, which is a private static final String field of the test class that serves as a formatting parameter for call stack creation. Execute the newCallStack method from CallStackUtils twice, first with the MESSAGE_FORMAT string and two boolean parameters set to false and false, then again with MESSAGE_FORMAT and boolean parameters set to false and true. For each call stack instance returned, invoke the assertNewCallStack helper method which performs a comprehensive validation sequence: call fillInStackTrace on the call stack to capture the current execution context, create a StringWriter and PrintWriter to capture output, invoke printStackTrace on the call stack to write the stack trace to the writer, assert that the resulting string output is not empty using assertFalse to verify the stack trace was properly captured, call clear on the call stack to reset its state, reset the StringWriter buffer length to zero, invoke printStackTrace again on the cleared call stack, and assert that the output string is now empty using assertTrue to confirm the call stack was properly cleared. This testing approach validates that CallStackUtils can create functional call stack instances regardless of the specific boolean configuration parameters and that the resulting call stacks maintain proper lifecycle behavior for capturing and clearing stack trace information. The test uses the standard JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

This test validates the behavior of an eroding pool utility that automatically discards idle objects over time based on a configurable erosion factor. Begin by asserting that the utility properly rejects null pool arguments and non-positive erosion factors by throwing appropriate exceptions. Create a mock pool using a proxy with an invocation handler that tracks method calls and returns a constant value for active and idle object counts. Initialize an eroding pool wrapper with a very small erosion factor to trigger rapid object discarding behavior. Verify that basic pool operations like adding objects, borrowing objects, and returning objects function correctly and invoke the expected underlying methods in the proper sequence. Check that the pool reports correct counts for active and idle objects. Perform multiple borrow-and-return cycles with short delays between them to simulate normal usage patterns, confirming that no erosion occurs during active use. After a significant delay that exceeds the erosion threshold, perform another borrow-and-return operation and verify that the pool automatically invalidates idle objects as part of the erosion process. Finally, clear and close the pool, ensuring all expected cleanup methods are called in the correct order. This test uses JUnit for assertions and exception validation.

This test validates the object pool's behavior when an exception occurs during object destruction while returning an object that fails validation, ensuring the pool maintains correct active and idle object counts despite the destruction failure. The test examines the GenericKeyedObjectPool class and its returnObject method, using assertions to verify that active and idle object counts remain accurate when both validation and destruction operations encounter errors. Initialize a SimpleFactory with exception throwing enabled on destroy and validation enabled, then configure the GenericKeyedObjectPool with test-on-return enabled by calling setThrowExceptionOnDestroy with true, setValidationEnabled with true, and setTestOnReturn with true respectively. Borrow two objects from the pool using the key "one" by calling borrowObject twice, storing the first returned object reference. Set the factory's validation to fail by calling setValid with false, then return the first borrowed object to the pool using returnObject with the key "one" and the stored object reference, which will trigger both validation failure and destruction exception. Assert that the number of active objects for key "one" equals 1 using getNumActive, assert that the number of idle objects for key "one" equals 0 using getNumIdle, assert that the total number of active objects across all keys equals 1 using getNumActive with no parameters, and assert that the total number of idle objects across all keys equals 0 using getNumIdle with no parameters, validating that the pool correctly maintains object counts when destruction fails during return processing. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework with Test and Timeout annotations specifying a 60-second timeout limit.

This test validates the behavior of a connection pool when configured with a null object factory and unlimited wait time. Initialize a thread pool executor with a fixed number of threads matching the pool size, then create a connection pool using a null object factory and a wait duration set to forever. Launch multiple concurrent threads equal to the pool size, where each thread attempts to borrow a connection fixture from the pool using the same key. After starting all threads, verify that the executor shuts down properly within the specified wait duration, considering the behavior of the null object factory. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates that string substitution operations correctly handle input text containing no variable placeholders by ensuring the original text remains unchanged. The test specifically examines the StrSubstitutor class and its replace method behavior, asserting that strings without substitution variables are returned unmodified. Initialize a HashMap field of the test class with key-value pairs where "animal" maps to "quick brown fox" and "target" maps to "lazy dog" during setup. Create a new StrSubstitutor instance using the populated values map as the variable source. Call the helper method doTestNoReplace with the string literal "The balloon arrived." which contains no variable placeholders. Within the helper method, since the template string is not null, invoke the replace method on the StrSubstitutor instance with the provided template string and assert that the returned result equals the original input string "The balloon arrived." using assertEquals. Create a new StrBuilder instance initialized with the template string, then call the replaceIn method on the StrSubstitutor with this StrBuilder instance and assert that it returns false using assertFalse, indicating no replacements were made. Finally, assert that the StrBuilder's string representation using toString still equals the original template string using assertEquals. During teardown, set the values field to null to clean up resources. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates that object pool borrowing handles activation exceptions correctly by continuing to attempt borrowing until a valid object is obtained or all options are exhausted. Initialize a factory and generic object pool, then borrow two objects and return them both to establish idle objects in the pool. Configure the factory to throw exceptions during activation and set validation to fail intermittently, then attempt to borrow an object which should succeed despite the activation exception because the pool continues trying until it finds a valid object. Verify that one object becomes active and no objects remain idle, then return the borrowed object. Next, configure the factory so that validation always fails during activation, then attempt to borrow an object which should throw an exception indicating no elements are available since all activation attempts fail. Confirm that no objects are active or idle after the failed borrowing attempt. The test includes cleanup that clears the pool, closes resources, unregisters management beans, and ensures eviction timers are properly shut down. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the method chaining behavior of a string tokenizer component by creating a new tokenizer instance and verifying that each configuration method returns the same tokenizer object reference for fluent API usage. Initialize a string tokenizer object, then sequentially call the reset method with no arguments, reset with an empty string, reset with an empty character array, set delimiter character to space, set delimiter string to a single space, set delimiter matcher to null, set quote character to space, set quote matcher to null, set ignored character to space, set ignored matcher to null, set trimmer matcher to null, set empty token as null to false, and set ignore empty tokens to false. After each method call, assert that the returned object is the exact same reference as the original tokenizer instance using equality assertions, confirming that all methods properly support method chaining by returning the tokenizer itself rather than a new instance. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the concurrent object creation and return behavior in a GenericObjectPool to ensure no object instances are leaked when multiple threads simultaneously borrow and return objects with validation enabled. The test specifically examines the pool's ability to maintain accurate object counts during concurrent operations with validation latency, asserting that the make counter equals the sum of idle objects plus borrowed objects. Initialize a SimpleFactory and GenericObjectPool in the setup, then configure the pool by calling setTestOnBorrow with true to enable validation on borrow and call setValid on the factory with true to ensure objects pass validation. Create and start a WaitingTestThread instance with the pool and a 200 millisecond pause duration, then sleep the main thread for 50 milliseconds to allow the background thread to begin its borrow operation. Call setValidateLatency on the factory with 400 milliseconds to introduce validation delay, then call borrowObject on the pool to obtain a string instance in the main thread. Assert that the factory's getMakeCounter equals the sum of the pool's getNumIdle plus one to verify no objects are leaked during concurrent operations. Call returnObject on the pool with the borrowed instance to return it, then assert that the factory's getMakeCounter equals the pool's getNumIdle to confirm all created objects are properly accounted for after the return operation. In teardown, retrieve the JMX name from the pool, clear and close the pool, set both pool and factory references to null, query the MBean server for any remaining registered pools, unregister any found pools while building a detailed message, assert that the registered pool count equals zero, yield the current thread, sleep for 1000 milliseconds if the EvictionTimer executor exists, and assert that the EvictionTimer executor is null. The testing frameworks used are JUnit 5 with the Test and Timeout annotations.

This test validates the eroding pool utility functionality by testing null parameter validation, negative factor rejection, and time-based object erosion behavior. Initialize a method call logger invocation handler that tracks all method calls and returns integer value 1 for numeric methods, then create a dynamic proxy object pool using this handler. Assert that illegal argument exceptions are thrown when passing null pools to the eroding pool utility methods and when providing negative erosion factors like -1. Create an eroding pool with a small erosion factor of 0.01 and verify that initial method calls like adding objects, borrowing objects, and returning objects are properly delegated to the underlying pool by comparing expected method call lists with actual logged calls. Retrieve active and idle object counts to confirm the handler returns 1 for both values. Perform multiple borrow and return cycles with 50 millisecond delays, clearing the method call tracking between iterations to verify normal operation. Sleep for 10 seconds to allow the erosion mechanism to activate, then borrow and return an object again to trigger the erosion behavior, which should result in additional method calls including getting idle count and invalidating objects. Finally, clear and close the pool within a try-with-resources block to ensure proper cleanup, and assert that all expected method calls including clear and close were logged in the correct sequence. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates that clearing a pool key unblocks threads waiting to borrow objects from that key's sub-pool during concurrent operations. Initialize a keyed object pool with configuration settings that limit each key to one object total and one object maximum, with a wait timeout of 500 milliseconds, and provide a custom factory that includes a small delay during object destruction. Create two concurrent threads using an executor service, where the first thread repeatedly borrows and returns objects using a specific key in a loop, and the second thread repeatedly clears that same key in a parallel loop, both executing the same number of iterations with brief pauses between operations. Submit both threads to the executor and wait for their completion, ensuring that the clearing operations properly interrupt any waiting borrow attempts without causing deadlocks or indefinite blocking. The test uses JUnit 5 with a timeout annotation.

This test validates that clearing a keyed object pool properly unblocks threads waiting to borrow objects during concurrent operations. Initialize a generic keyed object pool configuration with maximum total per key set to 1, maximum total set to 1, and maximum wait duration set to 500 milliseconds. Create a generic keyed object pool using a custom keyed pooled object factory that implements makeObject to return a default pooled object wrapping the integer 10, destroyObject to sleep for 10 milliseconds, and validateObject to return true, while leaving activateObject and passivateObject as no-ops. Set up two threads using an executor service with a fixed thread pool of size 2, where the first thread performs 100 iterations of borrowing an object with key 10, returning it, and sleeping for 10 milliseconds, and the second thread performs 100 iterations of clearing the pool for key 10 and sleeping for 10 milliseconds. Submit both threads to the executor and wait for their completion using future get methods to ensure both operations complete without throwing exceptions. The test framework used is JUnit with timeout annotation set to 10 seconds.

This test validates the eroding pool functionality which automatically discards idle objects over time to prevent resource accumulation, testing both the pool wrapper creation with proper validation and the time-based object erosion behavior through method call tracking and assertions. Initialize two IllegalArgumentException assertions using assertThrows to verify that PoolUtils erodingPool method rejects null ObjectPool parameters in both single-parameter and two-parameter variants with appropriate error messages. Create an ArrayList of String objects to track method calls and instantiate a MethodCallLogger InvocationHandler that overrides the invoke method to log all method calls while ensuring getNumActive and getNumIdle methods return the integer value 1 instead of zero. Assert that PoolUtils erodingPool throws IllegalArgumentException when provided with a negative float factor using the createProxy helper method which uses Proxy newProxyInstance to create a dynamic proxy of the ObjectPool class with the logging handler. Set the erosion factor to 0.01f and create an ArrayList for expected method calls, then instantiate an eroding pool using PoolUtils erodingPool with the proxied ObjectPool and the factor within a try-with-resources block. Assert that the called methods list equals the expected methods list initially, then call addObject on the pool and add "addObject" to the expected methods list. Call borrowObject to retrieve an object, add "borrowObject" to expected methods, and assert equality between the lists. Call returnObject with the borrowed object, add "returnObject" to expected methods, and assert list equality again. Call getNumActive and assert it returns 1, then add "getNumActive" to expected methods, followed by calling getNumIdle, asserting it returns 1, and adding "getNumIdle" to expected methods. Execute a loop five times where each iteration calls borrowObject, adds "borrowObject" to expected methods, sleeps for 50 milliseconds using Thread sleep, calls returnObject, adds "returnObject" to expected methods, asserts list equality, then clears both method lists. Sleep for 10000 milliseconds to allow the erosion timer to trigger, then call borrowObject again, add "borrowObject" to expected methods, call returnObject which should trigger erosion behavior by adding "getNumIdle" and "invalidateObject" to expected methods, and finally call clear on the pool. After the try-with-resources block closes, add "clear" and "close" to expected methods and assert final equality between expected and called method lists. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the object pool's behavior when activation exceptions occur during borrowing operations, specifically testing that the pool correctly handles activation failures and continues attempting to provide valid objects while maintaining accurate active and idle object counts. Initialize a SimpleFactory instance and create a GenericObjectPool using this factory, then borrow two string objects from the pool and return both objects to make them available in the idle pool. Configure the factory to throw exceptions on activation by calling setThrowExceptionOnActivate with true and set setEvenValid to false, which causes activation to throw every other time while allowing the borrowing loop to continue and eventually succeed on the second attempt. Call borrowObject to retrieve an object despite the activation exception, then assert that getNumActive equals 1 and getNumIdle equals 0 to verify the pool correctly tracks one active object and no idle objects. Return the borrowed object to the pool using returnObject, then configure the factory to fail validation by calling setValid with false, which causes validation to fail both on activation of idle instances and when creating new instances. Use assertThrows to verify that borrowObject throws a NoSuchElementException when both activation and creation fail, then assert that both getNumActive and getNumIdle equal 0 to confirm the pool maintains accurate counts when no objects can be successfully provided. In teardown, retrieve the JMX name from the pool, clear and close the pool, set both pool and factory references to null, query the MBean server for any remaining registered pools, build a detailed message about any lingering pools while unregistering them, assert that the registered pool count equals 0, yield the current thread, sleep for 1000 milliseconds if the EvictionTimer executor exists, and assert that the EvictionTimer executor is null. This test uses the JUnit testing framework with Test and Timeout annotations specifying a 60-second limit.

This test validates that clearing a keyed object pool properly unblocks threads waiting to borrow objects by testing concurrent operations between borrowing/returning and clearing pool objects. Initialize a GenericKeyedObjectPoolConfig with setMaxTotalPerKey set to 1, setMaxTotal set to 1, and setMaxWait set to a Duration of 500 milliseconds to create a highly constrained pool configuration. Create a GenericKeyedObjectPool using an anonymous KeyedPooledObjectFactory implementation where makeObject returns a DefaultPooledObject wrapping the integer 10, destroyObject includes a Thread.sleep call of 10 milliseconds to simulate destruction time, activateObject and passivateObject perform no operations, and validateObject always returns true. Set the borrow key as the integer 10 and iterations count to 100. Create an ExecutorService with a fixed thread pool of 2 threads. Define the first thread to repeatedly borrow objects using borrowObject with the borrow key, return them using returnObject, and sleep for 10 milliseconds in each iteration, catching any exceptions and calling fail if they occur. Define the second thread to repeatedly call clear with the borrow key and sleep for 10 milliseconds in each iteration, also catching exceptions and calling fail. Submit both threads to the executor using submit to get Future objects, then call get on both futures to wait for completion and ensure no exceptions are thrown. The test verifies that the clear operation properly interrupts and unblocks any threads waiting to borrow objects from the pool, preventing deadlocks in concurrent scenarios where pool clearing occurs while threads are waiting for available objects. This test uses the JUnit framework with Test and Timeout annotations set to 10000 milliseconds.

This test validates the string substitution functionality when handling empty placeholder keys and default value syntax. Initialize a hash map containing key-value pairs for animal names like "quick brown fox" and target references like "lazy dog". Create a string substitutor instance using this value map and test its replacement behavior across multiple string types including String, character arrays, StringBuffer, StringBuilder, and custom string builder objects. Execute replacement operations on templates containing empty placeholder braces and default value syntax with colons, using input strings like "The ${} jumps over the lazy dog." and "The ${:-animal} jumps over the ${target}.". Verify that empty placeholders remain unchanged while valid placeholders with default syntax are properly substituted, expecting results such as "The ${} jumps over the lazy dog." for empty keys and "The animal jumps over the lazy dog." for default value replacements. Test both full string replacement and substring replacement operations, asserting that the substitutor correctly processes each string type and returns the expected transformed content. Confirm that in-place replacement methods return true to indicate successful modifications. Clean up by nullifying the value map after test completion. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that the eviction mechanism can successfully create idle objects while concurrent borrowing operations are in progress. Initialize a factory with a creation latency of 300 milliseconds and configure both the factory and pool to have a maximum total of 2 objects, then set the pool's minimum idle count to 1. Borrow one object from the pool to establish an active object state, then create a test thread that will attempt to borrow an object after a 150 millisecond delay. Configure the pool's eviction timer to run after 100 milliseconds, which will trigger the creation of an idle object to satisfy the minimum idle requirement. Start the borrower thread and wait for it to complete, then verify that the borrowing operation succeeded without any failures. The test uses random number generation, pool configuration, thread management, timing controls, completion tracking, and error state monitoring. Cleanup involves clearing the pool, closing resources, unregistering management beans, and ensuring the eviction timer executor is properly shut down. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the interaction between object pool eviction and concurrent borrowing operations when the pool is configured with minimum idle objects. Initialize a simple factory with a make latency of 300 milliseconds and set both the factory and generic object pool maximum total to 2 objects, then configure the pool with a minimum idle count of 1. Borrow one object from the pool to establish an active object state, leaving the pool with 1 active and 0 idle objects. Create a test thread configured to perform 1 borrow operation with a 150 millisecond delay, then start this thread in parallel. Configure the pool's eviction timer to run after 100 milliseconds, which will trigger the creation of idle instances to meet the minimum idle requirement. Wait for the borrower thread to complete execution, then assert that the borrower thread did not fail during its operation. The test uses a timeout annotation with a 60-second limit and employs JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that string substitution functionality correctly handles empty placeholder keys and default value syntax within template strings. Initialize a mapping of replacement values containing animal and target entries, then execute substitution operations on templates that include empty placeholder braces and default value syntax with colons. The test exercises two specific scenarios: one with completely empty placeholder braces that should remain unchanged, and another using default value syntax where the placeholder should fall back to a predefined value when the key is not found. For each scenario, perform string replacement operations across multiple data types including strings, character arrays, string buffers, string builders, and custom string building utilities, validating both full string replacement and substring replacement within specified boundaries. Assert that the substitution correctly preserves empty placeholders as literal text while properly resolving default values, and verify that in-place replacement operations return true to indicate successful modifications. Clean up the mapping after test completion. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the interaction between object eviction and concurrent borrowing operations in a GenericObjectPool to ensure that eviction processes can successfully add idle objects while borrowing operations are in progress. The test configures a SimpleFactory with a make latency of 300 milliseconds and sets both the factory and GenericObjectPool maximum total to 2, while setting the pool's minimum idle to 1, then borrows one object to establish an initial state of one active and zero idle objects. Initialize a TestThread with the generic object pool, configured to run once with a 150 millisecond fixed delay before attempting to borrow, and create a Thread instance from this TestThread. Configure the generic object pool to run eviction with a duration between eviction runs of 100 milliseconds, which will trigger the evictor to create an idle instance. Start the borrower thread to initiate the concurrent borrowing operation, then call join on the borrower thread to wait for its completion. Assert that the borrower thread did not fail by calling the failed method on the TestThread and verifying it returns false, which validates that the eviction process successfully added objects without interfering with the concurrent borrowing operation. The test uses JUnit 5 testing framework with a timeout annotation set to 60000 milliseconds.

This test validates that an object pool correctly enforces its maximum capacity limit under concurrent load conditions. Initialize a simple factory and generic object pool with a maximum total of ten objects, configure the pool to block when exhausted, and disable eviction runs. Create nearly two hundred worker threads that will repeatedly borrow and return objects from the pool with delays, then start all threads and allow them to begin their work. In the main thread, perform twenty iterations of borrowing objects with delays, checking after each borrow that the number of active objects never exceeds the configured maximum total, and throwing an exception if this constraint is violated. Return each borrowed object in a finally block to ensure proper cleanup. After completing the main thread iterations, wait for all worker threads to complete and verify that none of them encountered failures during their object borrowing and returning operations. The test ensures that under heavy concurrent access, the pool maintains its capacity constraints and prevents over-allocation of objects. Cleanup involves clearing and closing the pool, unregistering management beans, and verifying that eviction timers are properly shut down. This test uses JUnit 5 framework with timeout annotations.

This test validates the lifecycle management of eviction timer scheduling and cancellation functionality within a pooling system. Initialize a generic object pool with a basic factory that creates null objects and wraps them in default pooled object containers. Create the first evictor component and schedule it with the eviction timer using a one-minute duration for both delay and period parameters. Use reflection to access the private scheduled future field of the evictor and verify that the timer task is not cancelled, then access the private executor field of the eviction timer class to confirm that the thread pool executor queue contains exactly two items representing the reaper plus one eviction task, and assert that the eviction timer reports one active task. Create a second evictor component and schedule it similarly, then verify through reflection that its scheduled future is also not cancelled, confirm the executor queue now contains three items, and assert the eviction timer reports two active tasks. Cancel the first evictor using the eviction timer's cancel method with default shutdown timeout and no interrupt flag, then verify through reflection that its scheduled future is now cancelled, confirm the executor queue size has decreased to two items, and assert the eviction timer reports one remaining task. Cancel the second evictor in the same manner, verify its scheduled future is cancelled through reflection, confirm the executor field is now null indicating the thread pool has been freed, and assert the eviction timer reports zero active tasks. The testing framework used is JUnit.

This test validates that an object pool correctly evicts idle objects using a first-in-first-out ordering strategy. Initialize a factory and object pool during setup, then configure the pool with a short idle duration threshold, minimum idle count, idle object testing enabled, and FIFO ordering disabled. Add multiple objects to the pool and trigger eviction to establish baseline behavior. Configure the factory to mark objects as invalid and throw exceptions during activation, then trigger eviction again to test error handling paths. Add more objects and configure the factory to throw exceptions during passivation, followed by another eviction cycle. Reset the factory to mark objects as valid again, wait for the idle duration to expire, and perform a final eviction. Assert that the pool maintains exactly the minimum number of idle objects after all eviction cycles complete. During teardown, clear and close the pool, verify no management beans remain registered, and confirm the eviction timer executor is properly shut down. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates that a generic object pool maintains proper active object limits under concurrent load conditions. Initialize a simple factory and generic object pool during setup, then configure the pool with a maximum total of 10 objects, enable blocking when exhausted, and disable eviction runs. Create 199 test threads that will each perform 40 iterations of borrowing and returning objects with random delays, then start all threads and allow them to begin concurrent operations. In the main thread, perform 20 iterations of borrowing objects with 25 millisecond delays, asserting after each borrow that the number of active objects never exceeds the configured maximum total limit, throwing an illegal state exception if this constraint is violated. Return each borrowed object in a finally block to ensure proper cleanup, and wait for all worker threads to complete their operations. Assert that no threads failed during execution, indicating successful concurrent access without violating pool constraints. During teardown, clear and close the object pool, unregister any remaining MBean registrations, and verify that the eviction timer executor is properly shut down. This test uses JUnit 5 with timeout and warning suppression annotations.

This test validates the FIFO eviction behavior of a generic object pool by configuring eviction parameters and exercising various failure scenarios. Initialize a simple factory and generic object pool during setup, then configure the pool with a soft minimum evictable idle duration of 10 milliseconds, minimum idle count of 2, test-while-idle enabled, and LIFO disabled to enforce FIFO ordering. Add 5 objects to the pool and trigger an initial eviction to establish baseline behavior. Configure the factory to mark both even and odd numbered objects as invalid and enable activation exceptions, then perform another eviction to test validation failure handling. Add 5 more objects to the pool, disable activation exceptions but enable passivation exceptions, and evict again to test passivation error scenarios. This test validates the string substitution functionality when handling empty variable keys and default value syntax in template strings, specifically testing the StrSubstitutor class's ability to process malformed or empty placeholder expressions and apply default values correctly. The helper method creates a StrSubstitutor instance with the values map, then systematically tests the replace method across multiple input types including String, char array, StringBuffer, StringBuilder, StrBuilder, and MutableObject, asserting that each produces the expected result, and when the substring parameter is true, also tests substring replacement by calling replace with start index 1 and end index length minus 2, expecting a shortened version of the result. Additionally, the helper method tests in-place replacement using replaceIn methods on StringBuffer, StringBuilder, and StrBuilder objects, asserting that the method returns true and the modified objects contain the expected result string. This test validates that an object pool maintains proper active object limits under concurrent load conditions, specifically ensuring that the number of active objects never exceeds the configured maximum total even when multiple threads are simultaneously borrowing and returning objects. Initialize a SimpleFactory instance and a GenericObjectPool with the factory, then configure the factory and pool with a maximum total of 10 objects, enable blocking when exhausted, and disable eviction runs by setting the duration between eviction runs to negative one millisecond. Create an array of 199 TestThread instances, each configured to perform 40 iterations with a 50 millisecond delay, and start each thread to begin concurrent borrowing operations. Allow the threads to initialize by sleeping for 5000 milliseconds, then execute 20 iterations in the main thread where each iteration sleeps for 25 milliseconds, calls borrowObject on the pool, immediately checks if getNumActive exceeds getMaxTotal and throws an IllegalStateException if true, sleeps again for 25 milliseconds, and returns the borrowed object via returnObject in a finally block while catching and failing on any exceptions during borrowing. After completing the main thread iterations, wait for all worker threads to complete by polling their complete method every 500 milliseconds, and fail the test if any thread reports failure via the failed method. During teardown, retrieve the JMX name from the pool, clear and close the pool, nullify the pool and factory references, query the platform MBean server for any remaining registered pools under the org.apache.commoms.pool3 domain, unregister any found MBeans while building an error message, and assert that zero pools remain registered. Additionally, yield the current thread and sleep for 1000 milliseconds if the EvictionTimer executor exists, then assert that the EvictionTimer executor is null. This test uses the JUnit 5 testing framework with Test, Timeout, and SuppressWarnings annotations.

This test validates that object pool eviction operates correctly when configured to use last-in-first-out ordering for object retrieval. Initialize a factory for creating pooled objects and establish a generic object pool with that factory, then configure the pool to maintain a minimum of two idle objects, enable validation during idle periods, set a short eviction threshold, and activate last-in-first-out behavior. Configure the factory to mark all objects as invalid and to throw exceptions during activation, then perform another eviction to test error handling during object validation. Add five more objects and reconfigure the factory to throw exceptions during passivation instead of activation, followed by another eviction to validate error handling during object return. Reset the factory to normal operation with all objects marked as valid, wait briefly to allow objects to exceed the eviction threshold, then perform a final eviction cycle and verify that exactly two objects remain idle in the pool as expected by the minimum idle configuration. After completion, clean up all pool resources, unregister management beans, and ensure eviction timers are properly shut down. This test uses JUnit framework with timeout constraints.

This test validates the behavior of a generic object pool when activation exceptions occur during object borrowing operations. Initialize a simple factory and generic object pool in the setup phase, then borrow two string objects from the pool and return them both to establish idle objects in the pool. Configure the simple factory to throw exceptions on activation and set validation to false for even-numbered objects, creating a scenario where activation will intermittently fail. Attempt to borrow an object from the pool, which should succeed on the second attempt after the first activation throws an exception, then assert that one object is active and zero objects are idle in the pool. Return the borrowed object to the pool and configure the factory to fail all validation attempts. Attempt to borrow an object again, which should throw a NoSuchElementException when both idle object activation and new object creation fail validation, then assert that both active and idle object counts are zero. During teardown, clear and close the object pool, verify no MBean registrations remain for pool monitoring, and ensure the eviction timer executor is properly shut down. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework with a 60-second timeout annotation.

This test validates the thread safety of the idle duration calculation method in a default pooled object implementation under high concurrency conditions. Initialize a default pooled object wrapping a generic object instance, create an atomic boolean flag to track if negative idle durations are encountered, and set up a thread pool executor with a size based on available processor cores multiplied by three. Define two types of concurrent tasks: an allocation task that repeatedly checks idle duration, allocates the pooled object, continues checking idle duration while allocated, then deallocates the object, and a simple idle time checking task that only monitors idle duration values. Submit ten thousand randomly selected tasks to the executor with a seventy percent probability of choosing the allocation task over the idle time checking task, then wait for all submitted futures to complete execution. Assert that the atomic boolean flag remains false, confirming that no negative idle duration values were returned during the concurrent operations, which would indicate a thread safety violation in the idle time calculation logic. This test uses the standard JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the behavior of a GenericKeyedObjectPool when the maximum active objects per key limit is exceeded under concurrent access conditions. Initialize a WaiterFactory with specific latency parameters including zero make latency, twenty waiter latency, and other timing values set to zero, along with eight maximum active objects and five maximum active per key. Create a GenericKeyedObjectPool using this WaiterFactory as the keyed pooled object factory, then configure the pool by calling setMaxTotalPerKey with a value of five to limit objects per key, setMaxTotal with eight to set the overall pool limit, setTestOnBorrow with true to enable validation on borrowing, setMaxIdlePerKey with five to control idle object limits, and setMaxWait with a Duration of negative one millisecond to indicate indefinite waiting. Execute the test behavior by calling the helper method runTestThreads with parameters twenty for the number of threads, three hundred for iterations per thread, two hundred fifty for delay between operations, and the configured waiter pool, which creates twenty TestThread instances that concurrently attempt to borrow and return Waiter objects from the pool while respecting the per-key limits, with each thread performing three hundred iterations and introducing a two hundred fifty millisecond delay between operations. The helper method monitors all threads for completion by polling their complete status every five hundred milliseconds using Waiter sleepQuietly, and if any thread reports failure through its failed method, the test fails with a detailed error message including the thread index and stack trace from the thread's exception field. The test uses the Test and Timeout annotations with a timeout of two hundred thousand milliseconds specified in TimeUnit MILLISECONDS.

This test validates the Last-In-First-Out eviction behavior of a generic object pool by exercising various eviction scenarios and exception handling paths. Initialize a simple factory and generic object pool during setup, then configure the pool with a soft minimum evictable idle duration of 10 milliseconds, minimum idle count of 2, test-while-idle enabled, and LIFO ordering activated. Add 5 objects to the pool and trigger an initial eviction to establish baseline behavior. Configure the factory to mark both even and odd numbered objects as invalid and enable exception throwing during activation, then perform another eviction to test validation failure handling. Add 5 more objects to the pool, disable activation exceptions but enable passivation exceptions, and evict again to verify exception handling during object return. Reset the factory to disable passivation exceptions and mark all objects as valid, wait 125 milliseconds to allow objects to become evictable based on the idle duration, then perform a final eviction. Assert that exactly 2 objects remain idle in the pool, confirming that the eviction process correctly maintained the minimum idle count while removing excess objects in LIFO order. During teardown, clear and close the pool, verify no MBean registrations remain, and ensure the eviction timer executor is properly shut down. This test uses JUnit 5 with a 60-second timeout annotation.

This test validates the Last-In-First-Out eviction behavior of a generic object pool, specifically testing that the eviction mechanism correctly removes idle objects while maintaining the minimum idle count and handling various factory validation states. Initialize a SimpleFactory instance and create a GenericObjectPool using this factory in the setUp method, storing both as private test class fields of types SimpleFactory and GenericObjectPool respectively. Execute the testEvictLIFO method which calls a helper method checkEvict with a true parameter to enable LIFO behavior. In the helper method, configure the pool by setting the soft minimum evictable idle duration to 10 milliseconds using setSoftMinEvictableIdleDuration, set the minimum idle count to 2 using setMinIdle, enable testing while idle using setTestWhileIdle with true, and configure LIFO ordering using setLifo with the provided boolean parameter. Add 5 objects to the pool using addObjects and trigger eviction using the evict method. Modify the factory state by setting both even and odd validation to false using setEvenValid and setOddValid, enable exception throwing on activation using setThrowExceptionOnActivate with true, then call evict again. Add another 5 objects using addObjects, disable activation exceptions using setThrowExceptionOnActivate with false, enable passivation exceptions using setThrowExceptionOnPassivate with true, and call evict once more. Reset the factory by disabling passivation exceptions using setThrowExceptionOnPassivate with false and re-enabling both even and odd validation using setEvenValid and setOddValid with true. Sleep for 125 milliseconds using Thread.sleep, call evict a final time, and assert that the number of idle objects equals 2 using assertEquals with getNumIdle. In the tearDown method, retrieve the JMX name using getJmxName, clear and close the pool using clear and close methods, nullify both pool and factory references, query the MBean server for remaining pool registrations, unregister any found MBeans, assert that no pools remain registered using assertEquals with 0 as the expected count, and verify the EvictionTimer executor is null using assertNull after yielding and potentially sleeping for 1000 milliseconds. This test uses the JUnit testing framework with Test and Timeout annotations specifying a 60-second timeout in milliseconds.

This test validates the string substitution functionality when handling incomplete variable prefix patterns in template strings. Initialize a map containing string key-value pairs representing variables like "animal" mapped to "quick brown fox" and "target" mapped to "lazy dog". Create a string substitutor instance using this variable map, then test its replacement behavior with a template containing an incomplete prefix pattern where a variable reference starts but doesn't complete properly, such as a template with "animal" variable reference followed by text ending with an incomplete "target" variable reference starting with a dollar sign. Execute the replacement operation using the template "The {animal} jumps over the lazy dog." as the expected result and "The {animal} jumps over the ${target}." as the replacement template, enabling substring testing. Verify that the substitutor correctly handles the incomplete prefix by testing replacement across multiple input types including strings, character arrays, string buffers, string builders, string builder objects, and mutable objects. Assert that each replacement operation returns the expected result string and that in-place replacement operations return true to indicate successful modification. For substring operations, assert that partial replacement within specified bounds produces the expected shortened result. Clean up by nullifying the variable map after test completion. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that idle time calculations for pooled objects remain consistent and non-negative under concurrent access conditions. Initialize a pooled object wrapper around a basic object and create an atomic boolean flag to track if any negative idle time values are encountered. Set up a thread pool with multiple worker threads and define two types of tasks: one that repeatedly allocates and deallocates the pooled object while checking idle time, and another that only checks idle time without state changes. Submit thousands of these tasks randomly to the thread pool with a higher probability of allocation tasks, then wait for all tasks to complete. Throughout execution, each task continuously queries the idle duration and sets the flag if any negative values are detected. Assert that the flag remains false, confirming that idle time calculations never return negative values even under heavy concurrent access. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a keyed object pool properly handles activation exceptions during the borrowing process while maintaining correct pool state tracking. Initialize a keyed object pool with a simple factory that can be configured to throw exceptions during activation and validation phases. Borrow two objects using the same key, then return both objects to make them available in the idle pool. Configure the factory to throw exceptions during activation on alternating attempts and disable even validation, then attempt to borrow an object which should succeed on the second activation attempt after the first fails, and verify that the pool shows one active object and zero idle objects both for the specific key and overall. Return the borrowed object to the pool, then configure the factory to fail all validation attempts and attempt to borrow another object, which should result in a no such element exception being thrown as both idle object activation and new object creation will fail validation. Assert that after the failed borrow attempt, all pool counters show zero active and idle objects for both the specific key and overall pool state. The test performs cleanup by clearing the pool, closing it, and unregistering any remaining management beans to ensure no pools remain registered. This test uses JUnit framework with timeout annotations.

This test validates the behavior of object pool activation exception handling during borrowing operations, specifically testing how the GenericKeyedObjectPool manages activation failures and continues processing to find valid objects. Initialize a SimpleFactory instance and create a GenericKeyedObjectPool using this factory in the setUp method, storing both as test class fields of types SimpleFactory and GenericKeyedObjectPool respectively. Borrow two string objects from the pool using key "one" via the borrowObject method, then return both objects to the pool using returnObject with the same key and respective object references. Configure the factory to throw exceptions during activation by calling setThrowExceptionOnActivate with true, and set the factory's even validation behavior to false using setEvenValid. Attempt to borrow another object from the pool with key "one", which should succeed despite activation exceptions because the pool continues processing until finding a valid object. Assert that the number of active objects for key "one" equals 1 using getNumActive, the number of idle objects for that key equals 0 using getNumIdle, and verify the total active and idle counts across all keys are 1 and 0 respectively. Return the borrowed object to the pool, then disable validation entirely by calling setValid with false on the factory. Attempt to borrow an object again, which should now throw a NoSuchElementException since both activation and validation will fail, and verify this using assertThrows. Finally, assert that all object counts return to zero for both the specific key and total pool metrics. In the tearDownJmx method, retrieve the JMX name from the pool, clear and close the pool, nullify the factory and pool references, query the MBean server for any remaining registered pools, unregister any found pools, and assert that no pools remain registered with a count of 0. This test uses the JUnit testing framework with Test and Timeout annotations specifying a 60-second limit.

This test validates the FIFO (First In, First Out) eviction behavior of a generic object pool, specifically testing the comprehensive eviction logic that handles various object states and factory configurations during the eviction process. Initialize a SimpleFactory instance and create a GenericObjectPool using this factory in the setUp method, then configure the pool by setting the soft minimum evictable idle duration to 10 milliseconds, minimum idle objects to 2, test while idle to true, and LIFO mode to false to enable FIFO ordering. Add 5 objects to the pool using addObjects and trigger an initial eviction with the evict method to establish baseline behavior. Configure the factory to make both even and odd numbered objects invalid by calling setEvenValid with false and setOddValid with false, then set the factory to throw exceptions on activation using setThrowExceptionOnActivate with true, and call evict again to test eviction behavior with invalid objects and activation exceptions. Add another 5 objects to the pool, disable activation exceptions by calling setThrowExceptionOnActivate with false, enable passivation exceptions using setThrowExceptionOnPassivate with true, and call evict to test eviction with passivation failures. Reset the factory by disabling passivation exceptions with setThrowExceptionOnPassivate set to false and making objects valid again by setting both setEvenValid and setOddValid to true. Sleep for 125 milliseconds to allow objects to become eligible for eviction based on the idle duration, then perform a final eviction and assert that exactly 2 objects remain idle in the pool using assertEquals with the expected value of 2 and the result of getNumIdle. In the teardown, retrieve the JMX name from the pool, clear and close the pool, set both pool and factory references to null, query the MBean server for any remaining registered pools, unregister any found pools while building a detailed message about their creation stack traces, assert that no pools remain registered using assertEquals with expected value 0, yield the current thread, sleep for 1000 milliseconds if the EvictionTimer executor exists, and assert that the EvictionTimer executor is null. The testing frameworks used are JUnit 5 with Test and Timeout annotations configured for a 60-second maximum execution time.

This test validates that the idle time calculation for pooled objects remains consistent and non-negative under high concurrency conditions, specifically testing the DefaultPooledObject class's getIdleDuration method to ensure it never returns negative duration values during concurrent allocation and deallocation operations. Initialize a DefaultPooledObject instance with a new Object, create an AtomicBoolean flag to track if negative idle time is ever returned, and establish an ExecutorService with a thread pool sized at three times the available processor count. Define an allocation and deallocation task that performs 10000 iterations of checking if getIdleDuration returns a negative value, breaking early if found, then calls allocate on the pooled object, performs another 10000 iterations of the same negative duration check, and finally calls deallocate. Create a separate idle time checking task that performs 10000 iterations of checking getIdleDuration for negative values. Set the probability of running the allocation task to 0.7 and submit 10000 randomly selected tasks to the executor service, collecting all Future objects in a list. Wait for all submitted tasks to complete by calling get on each Future. Assert that the AtomicBoolean flag remains false, ensuring that DefaultPooledObject.getIdleTimeMillis never returned a negative value throughout the concurrent execution with the message "DefaultPooledObject.getIdleTimeMillis() returned a negative value". The test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the proper handling of object return operations in a keyed object pool, particularly focusing on passivation behavior and exception handling during the return process. Initialize a failing factory that can simulate various failure conditions and create an empty pool using this factory, handling cases where pool creation is unsupported by returning early. Set up tracking for method calls and clear any existing state. Borrow an object from the pool using a test key, then clear the method tracking and return the borrowed object to verify that the pool correctly calls the passivation method on the returned object. Reset the pool state and add multiple objects to establish a pool with several idle and active objects, then borrow some objects to create the desired state. Configure the factory to fail during passivation operations and attempt to return an object, verifying that the pool handles the passivation failure gracefully by not adding the object back to the idle pool while maintaining correct active and idle counts. Finally, test the scenario where both passivation and destruction operations fail by configuring both failure modes and attempting to return an object, expecting that certain pool implementations will propagate the destruction exception while others may handle it differently. Close the pool to complete the test and perform cleanup by nullifying the pool reference. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that string tokenizer configuration methods support method chaining by returning the tokenizer instance itself. Initialize a new string tokenizer without any input content. Call the reset method without parameters and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Call the reset method with an empty string and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Call the reset method with an empty character array and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Set the delimiter character to a space character and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Set the delimiter string to a space string and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Set the delimiter matcher to null and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Set the quote character to a space character and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Set the quote matcher to null and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Set the ignored character to a space character and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Set the ignored matcher to null and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Set the trimmer matcher to null and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Configure empty tokens to not be treated as null and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. Configure the tokenizer to not ignore empty tokens and verify it returns the same tokenizer instance. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the thread safety and concurrent performance of a keyed object pool under high contention scenarios. Initialize a keyed object pool with a simple factory for creating pooled resources, then configure the pool to allow a maximum of fifteen total resources per key, maintain up to fifteen idle resources per key, and set a one-second timeout for resource acquisition requests. Execute a multi-threaded stress test by spawning twenty concurrent threads that each perform one hundred iterations of borrowing and returning resources with a fifty-millisecond delay between operations, ensuring all threads complete successfully without failures or exceptions. Monitor thread completion status and assert that no thread encounters errors during the concurrent pool operations. After testing, perform comprehensive cleanup by clearing the pool, closing all resources, nullifying references, and verifying through management bean inspection that no pool registrations remain in the system, asserting zero registered pools exist. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates the initial state timestamp behavior of a pooled object wrapper by creating a default pooled object instance that wraps a generic object and verifying that all temporal instant properties are correctly initialized to the same creation timestamp. Initialize a default pooled object implementation with a new object as the wrapped instance, which establishes the creation instant for the pooled object wrapper. Assert that the creation instant equals the last borrow instant, confirming that borrowing timestamps are initialized to the creation time. Assert that the creation instant equals the last return instant, verifying that return timestamps start at the creation time. Assert that the creation instant equals the last used instant, ensuring usage tracking begins at creation time. Assert that the creation instant equals itself as a sanity check for the getter method consistency. This test uses the JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a newly created pooled object has all of its timestamp fields initialized to the same creation instant, ensuring proper initial state management for object pool lifecycle tracking. The test creates a DefaultPooledObject instance wrapping a new Object, which represents a pooled object wrapper that tracks metadata such as creation time, borrowing history, and usage patterns within an object pool system. Initialize a DefaultPooledObject with a new Object as the wrapped instance, which automatically sets the creation instant to the current time and initializes all other timestamp fields to this same value. Call getCreateInstant to retrieve the object's creation timestamp, then assert that this creation instant equals the result of getLastBorrowInstant, verifying that the last borrow time is initially set to the creation time. Assert that the creation instant also equals the result of getLastReturnInstant, confirming that the last return time is initialized to the creation instant. Assert that the creation instant equals the result of getLastUsedInstant, ensuring that the last used time is set to the creation instant. Finally, assert that the creation instant equals itself when retrieved via getCreateInstant, providing a redundant but explicit validation of the creation timestamp consistency. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the Test annotation.

This test validates that a keyed object pool correctly handles exceptions during object destruction when validation fails on return. Initialize a pool with a factory configured to throw exceptions during destruction and enable validation, then configure the pool to test objects when they are returned. Borrow two objects using the same key, then configure the factory to make validation fail for returned objects. Return one of the borrowed objects, which should trigger validation failure and attempt destruction that throws an exception. Assert that the pool maintains one active object and zero idle objects for the specific key, and verify the same counts at the pool level, confirming that the object remains active despite the destruction exception. The test uses JUnit framework.

This test validates the correct behavior of object return operations in a keyed object pool, specifically testing that returned objects are properly passivated and that passivation failures are handled appropriately without corrupting pool state. Initialize a FailingKeyedPooledObjectFactory instance and create an empty KeyedObjectPool using the makeEmptyPool helper method, catching any UnsupportedOperationException and returning early if the test is not supported. Create an ArrayList of MethodCall objects to track expected method invocations. Test the correct behavior path by calling borrowObject on the pool with a KEY parameter to obtain an object, then use the clear helper method to reset the factory's method call list and expected methods list. Call returnObject on the pool with the KEY and borrowed object, which should trigger passivation, then add a new MethodCall with "passivateObject", KEY, and the object to the expected methods list and assert that the factory's getMethodCalls equals the expected methods using assertEquals. Test exception handling by using the reset helper method to clear the pool, reset the factory, and clear both method call lists. Call addObject three times with KEY to create three idle objects, then call borrowObject twice to obtain two objects, leaving one idle and two active. Verify the pool state by asserting that getNumIdle returns 1 and getNumActive returns 2 using assertEquals. Clear the method tracking again, then call setPassivateObjectFail with true on the factory to simulate passivation failure. Call returnObject with KEY and one of the borrowed objects, add the expected passivateObject method call, and use the removeDestroyObjectCall helper method from AbstractTestObjectPool to handle flexible timing of destroy operations. Assert that the expected methods match the factory's method calls, then verify that getNumIdle still returns 1 (object not added due to passivation failure) and getNumActive returns 1 (object no longer active) using assertEquals. Reset the pool and factory again, borrow another object, clear method tracking, and set both setPassivateObjectFail and setDestroyObjectFail to true. Attempt to call returnObject within a try-catch block, expecting either no exception for non-GenericKeyedObjectPool implementations or a PrivateException for other cases, using fail to indicate when the expected exception is not propagated. Finally, call close on the pool to clean up resources. In the tearDown method, set the pool field to null for cleanup. This test uses the JUnit testing framework as indicated by the @Test annotation.

This test validates the creation and behavior of an eroding keyed object pool utility that automatically removes idle objects after a specified time period. Begin by verifying that the utility properly rejects null pool arguments and non-positive erosion factors by attempting to create eroding pools with invalid parameters and confirming that appropriate exceptions are thrown. Set up a mock keyed object pool using a proxy with method call logging to track all pool operations, then create an eroding pool wrapper with a very small erosion factor to enable quick object removal during testing. Add an object to the pool using a string key, borrow and return the object multiple times while verifying that the expected pool methods are being called in the correct sequence and that active and idle object counts are properly maintained. Perform several rapid borrow-return cycles with short delays to establish normal pool behavior, then wait for the erosion timeout period to elapse before borrowing and returning an object again to trigger the automatic invalidation of idle objects. Verify that the pool correctly calls the invalidation method when objects have been idle beyond the erosion threshold, and finally close the pool to ensure proper cleanup occurs. Assert that all expected method calls occurred in the proper order throughout the entire test sequence, confirming both normal pool operations and the time-based erosion functionality. This test uses JUnit 5 testing framework.

This test validates that a cleared call stack produces no output when its stack trace is printed. Initialize a call stack and populate it with current execution context information, then clear all stored trace data from the stack. Direct the stack to print its trace information to a string-based output destination, capture the resulting output, and assert that the printed content is completely empty, confirming that clearing effectively removes all trace data and prevents any output during subsequent print operations. The validation spans multiple call stack implementations through parameterized inputs. This test uses JUnit 5 framework.

This test validates that a call stack component produces no output after being cleared by using parameterized test data. Initialize a string writer to capture output, then call the fill method on the provided call stack parameter to populate it with stack trace information. Clear the call stack to remove all previously captured trace data, then invoke the print stack trace method with a print writer that wraps the string writer to attempt outputting the trace. Retrieve the captured string content from the writer and assert that it equals an empty string, confirming that cleared call stacks produce no output when printed. This test uses JUnit 5 with parameterized testing via method source.

This test validates the thread-safety and concurrent behavior of a generic keyed object pool under multi-threaded access conditions. Initialize a simple factory and a generic keyed object pool during setup, then configure the pool with a maximum of 15 objects per key, a maximum of 15 idle objects per key, and a wait timeout of 1000 milliseconds. Execute a multi-threaded test scenario by spawning 20 concurrent threads, each performing 100 iterations with a 50-millisecond delay between operations on the shared object pool. Monitor all test threads for completion by polling their status every 500 milliseconds, and assert that no thread encounters failures during execution by checking each thread's completion and error status. During teardown, clear and close the object pool, retrieve the JMX management bean server, query for any remaining registered pool instances, unregister any lingering MBean objects, and assert that zero pools remain registered in the management system. This test uses the JUnit testing framework with timeout annotations.

This test validates that string substitution correctly replaces variable placeholders with their corresponding values from a lookup map. Initialize a map containing key-value pairs for variable substitution, specifically mapping an animal name to a descriptive phrase. Create a string substitutor using this map as the variable resolver. Test the replacement functionality by providing a template string containing a variable placeholder in the standard format and verifying that the substitution produces the expected result where the placeholder is replaced with the mapped value. The validation exercises multiple string representation types including standard strings, character arrays, string buffers, string builders, and custom string building utilities, ensuring consistent behavior across different input formats. Additionally, verify that in-place replacement operations return success indicators and properly modify the original string containers. The test uses a helper method to systematically validate both full string replacement and substring replacement scenarios across all supported string types, asserting that the output matches the expected substituted text in every case. Cleanup occurs by nullifying the variable map after test completion. This test uses JUnit testing framework.

This test validates that a cleared CallStack produces no output when its stack trace is printed, ensuring that the clear operation completely removes all trace information and that subsequent print operations are effectively no-ops. Initialize a StringWriter as a private final field of the test class to capture printed output, then execute the parameterized test method testPrintClearedStackTraceIsNoOp which accepts a CallStack parameter sourced from a data method. Call fillInStackTrace on the provided CallStack instance to populate it with current execution context information, immediately followed by calling clear to remove all stored stack trace data. Invoke printStackTrace on the cleared CallStack, passing a new PrintWriter constructed with the StringWriter field to capture any potential output. Retrieve the captured content by calling toString on the StringWriter and assert that it equals an empty string using assertEquals, validating that the cleared stack produces no trace output. This test uses the JUnit 5 testing framework with parameterized test support via ParameterizedTest and MethodSource annotations.

This test validates the behavior of the PoolUtils eroding pool functionality for keyed object pools by testing various error conditions and the time-based erosion mechanism. Initialize a list to track method calls and create a method invocation handler that logs all method invocations while returning integer value 1 for numeric methods to simulate non-zero pool statistics. Assert that IllegalArgumentException is thrown when attempting to create an eroding pool with null keyed object pool parameters across different method overloads, and when providing non-positive erosion factors like 0.0. Create a proxy keyed object pool using the invocation handler and initialize it with an eroding pool wrapper using a small erosion factor of 0.01. Verify that no methods have been called initially, then add an object to the pool using a string key, borrow an object from the pool, and return the object, asserting that the expected method sequence matches the actual calls after each operation. Check that the pool reports 1 active and 1 idle object as expected from the handler's behavior. Execute a loop that borrows and returns objects five times with 50-millisecond delays between operations, clearing the method tracking lists after each iteration to reset the state. This test validates the behavior of a keyed object pool's add object functionality using a failing keyed pooled object factory. This test validates the soft minimum idle eviction behavior in a GenericObjectPool where objects are evicted based on configurable idle time thresholds while respecting a minimum idle count. Sleep for an additional 2000 milliseconds to allow remaining objects to exceed the hard eviction threshold of 3 seconds, call evict again to perform hard eviction which should remove all remaining idle objects regardless of the minimum idle setting, and assert that getNumIdle equals 0 with the message "Idle count different than expected."
